2. Internal AGL/series-circuit training records (constant current regulators, isolating transformers, series-circuit safe working).

Statutory competence is governed by S010 001M and S010 002M.

ICAO Doc 9157 Aerodrome Design Manual Part 5 (Electrical Systems) - design of AGL series circuits, isolating transformers and supply arrangements 3. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Electrical Machinery Regulations 2011 reg 6(1) and reg 8(1) - ample clear working space at switchgear and transformer premises, unobstructed space front and back of switchboards 4. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Electrical Installation Regulations 2009 reg 5(1) and 5(5) - installation only in accordance with the incorporated health and safety standard (SANS 10142-1), and design above 1 kV approved by a registered professional
evidenceExpected: Approved AGL electrical design drawings/as-built records referencing Annex 14 Ch.8 and Doc 9157 Part 5, showing de-energised isolation/maintenance-access points on the series circuits.
target: Valid design data

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires each Electrical Maintenance Department to hold a Maintenance Programme aligned to the latest SACAA Technical Guidance Manual for Maintenance of Runway and Taxiway Lighting Systems and to replace all unserviceable equipment according to ICAO recommendations (D060 001M cl. 4.7 / 4.8). All airfield and apron lighting shall be designed and comply with ICAO Doc 9157 Part 5 Aerodrome Design Manual (D100MAN cl. 7.1). Design must incorporate adequate working space clearances, safe access routes and escape paths, and future construction shall not compromise statutory access or maintenance clearances (D119MAN cl. 3.3.5).
acsaThreshold: Design compliance is stated as 'ICAO Doc 9157 Part 5' and 'ICAO Annex 14 Volume 1' without an ACSA numeric value; D119MAN cl. 3.3.5 states the maintainability/accessibility requirement but no numeric clearance dimension. UPS switchover times adopted from ICAO Annex 14 Vol I Ch. 8 Table 8.1 are the one design number ACSA states verbatim (D118MAN cl. 4.3.6)
acsaEvidence: Maintenance Programme aligned to SACAA TGM for Maintenance of Runway and Taxiway Lighting Systems
As-built drawings and circuit diagrams (D060 001M cl. 4.13)
ECSA Stage 3 design report and General Arrangement drawings (D118MAN cl. 7/8)
acsaConflict: ACSA sets no numeric working-clearance dimension for electrical apparatus anywhere in the set (D119MAN cl. 3.3.5 expressly states the requirement without a figure), so 'safe working space for maintenance personnel' cannot be tested against an ACSA number.
basisNote: The detailed series-circuit design and maintenance practice sits in the IEC 61820/61821/61822/61823 series, which are technical standards reflected in Doc 9157 Part 5 rather than South African law.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

requirement: Ensure a COC is issued by a competent, qualified and registered person
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Electrical Installation Regulations 2009 reg 9(1) and 9(2) - only a registered person may issue a certificate of compliance, and only after inspection and test 2. Electrical Installation Regulations 2009 reg 7(1) and 7(5) - every user or lessor must hold a valid CoC; a change of ownership may not be allowed on a CoC older than two years 3. Electrical Installation Regulations 2009 reg 2(1) - the user or lessor is responsible for the safety, safe use and maintenance of the installation 4. SANS 10142-1:2024 (Ed. 3.2), the wiring of premises Part 1: low-voltage installations - the incorporated standard the installation is certified against
evidenceExpected: Original, signed CoC for the AGL electrical installation (not a photocopy/reprint), plus any supplementary CoC covering later alterations.
target: Valid COC with
walkabout: Walk the installation and check for any visible alterations or extensions since the CoC date that are not covered by a supplementary CoC.

acsaRequirement: Only a Registered Person may issue a COC, and only after inspecting and testing the installation; the Registered Person SHALL REFUSE to issue where any fault or defect is detected. Authorisation is tiered: single-phase LV by an electrical tester, installation electrician or master installation electrician; two-phase, three-phase and DC by an installation electrician or master installation electrician only; specialised installations (petroleum, medical, explosives) by a master installation electrician only (D060 004M cl. 4.1.2 / 4.4).
acsaThreshold: A COC older than two (2) years invalidates a change of ownership (D060 004M cl. 4.4 (h)); the calibration certificate of the testing tools must be presented for every new issue or re-issue of a COC (cl. 4.10.10); yearly COC reconciliation inspection for asset groups BDG, SBD, TRF and LGT, with new COCs issued immediately after any installation or alteration (cl. 4.9.1 / 4.9.2); records retained five (5) years
acsaEvidence: Certificate of Compliance in the latest SANS 10142-1 format
Test report in the format approved by the Chief Inspector
Calibration Certificate - Testing Tools
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit ME 031
acsaConflict: D060 004M expressly EXCLUDES airfield ground lighting systems from its scope, so ACSA has no COC regime covering AGL installations - this check cannot be evidenced against ACSA's own COC procedure for AGL. Separately, cl. 4.8.1 marks Transformers (TRF) as COC-applicable only at FAGG (George), not at FALE, despite transformers existing at King Shaka.
basisNote: SANS 10142-1 and the CoC regime cover the low-voltage installation only; the 11 kV network falls under SANS 10142-2:2018, so an LV CoC is not evidence of MV compliance.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

basis: 1. SANS 1186-1:2015 - symbolic safety signs Part 1: standard signs and general requirements (colours, symbols and placement) 3. OHS Act 85 of 1993 s13 - duty to inform employees of the hazards to health and safety and the precautionary measures to be taken 4. OHS Act 85 of 1993, General Administrative Regulations 2003 reg 4 - a copy of the Act and the relevant regulations kept readily available at the workplace
target: First aid, Emergency, electrical safety sign, PPE
walkabout: Walk each AGL electrical room/work point, including remote outstation cabinets, and visually confirm statutory notices and SANS 1186-1 compliant signage are present, legible, not faded/damaged, and reference current appointees/policy revisions.

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires legal notices and signage to be checked as one of the sixteen all-inclusive DAILY substation checks, with faded or missing signage reported (D060 023M cl. 4.7.4), warning signage inspected weekly (cl. 4.7.4 Weekly), and warning signs and safety devices confirmed present and correctly positioned at the annual transformer major maintenance (cl. 4.7.7). Before isolation a warning notice and prohibitory sign must be affixed at each point from which the apparatus can inadvertently be made alive (D060 013M cl. 4.9.1 / 4.9.3).
acsaThreshold: Legal notices and signage checked Daily (D060 023M cl. 4.7.4); warning signage checked Weekly (cl. 4.7.4 Weekly); no isolation is deemed complete until a warning notice/prohibitory sign is affixed at each point, and warning notices on the control panel shall be the LAST to be removed (D060 013M cl. 4.9.3)
acsaEvidence: Substation logbook (filled out and signed off daily)
Medium Voltage Operating Instruction Form M&E 080
acsaConflict: The daily/weekly signage regime sits in D060 023M, whose scope expressly EXCLUDES AGL; no ACSA procedure sets a statutory-signage requirement for AGL field installations, transformer pits or CCR/MCR rooms specifically.
basisNote: The warning notice and prohibitory sign affixed at each isolation point follow the Operating Regulations for High Voltage Systems (ORHVS), an industry code rather than a statute; EMR reg 5 is the statutory requirement.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

requirement: Ensure all associated regulary checks and functional tests are in place and performed
basis: 1. Civil Aviation Act 13 of 2009, CAR Part 139 reg 139.02.23 - general duties of the licence holder: aerodrome maintained in a serviceable condition under a maintenance programme, with installed apparatus functioning efficiently 2. CAR Part 139 reg 139.02.26 - aerodrome inspection programme (and reg 139.02.11, the approved aerodrome manual in which it sits) 3. ICAO Annex 14 Vol I, Chapter 10 (Maintenance), 10.5 Visual aids - preventive maintenance programme for aerodrome lighting systems 4. ICAO Doc 9137 Airport Services Manual Part 9 (Airport Maintenance Practices) - inspection and maintenance routines for aerodrome lighting
evidenceExpected: Daily AGL serviceability inspection logs and weekly/monthly functional/electrical test reports for the full audit period.
target: Is there daily, weekly, Monthly reports of system performance?
walkabout: Review the daily inspection log for gaps (including weekends/public holidays) and check whether entries look signed off at the time versus batched afterward; cross-reference the logged schedule against the maintenance schedule in the current approved Aerodrome Manual.

acsaRequirement: D060 001M sets ACSA's complete AGL inspection and maintenance matrix by light type - daily inspection of every light type before hours of darkness plus scheduled maintenance - and requires a daily test of all AGL control circuits including mimic panels, with problem circuits repaired immediately (cl. 4.9.19), and monthly functional testing of the field system MCR/CCR with six-monthly maintenance (cl. 4.9.24). At FALE the inspection sheet is the MALMS Engineer system electronic output with M&E 077 as the back-up form (cl. 4.4.8).
acsaThreshold: Approach lights: inspection Daily, maintenance Six Monthly and Yearly (cl. 4.9.1); threshold lights Daily inspection, Two-Weekly maintenance (cl. 4.9.4); runway centre line Daily inspection, photometric Two-Weekly, maintenance Six Monthly and Yearly (cl. 4.9.5); runway edge Daily, photometric Tri-Monthly (cl. 4.9.6); TDZ Daily, photometric Two-Weekly, torque Tri-Monthly (cl. 4.9.7); runway end Daily + Two-Weekly (cl. 4.9.8); stop bars Daily + Six Monthly (cl. 4.9.11); taxiway centre line Daily, torque Tri-Monthly (cl. 4.9.13); taxiway edge Daily, torque Six Monthly (cl. 4.9.14); PAPI Daily (cl. 4.9.15); obstruction lights Daily (cl. 4.9.17); control circuits/mimic panels Daily (cl. 4.9.19); CCR/MCR functional test Monthly, maintenance Six Monthly (cl. 4.9.24); windsock Daily (cl. 4.9.22); signage Daily (cl. 4.9.23)
acsaEvidence: MALMS Engineer system inspection output (FALE, electronically generated)
Planned AGL Maintenance Programme (FALE / King Shaka) M&E 077
Airfield maintenance report
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit ME 031
acsaConflict: Two internal defects in ACSA's own matrix: cl. 4.9.11 leaves the stop-bar torque/corrosion/prism maintenance frequency cell BLANK, and cl. 4.9.15 states the PAPI maintenance interval inconsistently as both 'Bi-Monthly (2M)' and 'Twice Monthly (TM)' in the same table cell.
basisNote: Visual-aid maintenance is 10.5 in the current (8th) edition of Annex 14 Vol I; earlier editions numbered the same material 10.4.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

requirement: Check the degree of abnormality from baseline performance (all systems) through Light output, insulation resistance, PAPI angles
basis: 1. ICAO Annex 14 Vol I, Chapter 8, Table 8-1 - maximum switch-over times by category of operation (one second for the inner 300 m of CAT II/III, 15 seconds for CAT I) 2. ICAO Annex 14 Vol I, 10.5 Visual aids - preventive maintenance and serviceability of lighting measured against its specified photometric performance 3. ICAO Doc 9157 Aerodrome Design Manual Part 4 (Visual Aids) - PAPI beam setting angles and calibration 4. IEC 61821:2011 - maintenance of aeronautical ground lighting constant current series circuits, including insulation-resistance measurement and trending
evidenceExpected:
1. Monthly on-load changeover test record, with measured switch-over time compared against the Annex 14 limit for the facility's category.

2. Current flight-check/calibration report showing PAPI angle results, from the current audit cycle.

3. AGL insulation-resistance test log for runway/taxiway edge and PAPI circuits, with recorded megohm readings (not just pass/fail).
target: PAPI angel < 3 degree Monthly On-Load Testing of Change-over times < 1 sec Photometric test results Insulation Resistance Test Results > 100M Ohm
question:
1. What is the aerodrome's certified lighting category, used to determine the applicable changeover-time limit?

3. Can the >100MΩ insulation-resistance threshold applied here be traced to a source document (OEM spec or internal AGL procedure), or does the SANS 10142-1 general 1.0MΩ minimum apply instead?

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires the Mega Ohm (insulation resistance) reading to be measured on ALL AGL circuits monthly and readings improved when a circuit has reached the airport's recommended minimum, photometric testing of runway centre line and touch down zone lights two-weekly and runway edge lights tri-monthly with the results interpreted, and verification of PAPI angle settings with annual flight calibration synchronised to the ILS glide path.
acsaThreshold: AGL circuit insulation resistance minimum reading 50 kOhm, meggered Monthly (D060 001M cl. 4.9.18); photometric testing of ALL runway centre line lights Two-Weekly (cl. 4.9.5); photometric testing of TDZ lighting for all the lights within 900m of each threshold Two-Weekly (cl. 4.9.7); runway edge photometric testing Tri-Monthly (cl. 4.9.6); PAPI flight calibrations once a year on ILS-equipped runways (cl. 4.9.15); MALMS photometric sensor calibration Yearly and photometric workshop bench sensor calibration Yearly (cl. 4.9.20 / 4.9.21)
acsaEvidence: Annual PAPI flight calibration certificates
MALMS / photometric sensor calibration records
SACAA exemption notice issued while the MALMS sensor is away for calibration
Approach Lighting elevation angle setting results (cl. 4.9.3)
Planned AGL Maintenance Programme (FALE) M&E 077
acsaConflict: ACSA states the interval and the insulation-resistance floor but gives NO photometric pass/fail intensity value (no candela figure or percentage-of-specification limit) against which 'degree of abnormality from baseline' can be judged; that limit sits only in the SACAA TGM and ICAO Annex 14, which cl. 4.7 refers out to.
basisNote: No ICAO or SANS source was confirmed for the >100 MOhm AGL insulation-resistance target; SANS 10142-1 sets a general low-voltage minimum that applies to the LV installation, not to the series circuit, so the threshold must be traced to OEM or ACSA documentation.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

requirement: Check lamp failure rate and spares holding
basis: 1. ICAO Annex 14 Vol I, 10.5 Visual aids - preventive maintenance of lighting systems and the permitted levels of unserviceable lights on precision approach runways 2. Civil Aviation Act 13 of 2009, CAR Part 139 reg 139.02.23 - apparatus installed to promote safety in flight must function efficiently, under a maintenance programme 3. ICAO Doc 9137 Airport Services Manual Part 9 (Airport Maintenance Practices) - maintenance planning and spares provisioning for aerodrome lighting 4. IEC 61821:2011 - lamp and group replacement practice on constant current series circuits (technical standard, not statutory)
evidenceExpected: ACSA's internal AGL serviceability target/procedure; recent lamp-fault/replacement log; current spares stock register.
target: No single ICAO numeric limit exists for fleet-wide AGL lamp failure rate; airports set their own internal serviceability target (commonly ≥95% overall, near-100% for PAPI/threshold/critical lights per CAR 139/SA-CATS 139). The checklist's observed "70" (%) should be checked against ACSA's own documented internal target. Spares holding must be adequate to restore unserviceable lights promptly, particularly critical lights.
walkabout: Check the current lamp-fault log distinguishes critical lights from general edge lighting; physically check spares stock against lamp types in use and against the recent replacement log to see whether restorations were actually prompt.

acsaRequirement: Each airport shall hold adequate AGL spares based on rate of consumption, resupply lead time and shelf life, or alternatively the OEM proposed minimum spare holding per the maintenance manuals, aligned to the SACAA TGM (D060 001M cl. 4.12). On PAPI, when any lamp fails in a group a group replacement shall be made IMMEDIATELY (cl. 4.9.15), and all unserviceable equipment shall be replaced according to ICAO recommendations (cl. 4.8). Storeroom minimum quantities are set by formula in D090 001M.
acsaThreshold: PAPI group replacement IMMEDIATELY on any lamp failure in a group (D060 001M cl. 4.9.15); minimum stock quantity = annual usage divided by twelve (12) months, applied over the lead time period (D090 001M cl. 4.4.6 b)); quarterly inventory counts fixed at end March / June / September / December with a 0.5% KARDEX tolerance above which a variance is a discrepancy (D090 001M cl. 4.4.1 / 4.4.3 c)); stock unused within one (1) year investigated as obsolete (cl. 4.5.1)
acsaEvidence: KARDEX Cards INV 001
Inventory Count Sheet INV 009
Inventory Count Discrepancy Report INV 008
Inventory Purchase Request Form INV 002
Airfield maintenance report
acsaConflict: ACSA sets no lamp-outage rate limit anywhere - there is no percentage-of-lights-unserviceable threshold for a runway, taxiway, approach or stop-bar system in any of the 99 documents, so 'lamp failure rate within limits' has no ACSA figure and must be taken from ICAO Annex 14 / CATS 139.
basisNote: No statute or ICAO SARP fixes a fleet-wide lamp failure percentage - the ICAO serviceability levels bite on precision approach CAT II/III systems - so the 70% figure must be traced to ACSA's own documented target.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

requirement: Ensure an active refurbishment/replacement plans are in accordance to the classification of assets
basis: 1. Civil Aviation Act 13 of 2009, CAR Part 139 reg 139.02.23 - duty to keep the aerodrome and its facilities in a serviceable condition under a maintenance programme 2. ICAO Annex 14 Vol I, Chapter 10 (Maintenance), 10.1 General - aerodrome maintenance programme including preventive maintenance 3. Public Finance Management Act 1 of 1999 s51(1) - the accounting authority is responsible for the management, including the safeguarding and maintenance, of the public entity's assets 4. ISO 55001 (asset management systems) and GRAP 17 (property, plant and equipment, annual review of useful life) - recommended practice and accounting requirement respectively, not safety or aviation law
evidenceExpected: ACSA's internal AGL asset management/life-cycle refurbishment plan, showing assets classified by criticality/age, with evidence of budget approval/scheduling.
target: Active Plans
question: Does ACSA have a current, funded asset management/refurbishment plan for AGL assets, classified by criticality/age, and is it actually being followed — or does replacement happen reactively on failure?
walkabout: Spot-check a sample of older/critical AGL assets on site against what the plan says should have happened to them by now.

acsaRequirement: ACSA classifies assets as Core (essential to airport functioning - named examples include navigational aids and primary electrical power systems), Key (tolerable non-operational for a defined period) and Supporting, and requires a seven-step renewal methodology with condition assessment against six hazards and eleven evaluation dimensions including obsolescence date and availability of spares (D060 026M cl. 4.1-4.2.3). Any extension of an asset's useful life requires nine documented steps ending in Group Executive approval and notification to Finance (cl. 4.2.5).
acsaThreshold: Key Assets are those that can be non-operational for a period of 8 to 48 hours (D060 026M cl. 4.1.2); physical-state test is whether the asset can continue operations for a period of a year or longer (cl. 4.2.2); hazards 3 and 4 (safety, and regulatory/compliance standards) trigger AUTOMATIC consideration of asset replacement (cl. 4.2.2); nine (9) mandatory steps before any useful-life adjustment (cl. 4.2.5); findings presented to MANCO Annually (cl. 4.2.6); system design life 20 years (D100MAN cl. 4.6.2)
acsaEvidence: Engineering Asset Modification Request Form M&E 088
Fixed Asset Register FIN 007
Asset condition assessment, cost estimate and risk assessment records (D060 026M cl. 4.2.7)
Asset Request Form ME 039
Asset Preventative Maintenance Request Form ME 040
basisNote: ACSA is a Schedule 2 major public entity, so the PFMA and not the MFMA is the financial-management authority; the paragraph letter within s51(1) was not confirmed, so it is cited at section level.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires two-weekly photometric testing of all runway centre line lights and of TDZ lighting within 900 m of each threshold with results interpreted, daily inspection of the CRE/MCR with monthly functional testing and six-monthly maintenance of the field CCR/MCR (including measuring output voltage with a true RMS meter), and secondary-power changeover verified by recording the change-over time at the monthly generator on-load test against the ICAO Annex 14 Table 8.1 limits adopted in D118MAN.
acsaThreshold: UPS/secondary power switchover for CAT II/III: inner 300 m of the approach lighting system = 1 second, runway threshold = 1 second, runway end = 1 second, runway centreline = 1 second, runway touchdown zone = 1 second, all stop bars = 1 second, other parts of the approach lighting system / runway edge / essential taxiway / obstacle = 15 seconds (D118MAN cl. 4.3.6); photometric testing Two-Weekly for centre line and for TDZ lights within 900m of each threshold (D060 001M cl. 4.9.5 / 4.9.7); CCR/MCR functional test Monthly, maintenance Six Monthly (cl. 4.9.24); generator on-load test minimum 15 minutes Monthly recording the change-over time (D060 006M cl. 4.5.7)
acsaEvidence: MALMS Engineer system inspection output (FALE)
Planned AGL Maintenance Programme (FALE) M&E 077
Monthly generator on-load test record including the recorded change-over time
acsaConflict: ACSA sets no lamp-outage percentage limit for AGL, and D060 006M cl. 4.5.7 defers the numeric change-over limit to ICAO Annex 14 rather than stating it; the figures must be pulled across from D118MAN cl. 4.3.6, which is a design manual for new/replacement UPS rather than a maintenance acceptance criterion.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

requirement:
Cable Arrangement, trenching, Handling shall be observed to SANS 10198
Arrangement of electric apparatus must afford accessibility to each part as needed to facilitate proper inspection, adjustment, maintenance, or replacement (Both within and outside).
basis: SANS 10142 - The wiring of premises - Part 1: Low-voltage installations SANS 10198 - Jointing and termination of paper insulated cables

acsaRequirement: ACSA's strategy for new electrical system installations is that associated MV and LV cabling is inspected and maintained only at fault condition and shall 'Run-To-Failure'; on commissioning or recommissioning seven tests shall be done - safety test, MV phasing test, phase rotation sequence test, phase to phase impedance test, phase to earth impedance test, insulation resistance and voltage withstand level, and labelling and signage (D060 023M cl. 4.7.11). Substation installation, maintenance and housekeeping shall follow SANS 60076-1, SANS 10142-1 and SANS 10142-2 (cl. 4.7.4 note); cable trenches and ducts shall be sized for future feeders (D119MAN cl. 3.3.2).
acsaThreshold: Seven (7) commissioning/recommissioning tests for MV and LV cabling; run-to-failure strategy for ALL MV and LV cabling; stored cable drums to be rolled Yearly and MV cable repairs (cable identification and cable spiking) on an ADHOC basis (D060 023M cl. 4.7.11 / 4.7.5). No numeric clearance or accessibility dimension is stated (D119MAN cl. 3.3.5)
acsaEvidence: Commissioning test records for new MV/LV cabling
As-built drawings and single line diagram
Certificate of Compliance and test report (D060 004M)
acsaConflict: Two conflicts. First, D060 023M cl. 4.7.11 adopts an explicit RUN-TO-FAILURE strategy for ALL MV and LV cabling, which removes any periodic cable inspection, testing or trench/cover integrity regime and is at odds with the audit expectation of scheduled cable testing. Second, no ACSA document in the set cites SANS 10198 (the standard named in the check) at all - ACSA's cabling standards are SANS 10142-1/-2, SANS 876 and SANS 1019.
pfq: Switchgear and generators, central to the distribution network, rated Unacceptable; distribution system Tolerable until those findings are closed.

acsaRequirement: ACSA fixes the quality-of-supply envelope for its distribution network and the redundancy rules for the assets feeding it: power factor to be maintained at a minimum, standard frequency and voltage-drop deviations set, parallel operation of transformers generally NOT permitted (redundancy achieved by manual intervention with a mechanical interlock), N+1 redundancy considered for airfield substations, terminal building and core and key assets, and N-1 firmness required of the UPS system and associated distribution network. acsaRequirement: ACSA requires annual circuit breaker maintenance with an outage covering trip test, auto trip/close/trip illuminations, vacuum interrupter checks, primary contact resistance check, closing and trip solenoid service and interlock lubrication (D060 018M cl. 4.7); the annual MV switchgear service in D060 023M cl. 4.7.5 names the same four certificate-generating tests the check asks for - circuit breaker functional testing (SF6/vacuum), continuity test, contact resistance test and circuit breaker speed test - performed per D060 018M.
acsaThreshold: Circuit breaker functional testing (SF6/vacuum), continuity test, contact resistance test and circuit breaker speed test: Yearly (Y), outage REQUIRED (D060 023M cl. 4.7.5; D060 018M cl. 4.7). Four-tier ladder applies to every breaker: Monthly inspection, Yearly, Tri-Yearly (3Y) and Six-Yearly (6Y) maintenance (D060 018M cl. 4.3). At FALE (King Shaka) the applicability table gives Oil = N, SF6 = N, Vacuum = Y - only vacuum circuit breakers exist, so SF6 test certificates should not be expected (cl. 4.3)
acsaEvidence: Annual Inspections for 11kV Circuit Breakers (Electrical Department record)
Monthly Inspection Report for Air Circuit Breakers ME 033
MV Switchgear Calibration Certificate
ORHVS Certificate of the authorised person
Authorization letter by GMR 2.1
acsaConflict: D060 018M prescribes the contact resistance, dielectric strength and moisture content tests but states NO numeric pass/fail limits for any of them (cl. 4.5 / 4.7), and no numeric SF6 gas pressure limit (cl. 4.6) - so the certificates can be tested for existence and date but not against an ACSA acceptance value.

siteVariant.note: Circuit breaker functional testing (SF6/vacuum), continuity test, contact resistance test and circuit breaker speed test: Yearly (Y), outage REQUIRED (D060 023M cl. 4.7.5; D060 018M cl. 4.7). Four-tier ladder applies to every breaker: Monthly inspection, Yearly, Tri-Yearly (3Y) and Six-Yearly (6Y) maintenance (D060 018M cl. 4.3). At FALE (King Shaka) the applicability table gives Oil = N, SF6 = N, Vacuum = Y - only vacuum circuit breakers exist, so SF6 test certificates should not be expected (cl. 4.3)

basisNote: No OHS Act regulation names SF6/vacuum functional, continuity, contact-resistance and breaker-speed testing or a twelve-month interval, so a finding rests on the general duty to maintain safe plant plus ACSA's own procedure and the OEM schedule; IEC 62271-100 covers AC circuit-breaker performance.

requirement: Annual switchgear maintenance report evidences ALL required checks: VCB service & timing, protection relay secondary-injection tests, auxiliary relays, panel/busbar inspection, insulation resistance, contact resistance.
basis: OHS Act - Electrical Machinery Regulations; OEM maintenance manual; ACSA D060 procedures
evidenceExpected: Signed maintenance reports (last 12 months) per switchboard
target: 100% of checks evidenced [PRIOR FINDING Mar 2025]
question: What corrective action was taken to close the March 2025 finding, and has it been verified fixed for switchboards beyond the one originally flagged?
walkabout: Pick a sample switchboard, note its serial/asset number, and match it to its maintenance report; check the report shows actual results for all six checks; look for a physical sign the board was actually opened and serviced around the report date (service sticker, tamper seal broken and replaced, fresh grease on moving parts).

acsaRequirement: The annual MV switchgear service with outage shall cover panel structure integrity, panel cleaning, cabling and termination visual inspection, circuit breaker functional/continuity/contact resistance/speed testing per D060 018M, CT and VT visual inspection, VT alignment and fuses, CT knee point voltage test and CT saturation curve test, metering equipment calibration and testing, protection equipment calibration and testing with settings confirmed against design, indication lighting functionality, and battery tripping unit servicing including measuring and recording battery voltage and confirming TRICKLE charge operation (D060 023M cl. 4.7.5).
acsaThreshold: MV switchgear full service Yearly (Y), outage REQUIRED (D060 023M cl. 4.7.5); breaker ladder Monthly inspection / Yearly / Tri-Yearly (3Y, adds selector servicing, DC battery unit servicing and protection relay and remote control servicing) / Six-Yearly (6Y, adds busbar maintenance, breaker chamber maintenance, CT chamber maintenance and a Ductor test on busbars) (D060 018M cl. 4.5 / 4.6 / 4.7); calibration certificates for Metering Equipment and Protection Equipment kept with the Electrical Maintenance Department (D060 023M cl. 4.8)

acsaConflict: ACSA's wording is 'protection equipment calibration and testing with settings confirmed against design' - it does not name secondary injection testing, and it states no numeric limit for the CT knee point voltage, contact resistance or the battery tripping unit voltage that must be 'measured and recorded'. The 3Y and 6Y tiers are the ones most likely to be missing from a KSIA PM history.
pfq: Switchgear annual maintenance reports inadequate, do not show all required checks on VCB, protection & auxiliary relays, panels and busbars.

requirement: MV switchgear age/condition assessed; refurbishment or replacement plan in place for units beyond design life (>25-30 yrs) or with obsolete spares.

evidenceExpected: Condition assessment report; capital plan entry
target: Plan exists & funded
walkabout: Check the nameplate/manufacture date on a sample of switchgear units against the condition assessment; look for visible wear, corrosion, or degraded control wiring consistent with age, and check whether that unit appears on the refurbishment plan if it looks due.

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires assets approaching or at end of life to be identified regularly from maintenance records, performance indicators and asset life expectancy data, assessed against six hazards (criticality, physical state, safety, regulatory and compliance standards, lifecycle phase, performance/KPIs) and eleven evaluation dimensions expressly including whether the equipment has passed its obsolescence date and the availability of spares; safety and regulatory/compliance hazards trigger automatic consideration of replacement (D060 026M cl. 4.2.2 / 4.2.3). MV switchgear at an airfield substation falls in the Core Asset tier (cl. 4.1.1).
acsaThreshold: Physical-state test: can the asset continue operations for a period of a year or longer (D060 026M cl. 4.2.2); hazards 3 and 4 trigger AUTOMATIC consideration of asset replacement or at minimum a risk assessment and mitigation strategy (cl. 4.2.2); nine (9) mandatory steps before adjusting an asset's useful life, ending in Group Executive: CIAM and/or Operations Management approval and notification to Finance for update of Fixed Asset Register FIN 007 (cl. 4.2.5); system design life 20 years (D100MAN cl. 4.6.2)
acsaEvidence: Asset condition assessment records
Fixed Asset Register FIN 007
Engineering Asset Modification Request Form M&E 088
MANCO approval records (D060 026M cl. 4.2.6)
acsaConflict: ACSA states NO design-life figure for MV switchgear. The only design-life number anywhere in the set is D100MAN cl. 4.6.2's 'System Design life - 20 years' for energy systems, so the checklist's '>25-30 yrs beyond design life' test has no ACSA basis and should be recorded as an ACSA gap rather than measured against ACSA's own figure.

requirement: Switching procedures, authorised persons (switching authority) register, arc-flash PPE and lock-out/tag-out available and used.

question:

2. Is LOTO actually enforced with checks/audits, or does the paper procedure get bypassed for a quick job?

2. Physically inspect arc-flash PPE (suits, visors, gloves) for condition and in-date inspection tags; check LOTO padlocks and permits are on hand and show signs of actual use, not just stored unused.

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires written authorisation for every person operating the 11 kV network, a maintained register of the names and telephone numbers of all authorised operating persons and the EXTENT of their authorisation (D060 013M cl. 4.2), a Permit to Work issued only by an authorised person to a competent responsible person with a Risk Assessment and Workers Register completed before any work (D060 011M cl. 4.3 / 4.11), an ORHVS certificate and a GMR 2.1 authorisation letter for authorised switching personnel (D060 018M cl. 4.11), isolators locked whether open or closed and every interlock defeat recorded in the logbook by the Maintenance Manager/Engineer (D060 013M cl. 4.6.6 / 4.6.7).

Also, D060 011M cl. 4.7 permits a responsible person to hold more than one permit at a time whereas D060 013M cl. 4.8.4 states no person shall work under more than one - the two ACSA procedures are worded differently. ACSA specifies no arc-flash incident-energy study or labelling requirement, only the SANS 724 PPE standard.

requirement: Dedicated electrical rooms for MV breaker, Transformer, LV Room, Generator Room and Battery room/UPS)
basis: Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 (Act No. 85 of 1993) ORHVS - Operating Regulations of High Voltage System
target: Dedicated, segregated rooms are expected for MV switchgear/breakers, transformers, LV distribution, generators, and battery/UPS — separating incompatible risks (arc-flash, fire load, battery gassing, noise) and restricting access to authorised persons only (OHS Act general duty; Eskom Standard 32-846 ORHVS; EMR reg 6).
walkabout: Walk each room and confirm it is physically separate from the others, has its own access control (not a shared key/card across risk classes), and contains only its designated equipment (no incompatible storage, e.g. flammables in the battery room, or generator/battery rooms combined).

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires transformers to be installed in a DEDICATED ROOM separate from other electrical or mechanical equipment, with fire-rated walls, floors and ceilings providing full enclosure, all cable trenches, ducts and wall penetrations fire-sealed to maintain the fire rating, and for oil-filled units reinforced firewalls designed to withstand internal fault pressure or explosion forces plus oil containment (bund walls, oil catchment trenches, sumps, oil-water separation) (D119MAN cl. 3.3.4). Dry-type transformers are PREFERRED for indoor installations in occupied buildings and substations within terminals (cl. 4.1.1). UPS installations require proper ventilation and thermal management, safe and accessible layout, correct earthing and bonding and an adequate enclosure IP rating (D118MAN cl. 4.3.11).
acsaThreshold: Transformers in a dedicated room, fire-rated full enclosure with fire-sealed penetrations and oil containment for oil-filled units - but NO numeric fire rating (minutes/hours) and NO bund capacity percentage is stated (D119MAN cl. 3.3.4). No numeric IP rating value is stated (cl. 7.8). ACSA's asset-group frequency table treats Substations (BDG), MV switchgear, LV switchboard, transformers, PFC, mini-substations and RMUs as distinct asset groups with distinct inspection regimes (D060 023M cl. 4.7.2)
acsaEvidence: Register for Transformers and Substations EMS 104
MV Electrical Installation Safety Report (D119MAN cl. 8.5)
As-built drawings and layout drawing showing mounting positions and free space (D118MAN cl. 7/8)
acsaConflict: D119MAN mandates a fire-rated dedicated transformer room and oil containment but states no fire-resistance duration and no bund capacity, so 'adequately segregated and fire-rated' cannot be tested against an ACSA figure. There is no ACSA requirement anywhere for separate dedicated rooms for LV, generator or battery/UPS plant - only for transformers.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

requirement: Rooms have adeqaute vetilation & cooling, fire protected, Roden free, Corrosion protected/free, drainage outlets
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Electrical Machinery Regulations 2011 reg 6 - switchgear and transformer premises to be sufficiently ventilated to keep equipment at a safe working temperature, proof against rodents, leakage, seepage and flooding, adequately lit, doors opening outwards, with fire-extinguishing appliances maintained in working order 2. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Environmental Regulations for Workplaces 1987 reg 5 - ventilation of every workplace by natural or mechanical means 3. SANS 10400-T - the application of the National Building Regulations Part T: fire protection of the building and its rooms 4. SANS 10105-1 - the use and control of fire-fighting equipment, including servicing of portable extinguishers
evidenceExpected: Current fire-suppression system service/inspection certificate.
target: Electrical plant rooms must be adequately ventilated/cooled to manufacturer/design ratings, fire-protected (fire detection/suppression appropriate to electrical risk, not water-based, in live LV/MV rooms), free of rodent ingress and corrosion, and fitted with drainage to prevent water ingress/pooling (EMR reg 6). No single generic numeric SANS value applies to all rooms — check against the specific OEM design spec.
walkabout: In each electrical plant room, confirm ventilation fans/cooling are actually running (not just installed); check the fire-suppression certificate date; visually inspect for rodent droppings/nesting in cable trays or under raised flooring, corrosion on busbars/cable trays, and functioning floor drains.

acsaRequirement: The sixteen all-inclusive DAILY substation checks include ensuring no excessive heat build-up, inspecting fireproofing and confirming room integrity is valid, no water accumulation, all equipment free of dust, the fire extinguisher system in working order, and checking for visible holes allowing unauthorised access which must be blanked off (D060 023M cl. 4.7.4); daily inspection also covers air conditioning and gaseous suppression pressure. The WEEKLY visual inspection expressly covers substation floors, water leaks, vegetation ingress/growth and RODENTS/VERMIN (cl. 4.7.4 Weekly). Corrosion protection shall follow SANS 780 appropriate to coastal exposure - directly relevant to KSIA (D119MAN cl. 7.6).
acsaThreshold: Sixteen (16) daily substation checks including fireproofing/room integrity, no excessive heat build-up, no water accumulation and fire extinguisher serviceability (D060 023M cl. 4.7.4, Daily, outage NOT required); rodents/vermin, vegetation ingress and water leaks inspected Weekly (cl. 4.7.4 Weekly); transformer rust, corrosion or defective coating inspected, cleaned and painted Yearly (cl. 4.7.7); UPS normal operating environment temperature 0 degC to +40 degC, relative humidity 20% to 80%, altitude up to 1000 m without derating (D118MAN cl. 8.2)
acsaEvidence: Substation logbook (filled out and signed off daily)
Weekly Inspection Report for Electrical Power Transformers Form M&E 001
Annual UPS service record including measured and recorded UPS room temperature
acsaConflict: No numeric ventilation rate, room-temperature limit or fire-resistance rating is stated for substations, transformer rooms or battery rooms; the only environmental figures in the set are D118MAN's UPS operating envelope (0-40 degC, 20-80% RH). D119MAN cl. 3.3.4 states no bund capacity percentage.
basisNote: EMR reg 6 is the direct statutory hit - ventilation, vermin, seepage/flooding and fire appliances are all named in it - but it sets no numeric value, so cooling performance must be judged against the OEM or design rating.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

requirement: Clear accesss and spacing shall be observed for all electrical equipment
basis: NRS 060 - Code of practice for clearances for electrical systems with rated voltages up to and including 145kV, for the safety of persons.
target: NRS 060 sets minimum clearance/access-space distances around electrical equipment (live parts, switchgear, busbars), scaled to system voltage. Measured clearances around MV/LV switchgear and busbars must meet or exceed the NRS 060 table for the installed voltage class, with clear, unobstructed access maintained.
walkabout: Measure clearance distances around MV/LV switchgear and busbars on site and compare against the NRS 060 clearance table for the installed voltage class; check for storage or clutter encroaching into the clearance zone, and for any added equipment/trunking that may have reduced clearances since installation.

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires that substation doors are serviceable, lockable and UNOBSTRUCTED, that all conductors are insulated/covered and not lying on the floor, and that all emergency EXIT door mechanisms are in order - all as part of the sixteen daily substation checks (D060 023M cl. 4.7.4). Design shall incorporate adequate working space clearances, safe access routes and escape paths, clearly defined isolation points and accessibility for condition monitoring and testing equipment, and future construction around existing transformer installations shall NOT compromise statutory access or maintenance clearances (D119MAN cl. 3.3.5).
acsaThreshold: Doors serviceable, lockable and unobstructed and emergency EXIT door mechanisms in order: checked Daily (D060 023M cl. 4.7.4); to facilitate emergency exit exactly ONE door or gate shall remain unlocked while work or operating is in progress, provided no unauthorised person can gain unrestricted access (D060 013M cl. 4.5.1). NO numeric working-clearance dimension is stated (D119MAN cl. 3.3.5)
acsaEvidence: Substation logbook
Layout drawing showing mounting positions and free space (D118MAN cl. 7/8)
acsaConflict: ACSA prescribes the accessibility principle but no measurable clearance (no front/rear/side working space dimension, no escape-route width), so 'clear access and spacing shall be observed' has no ACSA figure - the auditor must fall back on SANS 10142-1/-2. This is itself a recordable gap.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

requirement: Existence and adherence to Emergency plans
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993 s8(1) - general duty to provide and maintain a working environment that is safe and without risk to the health of employees 2. Civil Aviation Act 13 of 2009, CAR Part 139 reg 139.02.14 - establishment of an aerodrome emergency management system 3. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Major Hazard Installation Regulations 2022 reg 15 - on-site emergency plan developed in accordance with SANS 1514 and, under reg 15(4)(e), tested or exercised in practice at least once a year 4. Electrical Machinery Regulations 2011 reg 5(c) and 5(d) - notices at electrical premises giving the procedure in case of fire and directions for resuscitating persons suffering from electric shock
evidenceExpected: Current written emergency response plan covering electrical incidents; drill/training attendance records for the audit period.
target: Emergency response plans covering electrical incidents (fire, arc-flash, MV/HV fault, loss of power to critical airport systems) must exist, be current, and be demonstrably exercised/drilled (OHS Act s.8 general duty).
walkabout: Confirm the plan references the actual electrical rooms/plant on site, not just a generic site-wide document; check evacuation routes/assembly points named in the plan still match the current site layout.

acsaRequirement: For the 11 kV network ACSA requires that on any failure or interruption of supply, or if abnormal conditions arise including signs of approaching inclement weather, the Maintenance Manager/Engineer is informed as soon as possible, and that ANY PERSON is authorised to carry out emergency switching, reporting it as soon as possible afterwards (D060 013M cl. 4.15); in an emergency where human life is endangered any person may open the key cabinet, breaking the transparent window or seal, and must then take possession of all keys and report it (cl. 4.6.3). No outage lead times apply to faults, unplanned outages or emergency switching, and emergency switching may only be conducted if people and equipment are exposed to danger (D060 019M cl. 4.2.4).
acsaThreshold: No lead time applies to faults, unplanned outages or emergency switching (D060 019M cl. 4.2.4); every emergency switching event must be recorded with its time, details and the names of the persons who carried it out on the Medium Voltage Operating Instruction Form M&E 080 (D060 013M cl. 4.1). For the Fuel Depot only, the emergency plan shall be current and TESTED at least every twelve (12) months with records of the practice test kept for audit (D060 021M cl. 4.11 b))
acsaEvidence: Medium Voltage Operating Instruction Form M&E 080 (time, details and names for every emergency switching event)
Key cabinet seal/window breakage reports
Fuel Depot emergency plan and 12-monthly practice test records
acsaConflict: ACSA has NO substation or electrical-network emergency plan requirement and NO test interval for one. The only emergency plan in the electrical set that must exist, be current and be tested annually is the Fuel Depot plan (D060 021M cl. 4.11 b)), which is submitted to the DOE/NERSA annually. A substation emergency plan check cannot be evidenced against an ACSA requirement.
basisNote: MHI reg 15 applies only where the fuel installation meets the major hazard installation thresholds, but it is the source of the twelve-monthly practice test ACSA applies at the fuel depot; the 2022 regulations replaced the 2001 set, in which the same duty sat at reg 6.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

OHS Act 85 of 1993, Electrical Machinery Regulations 2011 reg 4 - precautions before work on disconnected electrical machinery, which depend on the diagram matching the installation

acsaRequirement: ACSA's annual transformer major maintenance (outage required) includes transformer oil tests and analysis, scanning the transformer with an infra-red tester to check for abnormal hot spots, and inspection of earthing and its resistance (D060 023M cl. 4.7.7). Oil test limits are stated only for PCB content; if PCBs are present the oil shall be removed and replaced IMMEDIATELY and safely disposed of (cl. 4.7.7 item 2). Thermographic inspection of bus bars and hot connections is required annually on LV panels and mini-substations (cl. 4.7.6 / 4.7.9).
acsaThreshold: PCB content of RECLAIMED mineral insulating oils not more than 20 mg/kg, and UNDETECTABLE in unused oils, determined per IEC 61619 to SANS 555 - tested Yearly with outage (D060 023M cl. 4.7.7 items 6 and 7); infra-red hot-spot scan, earthing and its resistance inspection, and oil tests: Yearly (Y), outage REQUIRED (cl. 4.7.7); LV bus bar thermographic inspection and mini-substation hot connection infra-red scanning: Yearly (cl. 4.7.6 / 4.7.9)
acsaEvidence: Transformer oil test and analysis reports (PCB content per IEC 61619 / SANS 555)
Register for Transformers and Substations EMS 104
Weekly Inspection Report for Electrical Power Transformers Form M&E 001
Service Report per Mini-Substation
acsaConflict: MATERIAL GAP. D119MAN, ACSA's own transformer manual, contains NO in-service oil test limits at all - no breakdown voltage (BDV), no acidity, no moisture ppm, no dissolved gas analysis (DGA) limits - and no winding or oil temperature alarm or trip settings; D060 023M cl. 4.7.7 states NO numeric earth resistance limit and NO hot-spot temperature limit. The only numeric oil figure in the entire ACSA set is PCB 20 mg/kg. A transformer oil-condition (DGA/BDV) or earthing-resistance check therefore cannot be evidenced against an ACSA figure. Note also that EMS 104 carries a THREE (3) year retention while every other record in D060 023M is retained five (5) years.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

requirement: Functional test records - Monthly (AGL related) and yearly (all)

Civil Aviation Act 13 of 2009, CAR Part 139 reg 139.02.10A(6) - adequate primary power supply for air navigation facilities, arranged so that facilities connect automatically to the secondary supply on failure of the primary source 2. ICAO Annex 14 Vol I, Chapter 8, Table 8-1 - maximum switch-over times, which the monthly on-load changeover test must demonstrate 3. ICAO Doc 9157 Aerodrome Design Manual Part 5 (Electrical Systems) - secondary power supply, generating plant and changeover arrangements 4. OHS Act 85 of 1993, General Machinery Regulations 1988 reg 2 - written designation of a competent person to supervise the machinery
evidenceExpected:
1. Monthly on-load test/run logs for AGL-critical standby generators, covering the full audit period.

2. Annual test certificates for all other standby generators, covering the full audit period.
target:
1. AGL-related generators: functionally tested (start, transfer, run-on-load) at least monthly, consistent with the secondary-power reliability duty under CAR 139.02.10A; logs must cover the full audit period with no gaps.

2. All other standby generators: functionally tested at least annually (GMR regs 2/3).
question: 1. Are generators actually run on load during tests, or just started/idled, and is the ATS changeover time timed as part of the routine?
walkabout:
1. Check the monthly log for gaps (e.g. skipped over a holiday period); check whether run duration, load percentage and fuel/oil pressure readings are recorded, not just "ran OK".

2. Check the annual test certificate date and confirm it records the generator being run under load, with measured readings recorded.

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires each diesel generator to be tested OFF LOAD weekly and ON LOAD monthly, with a yearly service, and the alternator and controls maintained weekly with a yearly service (D060 006M cl. 4.5.2 / 4.5.7). The weekly alternator check requires voltage and amps per phase to be checked AND RECORDED and all alarm circuits (high temperature, low oil pressure, over speed, low fuel warning) checked (cl. 4.5.4).
acsaThreshold: Test each diesel generator OFF LOAD for a MINIMUM OF FIVE (5) MINUTES weekly, recording engine oil pressure, dynamo charging readings, strange noise, active alarms or indication lights and any oil/fuel leaks (D060 006M cl. 4.5.7, Weekly, outage REQUIRED); test each diesel generator ON LOAD for a MINIMUM OF 15 MINUTES monthly, recording the change-over time between simulated mains failure shut down and generator supply restoration (cl. 4.5.7, Monthly); yearly service; asset frequency matrix Generator Set (GST) W + M + Y, Alternator and Controls (ALT) W + Y (cl. 4.5.2)
acsaEvidence: Weekly generator off-load test records
Monthly generator on-load test records including the recorded change-over time
Weekly alternator recorded voltage and amps per phase
Annual generator fuel sample analysis results
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit ME 031
acsaConflict: ACSA's regime is stricter than the checklist assumes: it requires a WEEKLY off-load run (not monthly) plus a MONTHLY on-load run, and it does not distinguish 'AGL related' generators from others. Statutory calibration certificates: NONE required (D060 006M cl. 4.6).
basisNote: No South African statute fixes the weekly, monthly or annual generator test intervals - those are OEM and ACSA driven - and CAR 139.02.10A was only inserted in 2025, so the enforceable point is that the secondary supply works within the Table 8-1 switch-over time.
pfq: No diesel cut-out fuse installed on any generator (fire isolation); oil leaks on the floor of some airside substations; maintenance records run to March 2024; weekly off-load, monthly on-load tests and annual service to be evidenced.

SANS 10089-3:2010 - the installation, modification and decommissioning of underground storage tanks, pumps/dispensers and pipework: the leak and pressure testing standard for underground fuel lines 4. requirement: Demarcation of Noise Zones and requirements for hearing protection
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Noise Exposure Regulations, 2024 (GN R.5953, 6 March 2025) reg 11 — designation and clear demarcation of a noise zone 2. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Noise-Induced Hearing Loss Regulations, 2003 (GN R.307) reg 9 — noise zone demarcation, notices and compulsory hearing protection (reg 3 sets the 85 dBA noise-rating limit) 3. SANS 1186-1:2015 (Ed. 3.7) Symbolic safety signs Part 1: Standard signs and general requirements — form, colour and siting of the mandatory hearing-protection and noise-zone signs 4. SANS 10083:2013 — measurement and assessment of occupational noise for hearing conservation purposes, the method that fixes where the zone boundary falls

walkabout: Walk the plant areas identified in the noise assessment as noise zones and check signage is present, legible, and correctly specifies the hearing protection required; check any area added/changed since the last assessment has since been signed.

basis: 1. Major Hazard Installation Regulations, 2022 reg 10, reg 12 and reg 15 — risk assessment, safety report and on-site emergency plan for a registered establishment 3. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Explosives Regulations, 2024 (GN R.5048, 23 July 2024) — licensing of an explosives workplace, danger areas and danger buildings; repeals the Explosives Regulations, 2002 4. SANS 10089-1 — the petroleum industry Part 1: storage and distribution of petroleum products in above-ground bulk installations (bulk diesel tank installation and separation distances)

2. Any Explosives Act licence/declaration, if explosives distinct from diesel fuel are stored.

MHI declaration: if ACSA's bulk diesel fuel inventory for standby generators exceeds the Major Hazard Installation Regulations (MHIR, GNR.692) schedule threshold quantities, the installation must be declared/registered as a Major Hazard Installation, with a risk assessment/on-site emergency plan maintained — exact threshold quantity applicable to diesel not confirmed this session.

requirement: Requirement to not expose personnel to >85dBA subject to regulation 9 and 10(1)
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Noise Exposure Regulations, 2024 (GN R.5953, 6 March 2025) reg 3 — no person may be exposed at or above the noise-rating limit or noise action level 2. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Noise-Induced Hearing Loss Regulations, 2003 (GN R.307) reg 3, reg 10 and reg 12 — 85 dBA noise-rating limit, hierarchy of control, hearing protective equipment 4. acsaRequirement: Where noise exceeds 85 dBA ACSA requires control measures to reduce noise AT SOURCE BEFORE resorting to hearing protection, using the best reasonably practical engineering methods to reduce the level below 85 dBA including acoustically enclosing machines, processes or operators (S010 001WI cl. 4.4 / 4.4.1). acsaThreshold: Generator OFF-LOAD test: minimum of FIVE (5) MINUTES, WEEKLY (D060 006M cl. 4.5.7); generator ON-LOAD test: minimum of 15 MINUTES, MONTHLY, recording the change-over time between simulated mains failure shut down and generator supply restoration, engine oil pressure, coolant temperature, dynamo charging readings, exhaust smoke/breather fumes condition and any oil and fuel leaks (cl. 4.5.7); yearly service including bulk tank bottom and primary filter fuel samples for contamination analysis (cl. 4.5.7); frequency matrix GST = Weekly + Monthly maintenance, Yearly service (cl. 4.5.2)

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires a WEEKLY inspection of oil transformers by authorised personnel only, covering oil leaks, active silica gel colour, flags on protection devices including Buchholz, excessive heat generation where a thermistor is fitted, confirmation that the tap changer is locked, and requires the TEMPERATURE GAUGE AND WINDING GAUGES TO BE CHECKED AND RECORDED along with the oil level gauge (D060 023M cl. 4.7.7). Dry-type transformers are inspected weekly with the temperature checked and recorded. Power transformers shall be provided with remote monitoring giving real-time visibility of temperature, loading, alarms and fault conditions (D119MAN cl. 7.5). The factory baseline is set by twelve routine tests and nine type tests (D119MAN cl. 8.1.2 / 8.1.3).
acsaThreshold: Weekly recording of temperature gauge and winding gauge readings and oil level gauge - but NO numeric temperature limit is stated (D060 023M cl. 4.7.7, Weekly, outage NOT required); annual major maintenance with infra-red hot-spot scan - no hot-spot limit stated (cl. 4.7.7, Yearly, outage required); twelve (12) routine tests before the transformer leaves the factory and nine (9) type tests per design, including no-load loss and current measured at 90% and 110% of rated voltage (D119MAN cl. 8.1.2 / 8.1.3)
acsaEvidence: Weekly Inspection Report for Electrical Power Transformers Form M&E 001
Register for Transformers and Substations EMS 104
Routine test reports (12 tests) per SANS 780 and SANS 60076-1
Type test certificates/reports (9 tests), submitted at ECSA Stage 4
acsaConflict: MATERIAL GAP. ACSA requires the temperature and winding gauge readings to be RECORDED weekly but sets no alarm or trip value; D119MAN, the transformer manual itself, contains NO temperature alarm or trip settings, NO in-service oil test limits (no BDV, acidity, moisture or DGA) and no BIL value (it refers out to SANS 60076-3). 'Degree of abnormality from baseline performance' therefore cannot be evidenced against any ACSA figure - the only numeric transformer limit ACSA states is PCB 20 mg/kg in D060 023M cl. 4.7.7.
basisNote: IEC 60422 and IEC 60599 are cited at document level and are engineering good practice adopted by ACSA — no South African regulation prescribes an oil-test or DGA frequency for transformers, so a finding here is a maintenance-standard finding, not a statutory contravention.
pfq: TRF 02 at AS1 off (oil below minimum); AS4 TRF 01 and 02 indicate partial discharges; Basement Chamber A1 TRF 04 and 05 indicate a high-range thermal fault (above 700 °C); production rates to be monitored.

Service Report per Mini-Substation
Transformer oil test and analysis reports

No Buchholz alarm/trip setting, no temperature alarm/trip setting and no loading limit figure are stated anywhere; D119MAN also mis-cites 'SANS 1042-2' where SANS 10142-2 is intended.

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires MONTHLY UPS maintenance (visual inspection, dust removal from batteries and UPS, inspection of wiring for overheating and insulation breakdown, review of the event log, cabinet fans, checking and RECORDING the battery charger charge rate, air filter inspection and replacement, verification of metering display accuracy, input and output current and voltage readings, load sharing verification on parallel systems and recording of event memories) and an ANNUAL service that measures and records UPS room temperature, % load, charger voltage, battery cells, inverter output voltage, current, frequency and power factor, records alarm conditions, performs lamp test and static and manual bypass switch tests, measures and verifies capacitor and rectifier values, and simulates mains failure with an on-load test, expressly requiring any EXCESSIVE HEAT BUILD-UP IN THE UPS ROOM TO BE RECORDED AS THIS REDUCES BATTERY LIFE (D060 006M cl. 4.5.6). The Rotary UPS regime applies at only FALE and FAOR and includes an annual BATTERY BANK DISCHARGE TEST.
acsaThreshold: UPS maintenance MONTHLY and service YEARLY; Battery Tripping Unit maintenance MONTHLY (measure and record battery voltage, ensure TRICKLE charge operational) and service TRI-MONTHLY (top up cells with distilled water) (D060 006M cl. 4.5.2 / 4.5.5 / 4.5.6); rotary UPS annual battery bank DISCHARGE TEST recording battery bank DC voltage on discharge, discharging current with customer load and battery voltage - applicable at FALE and FAOR ONLY (cl. 4.5.6); UPS operating environment temperature 0 degC to +40 degC and relative humidity 20% to 80% (D118MAN cl. 8.2); battery technology shall be lithium-ion (cl. 8.6); availability 99,5% and N-1 firmness (cl. 4.3.1)
acsaEvidence: Monthly UPS maintenance record (recorded battery charger charge rate, input/output current and voltage readings, event memories)
Annual UPS service record (UPS room temperature, % load, charger voltage, battery cell readings, inverter output, bypass switch test, capacitor and rectifier values)
Annual rotary UPS battery bank discharge test record (FALE and FAOR)
acsaConflict: MATERIAL GAP. D118MAN specifies NO minimum battery autonomy in minutes and no battery end-of-life or replacement criterion despite mandating lithium-ion; no battery IMPEDANCE test is prescribed anywhere in ACSA's set. The only capacity evidence ACSA requires is the annual rotary-UPS battery bank discharge test, which applies at FALE but not to static UPS units. An autonomy/capacity check therefore has no ACSA figure.

siteVariant.note: UPS maintenance MONTHLY and service YEARLY; Battery Tripping Unit maintenance MONTHLY (measure and record battery voltage, ensure TRICKLE charge operational) and service TRI-MONTHLY (top up cells with distilled water) (D060 006M cl. 4.5.2 / 4.5.5 / 4.5.6); rotary UPS annual battery bank DISCHARGE TEST recording battery bank DC voltage on discharge, discharging current with customer load and battery voltage - applicable at FALE and FAOR ONLY (cl. 4.5.6); UPS operating environment temperature 0 degC to +40 degC and relative humidity 20% to 80% (D118MAN cl. 8.2); battery technology shall be lithium-ion (cl. 8.6); availability 99,5% and N-1 firmness (cl. 4.3.1)

requirement: is there a significant deviation beyond strict limits?
basis: 1. ICAO Annex 10 Vol I, para. 3.1.3 (VHF localizer and associated monitor) and para. 3.1.5 (UHF glide path and associated monitor) — course alignment, displacement sensitivity, clearance and monitor limits by ILS facility performance category 2. ICAO Doc 8071 Vol I, Manual on Testing of Radio Navigation Aids — ground and flight inspection parameters, tolerances and test periodicities for ILS 3. SA Civil Aviation Regulations, 2011 Part 171 (Aeronautical Telecommunication Service Providers) — approval of the service provider and its duty to maintain the facility to the prescribed performance standard 4. Annual Flight Inspection and Calibration Certificate (SA CAA)

acsaConflict: MATERIAL GAP. D060 022M names every parameter to be measured but states NO numeric tolerance or alarm limit for any of them - the only quasi-numeric entries are procedural (battery on load for '+/- 10 minutes', DDM measured 'at the 25 degree point', phasing 'at 90Hz and 150Hz'). A finding of 'significant deviation beyond strict limits' cannot be evidenced against an ACSA figure and must be taken from the OEM manuals (NORMAC 700B / Thales 420) and ICAO Annex 10 Volume I.
basisNote: The Part 171 obligation sits with whichever entity holds the aeronautical telecommunication service approval for the ILS (commonly ATNS rather than the aerodrome licensee) — confirm which entity is approved before framing a finding against ACSA.

basis: SANS 10114 - Interior lighting Part 1: Artificial lighting of interiors SANS 10098-2/ SANS 10389 OHS Act

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires a DAILY visual inspection of high mast and apron lights (verify lights are on, observe any discolouration or flickering, check the integrity of the supporting structure) and a MONTHLY light output measurement as per grid against a stated minimum (D060 024M cl. 4.7.5). Street lights and building/landside obstruction lights are inspected daily including supporting structure integrity (cl. 4.7.4 / 4.7.7); lighting accessories (kiosks, mast brackets and fixtures, control gear, timers, motion sensors, switches, photocells and luminaires) are inspected and repaired six-monthly (cl. 4.7.6). Street lighting and high masts shall be controlled by photocells according to available daylight levels (D100MAN cl. 7.1).
acsaThreshold: Apron / high mast lighting output at least 20 LUX, as per ICAO Annex 14 section 5.3.24, measured MONTHLY, ELEC, outage NOT required (D060 024M cl. 4.7.5); daily visual inspection including supporting structure integrity (cl. 4.7.5); lighting accessories six-monthly (cl. 4.7.6); car park lighting occupancy sensors to increase lighting levels to 100% in human presence and decrease to 40% in human absence (D100MAN cl. 7.1); lighting masts designed per SANS 10225

Certificate of Compliance issued per D060 004M
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit ME 031
acsaConflict: ACSA states the 20 lux minimum but NO uniformity ratio for apron lighting, and perimeter lights are marked N/A at FALE (D060 024M cl. 4.7.8) so their absence at King Shaka is not a non-conformance. No high-mast structural inspection interval beyond the daily visual 'integrity of supporting structure' check, and no lowering-device or winch test interval, is stated.
pfq: Acceptable in Mar 2025.

acsaThreshold: Emergency lights: visual inspection and escape route clearance check DAILY, ELEC, outage NOT required; integrity testing of the back-up supply to emergency lighting (operability, adequacy and light output measurement) SIX MONTHLY (D060 024M cl. 4.7.11)

acsaConflict: ACSA's regime is DAILY plus SIX-MONTHLY, not the monthly-function-test / annual-full-duration regime the checklist assumes - a KSIA maintenance history should be tested against ACSA's own intervals, not the assumed ones. 2. Physically inspect suppression cylinder pressure gauges (should read normal/green) and check the weight-check tag date; check the protected room's door seals and any wall/floor/ceiling penetrations look properly sealed.

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires tri-monthly X-ray machine maintenance that expressly includes performing a RADIATION LEAKAGE SURVEY, calibrating the unit, inspecting safety devices, checking E-Stop buttons, checking the interlock system, checking the wiring of the protective earth and completing diagnosis report 06; and a yearly VERIFICATION OF THE RADIATION EQUIPMENT REGISTRATION WITH THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH, with deregistration of decommissioned or transferred assets (D080 013M cl. 4.4.4). Calibration certificates are named as a statutory requirement at a three-monthly interval (cl. 4.6). A written Safe Work Procedure is required for X-ray equipment and archway metal detectors (S010 003WI cl. 4(a)).
acsaThreshold: X Ray Machine Calibration Certificates: THREE (3) MONTHLY (D080 013M cl. 4.6); radiation leakage survey and full functional maintenance TRI-MONTHLY (3M) (cl. 4.4.4); Department of Health Radiation Equipment registration VERIFIED YEARLY (cl. 4.4.4); Archway Metal Detectors (AMD) are explicitly RUN TO FAILURE with no scheduled maintenance, and only a daily operator piece calibration (cl. 4.4.1 / 4.4.3)

Radiation leakage survey records (tri-monthly)
Department of Health Radiation Equipment registration verification (annual) and deregistration records

acsaConflict: Two gaps. First, D080 013M requires a radiation leakage survey but states NO numeric dose or leakage limit (no microSv/h figure), so pass/fail cannot be judged against an ACSA figure. Second, NO Radiation Protection Officer appointment exists anywhere in ACSA's set - S010 001M's complete list of legislative appointments (s16(2), s8(2)(i), s17(1), s19(3), GMR 2(1), GMR 2(7), First Aider, Fire Warden, Pressure Equipment competent person, incident investigator, emergency co-ordinator, evacuation officer) contains no RPO under the Hazardous Substances Act. Note also that D080 013M is the only 2025-dated procedure in the electrical set and still uses superseded airport names.
pfq: Quarterly PM records for the previous two quarters submitted (calibration confirmed); one sampled machine at international arrivals not in good condition, one at local departures not functional.

acsaConflict: MATERIAL GAP - two parts. First, ACSA states NO numeric earth resistance limit anywhere in the 99 documents, so an earthing test result cannot be judged against an ACSA figure. Second, NO ACSA document in the set contains ANY lightning-protection requirement at all - there is no reference to SANS 62305 or IEC 62305, no lightning protection system test interval, and no bonding requirement for airside structures or fuelling points. The lightning-protection half of this check has no ACSA basis whatsoever and should be raised as a standards gap.

requirement: All employees shall be trained and familiar with electrical safety and circuitry
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993 s.8(2)(e) and s.13 — providing such information, instructions, training and supervision as necessary, and causing every employee to be made conversant with the hazards attached to the work and the plant or machinery used 2. OHS Act 85 of 1993, General Machinery Regulations, 1988 reg 5(1) — no person other than a competent person, or a person trained to the satisfaction of an inspector, may work on or near electrically alive machinery; reg 2 — designation of the competent person to supervise machinery 3. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Electrical Installation Regulations, 2009 reg 9 — a certificate of compliance may only be issued by a registered person; reg 11 — application for registration as a registered person with the chief inspector 4. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Electrical Machinery Regulations, 2011 reg 5 — notices prohibiting unauthorised persons from entering the premises or handling electrical machinery
evidenceExpected:
1. Electrical safety induction/training records for staff working near circuitry.

2. Current DoEL registration certificates for anyone (including contractors) performing fixed-installation electrical work.
target:
1. All employees working near or on electrical circuitry must be informed/trained on relevant electrical hazards proportional to their exposure (OHS Act ss.8(2)(d)/(e), 13).

2. Only DoEL-registered persons may perform work on fixed electrical installations (EIR reg 3).
question:
1. Is training refreshed periodically, or given once at hire only?

2. Is a contractor's DoEL registration actually checked before they start work, or assumed?
walkabout:
1. Ask staff working near electrical circuitry what electrical hazard training they've had and when; cross-check against the training register.

2. Identify anyone on site performing electrical installation work, including contractors, and confirm their DoEL registration certificate is on file and was actually checked.

basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Electrical Installation Regulations, 2009 reg 5 — no person may authorise, design, install or permit the installation of an electrical installation other than in accordance with the incorporated health and safety standard, with a registered person in general control 2. SANS 10142-1 (current edition 3.2, 2024) — the wiring code incorporated as a health and safety standard by GN R.243 of 6 March 2009 under OHS Act s.44 3. Electrical Installation Regulations, 2009 reg 7 and reg 9 — certificate of compliance with an approved test report, issued only by a registered person; reg 2 — the user's or lessor's responsibility for the installation 4. SA Civil Aviation Regulations, 2011 reg 139.02.10A(8) — aerodrome electrical installations and equipment shall comply with the relevant South African National Standards and the OHS Act

requirement: All statutory notices and signs should be clearly displayed
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Electrical Machinery Regulations, 2011 reg 5 — notices displayed within and at all designated entrances to premises housing generating plant and transforming, switching or linking apparatus: prohibition of unauthorised entry and handling, fire procedure, and shock resuscitation directions 2. SANS 1186-1:2015 (Ed. 3.7) Symbolic safety signs Part 1: Standard signs and general requirements — the compulsory form, colour and symbols for danger, prohibition and PPE signage 3. Electrical Machinery Regulations, 2011 reg 6(d) — lighting sufficient for all instruments, labels and notices to be easily read 4. OHS Act 85 of 1993 s.13, read with the General Administrative Regulations, 2003 reg 7 — hazard information to employees and a copy of the Act kept available at the workplace

basis: 1. SA Civil Aviation Regulations, 2011 reg 139.02.23(2)(a) — the licence holder shall keep the aerodrome in a serviceable condition by establishing a maintenance programme 2. ICAO Annex 14 Vol I ch. 8 (Electrical systems: 8.1 power supply for air navigation facilities, 8.3 monitoring) and ch. 10 (Aerodrome maintenance: 10.1 general, 10.5 visual aids) — the maintenance and monitoring standard behind the CAR 4. requirement: Protection against direct contact shall be observed
basis: ORHVS - Operating Regulations of High Voltage System
evidenceExpected: ORHVS-authorised persons register for anyone accessing HV/MV areas.
target:
1. Physical barriers/enclosures: switchgear/transformer premises must be constructed so persons cannot reach in and touch bare conductors or exposed live parts; barriers/enclosures around live LV/MV/HV parts must be intact and correctly rated (EMR reg 6).

2. Controlled access (ORHVS): work on live/electrically-alive machinery is only permitted under strict controlled conditions per GMR reg 5; MV/HV plant staff and procedures should comply with ORHVS, including an authorised-persons register.
walkabout:
1. Physically inspect enclosure panels for any left open or unlocked after maintenance; check the voltage rating marked on each barrier/enclosure against what is actually installed behind it.

2. Cross-check the ORHVS-authorised persons register against current staff records for anyone listed who is no longer employed or authorised.

acsaRequirement: ACSA requires that all conductors are insulated/covered and NOT LYING ON THE FLOOR and that any visible holes allowing unauthorised access are blanked off with a plain rivet or suitable device - both part of the sixteen DAILY substation checks (D060 023M cl. 4.7.4). The annual LV panel inspection covers the front cover and interphase barriers (cl. 4.7.6). Live apparatus shall be barricaded to afford reasonable protection and a person not authorised for a prohibited area shall remain at ground level unless the work area is suitably demarcated by barriers preventing inadvertent contact with live apparatus (D060 013M cl. 4.5.2); truck type switchgear shall be racked out and locked or have shutters/barrier devices in place and locked (cl. 4.6.6). The UPS shall be equipped with back feed protection and an adequate enclosure IP rating (D118MAN cl. 4.3.10 / 4.3.11).

requirement: Isolation and lockout requirements including earthing requirements for machinery that can acquire electrical charge. Check that distribution panels can be isolated and locked out
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Electrical Machinery Regulations, 2011 reg 4 — where machinery liable to acquire or retain a charge is disconnected, precautions by earthing or other means to discharge it before it is handled, and to prevent it being made live while persons work on it 2. OHS Act 85 of 1993, General Machinery Regulations, 1988 reg 5(1) and 5(2) — only a competent person may work on or near electrically alive machinery, and all reasonable precautionary measures must be taken 3. Electrical Machinery Regulations, 2011 reg 18 — earthing of accessible metallic parts that may become live, with the earth continuity path not exceeding 0,2 ohm 4. SANS 10142-1:2024 (isolation and switching of low-voltage installations) and SANS 10142-2 (medium-voltage installations above 1 kV to 22 kV) — isolation, locking and proving-dead requirements for the LV and 11 kV portions

question: Is the LOTO procedure actually followed in practice or bypassed 'for a quick job', and is a multi-lock hasp used when more than one person works on the same circuit?
walkabout: Physically test/observe that distribution panels/switchboards have lockable isolators; check padlocks and permits are actually being issued and used, not just available; check earthing/discharge equipment is present.

requirement: Requirements to safe guard machinery and ensure they are installed, operated and maintained in a manner to prevent exposure to hazards

requirement: Flow and functional test records of smoke extraction fans
basis: 1. SANS 10400-T:2011 cl. 4.42 — smoke control 2. SANS 10400-T:2011 cl. 4.32 — provision and maintenance of fire-fighting equipment, installations and fire protection systems (grease-laden ductwork is the fire load being managed) 4.
