Asset Activity Update Request ME 041
acsaConflict: No ACSA procedure names roof vents or natural smoke/heat ventilators, and none states a functional-test frequency or an opening-time/area criterion for them. The absence of any roof-vent maintenance task in D080 025M is itself an audit finding.
basisNote: No external instrument sets a monthly test interval for roof ventilators — reg O6 requires testing at "acceptable intervals" only, so a missed month is a departure from ACSA's own schedule rather than a contravention.

requirement: Functional Test records of Fire dampers
basis: 1. SANS 193 — fire dampers; the product and performance standard normatively referenced by SANS 10400-T 2. SANS 10400-T:2011 cl. 4.41 — services in structural or separating elements (protection where ducts penetrate fire-separating elements); cl. 4.40 for service shafts 3. SANS 10400-T:2011 cl. 4.32 — provision and maintenance of fire protection systems, "maintained" being defined at cl. 3.57 as a condition of operational readiness in accordance with the original design 4. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Environmental Regulations for Workplaces reg 9 — fire precautions and means of egress
evidenceExpected: Fire damper functional test records — location/reference, date tested, confirmation it closes fully and resets. Cross-referenced to the building's fire safety file or fire engineer's O&M schedule.
target: Monthly
question: Which O&M document / fire safety file actually sets the monthly test frequency for these dampers?
walkabout: Select a sample of dampers from the register, physically locate them (checking access panels aren't sealed/obstructed above ceilings), and visually confirm none are painted over or obstructed such that they couldn't close; cross-check the sample against the full register to confirm no dampers are missing from testing.

acsaDocs.title: Maintenance of Fire Fighting Systems Procedure
Maintenance of HVAC Systems Procedure

acsaRequirement: No ACSA procedure imposes a fire damper drop test. The only related obligations are the three-monthly auxiliary-system activation test by double knock or fire simulation in the fire procedure, and the tri-monthly HVAC task to inspect proper operation of dampers and lubricate on air handling units (these are control dampers, not fire dampers).
acsaThreshold: Auxiliary system activation test "3 Monthly (3M)" — D080 002M cl. 4.7.5. AHU damper inspection and lubrication "Tri-Monthly (3M)" — D080 025M cl. 4.4.5. No fire-damper release, drop-test or reset interval is stated.
acsaEvidence: Fire panel logbook with logging analysis
Record of abnormality or non-responsive auxiliary system (D080 002M cl. 4.7.5)
acsaConflict: D080 025M lists SANS 193:2004 (Fire Dampers) and SANS 1253:2003 (Fire Doors and Fire Shutters) in its referenced standards, and D080 002M also lists SANS 193:2004, yet NEITHER document contains a single fire damper maintenance, drop-test or fusible-link task. A standard is cited that nothing implements — a direct, defensible finding.
basisNote: Neither SANS 193 nor SANS 10400-T states a damper drop-test interval; the monthly frequency comes from the fire engineer's rational design and O&M schedule, which reg A19 obliges the owner to keep a competent person appointed against.

requirement: Certificate of Conformity for Refrigerant gas lines
basis: Pressure equipment regulations (PERs)
evidenceExpected: Current Certificate of Conformity (PER reg 17) for the refrigerant gas line installation, issued by an Approved Inspection Authority/authorised person. Evidence no modification has occurred to the pressure-retaining parts since it was issued.
target: Validity
walkabout: Physically trace the refrigerant gas line installation and check the CoC's plant room/asset references match what's actually installed; look for any visibly recent modification (new sections, welds, added branches) not reflected on the certificate.

acsaDocs.title: Maintenance of HVAC Systems Procedure
Maintenance of Specialised Equipment Procedure

acsaRequirement: D080 025M states plainly that for HVAC systems Statutory Requirements — Calibration Certificates are 'None required'; it imposes no certificate of conformity, pressure test or installation certificate on refrigerant gas lines. The only statutory pressure obligation that reaches refrigerant circuits is the Pressure Equipment group in D080 017M: three-yearly inspection and testing including a pressure test where applicable, with the register updated per the Pressure Equipment Regulations.
acsaThreshold: "Statutory Requirements — Calibration Certificates: None required" — D080 025M cl. 4.8. Pressure Equipment inspection and testing "Three Yearly (3Y)" — D080 017M cl. 4.2.3.
acsaEvidence: Pressure Equipment Regulations register (3-yearly inspection/test) — D080 017M
Load test / pressure test certificates retained 5 years — D080 017M cl. 4.3
acsaConflict: ACSA cites SANS 10147:2009 (Refrigerating Systems) in D080 025M but requires no Certificate of Conformity, pressure test, brazing qualification or leak-tightness certificate for refrigerant pipework — a gap against the Pressure Equipment Regulations, which bring refrigeration pressure piping into scope. The blanket 'None required' at cl. 4.8 conflicts with D080 017M cl. 4.2.3, which does impose a 3-yearly statutory regime on pressure equipment at FALE.

requirement: Legionela test and clearance certificate
basis: SANS10147 Incorporated under PER
evidenceExpected: Most recent dated Legionella clearance certificate (SANS 10147 cl 6.1.6.1) for each water-cooled/evaporative system, issued within the last 12 months. Pass result and sampling details.
target: Yearly
walkabout: Physically locate each cooling tower/evaporative condenser on site and count them against the certificates held — a certificate covering only one tower when the site has several is a fail; check the certificate's sampling point description against the actual system.
acsaConflict: NO ACSA document in the 99-document set mentions Legionella, Legionnaires' disease or cooling-water microbiological testing — not D080 025M (HVAC, which owns the Cooling Tower ACT asset group), not D080 014M (Water Systems), not the environmental T050 series and not the OHS S010 series. ACSA mandates monthly and tri-monthly cooling tower cleaning tasks (D080 025M cl. 4.4.3) but no water treatment programme, no dosing regime, no microbiological sampling and no clearance certificate. This is an unmitigated public-health exposure on an ACSA-owned asset group that is applicable at FALE.

requirement: COC for electrical reticulation in plant rooms
basis: EIRs
evidenceExpected: Certificate of Compliance (EIR reg 6) for the plant room electrical reticulation, issued by a registered person. Confirmation it matches the current as-installed wiring, with no un-certified additions since issue.
target: Validity
walkabout: Walk the plant room and visually compare the wiring/DB layout against what the CoC describes; look for obvious un-certified additions (new circuits, extensions) and check the registered person's details are stated on the CoC, not just an invoice.

acsaDocs.title: Maintenance of Certificate of Compliance Issuance Procedure
Maintenance of Certificate of Compliance Issuance Procedure
Maintenance of Certificate of Compliance Issuance Procedure

acsaRequirement: A Certificate of Compliance is required for new, altered, modified or extended LV electrical installations; it may only be issued by a Registered Person after inspection and testing to SANS 10142-1, must be in the latest SANS 10142-1 format and be accompanied by a test report in the format approved by the Chief Inspector. A yearly inspection must confirm all COCs are accounted for across all asset group circuits, and new COCs must be issued immediately after any new installation or alteration.
acsaThreshold: COC inspection "Yearly (Y)" for Substations (BDG), LV Switchboards (SBD) and Lighting (LGT); ad-hoc issue "IMMEDIATELY after any new installation or alteration" — D060 004M cl. 4.9.1/4.9.2. "the user or lessor may not allow a change of ownership if the Certificate of Compliance is OLDER THAN TWO YEARS" — cl. 4.4(h). "the CALIBRATION CERTIFICATE of the testing tools must be presented for the new issue or re-issue of the COC" — cl. 4.10.10.
acsaEvidence: Certificate of Compliance in the latest SANS 10142-1 format (original to Responsible Person/User, copy to local authority, copy to the Asset Information Officer in Enterprise Asset Management)
SANS 10142-1 test report accompanying every COC
Calibration Certificate — Testing Tools (5 years)
Record of the date of the yearly COC inspection
Register/reconciliation showing all COCs accounted for across all asset group circuits
acsaConflict: D060 004M cl. 4.8.1 marks the Transformers (TRF) asset group as COC-applicable ONLY at FAGG (George), not at FALE — an apparent scope error to challenge, since KSIA plant rooms are transformer-fed.

requirement: Wiring diagrams
basis: 1. SANS 10142-1:2020 cl. 6.6.1.19 — permanent labelling identifying all incoming and outgoing circuits of a distribution board 2. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Electrical Installation Regulations 2009 reg 7 — certificate of compliance and its accompanying test report, which must describe the installation as it stands 3. OHS Act, General Machinery Regulations reg 5 — working on moving or electrically alive machinery; safe isolation depends on circuit records matching the installation 4. ISO 55001:2014 cl. 7.5 and 7.6 — asset information requirements and control of documented information (recommended practice unless contractually imposed)
evidenceExpected: Current as-built wiring/reticulation diagram for the plant room, dated and signed off. Confirmation it matches the physical installation.
target: As built
walkabout: In the plant room, physically trace a sample of circuits/panel labelling against the diagram; check the diagram carries a version/date. A diagram that is only the original design drawing (never updated), or held only centrally and not on site, is a fail.

acsaDocs.title: Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency
CAD and GIS Asset Information Procedure

acsaRequirement: ACSA's energy-efficiency standard requires complete sets of as-built drawings on handover — one electronic and three hard copies of the entire project — including electrical wiring diagrams showing all cable sizes, control units, site cable reticulation and schematic wiring diagrams, with electronic records handed to the site Asset Information Office and laminated, framed copies of circuitry schematics fixed to the wall in a well illuminated and accessible area. W010 001M requires drawings to be issued and received in both PDF and native format, named project number + drawing number + revision number, against a Document Transmittal.
acsaThreshold: "one (1) electronic and three (3) hard copies" of the as-built set — D100MAN cl. 9.2 item 3. Drawings in "pdf AND native formats"; file name = "project number, drawing number and the revision number"; "minimum paper size is A3" — W010 001M cl. 4/4.2.
acsaEvidence: Complete as-built drawing set — 1 electronic + 3 hard copies, handed to the Asset Information Office at site
Laminated and framed circuitry schematics fixed to the plant-room wall
Document Transmittal (project number, description, site, from/to blocks, per-item title, description, rev, date, format)
Design Drawings register (Asset Information Management Department, 5 years)
acsaConflict: W010 001M sets no maximum update lag after an asset change and no drawing-currency test, so 'wiring diagrams exist' cannot be distinguished from 'wiring diagrams are current' under ACSA's own rules. D060 023M cl. 4.7.4 does require corrective action where substation drawings are outdated, but no equivalent exists for HVAC plant rooms.
basisNote: No South African instrument uses the phrase "as-built wiring diagram"; the enforceable hooks are circuit identification under SANS 10142-1, the CoC test report, and the safe-isolation duty.

requirement: HVAC/FIRE Detection interface test records
basis: OHS Act
evidenceExpected: Quarterly interface test record — fire alarm triggered/simulated, HVAC response observed and recorded. Cross-referenced to the fire engineer's cause-and-effect matrix.
target: Quarterly
walkabout: Where a live or simulated test can be reviewed on site, check that the HVAC equipment response was actually exercised (not the fire panel alone), and confirm a cause-and-effect matrix exists covering all interface zones, not just some tested each quarter.

acsaDocs.title: Maintenance of Fire Fighting Systems Procedure

acsaRequirement: Where the fire rational design supports activation of auxiliary systems during a fire condition, ACSA requires auxiliary system activation tests by simulating double knock or fire simulation, with any abnormality or non-responsive auxiliary system recorded. This is the HVAC/fire-detection interface test. It sits alongside weekly global and local fire panel inspection, monthly panel functionality tests and at-least-annual removal, cleaning and testing of all detection sensors per SANS 10139.
acsaThreshold: Auxiliary system activation test (double knock or fire simulation) — "3 Monthly (3M)"; global/local panel inspection "Weekly (W)"; panel functionality test "Monthly (M)"; detection sensors removed, cleaned and tested "At least once a year" — D080 002M cl. 4.7.5.
acsaEvidence: Fire panel logbook (one per panel) with logging analysis
Record of any abnormality or non-responsive auxiliary system
Downloaded fire panel status reports submitted to ACSA
Fire rational design / council-approved designs of existing installations (validated yearly)
acsaConflict: The test is conditional — 'where the fire rational design supports activation of auxiliary systems' — so if the rational design is missing at KSIA the interface is never tested. Neither D080 002M nor D080 025M identifies which HVAC plant must shut down or change state on fire alarm.

requirement: DB Earth leakage
basis: EIRs
evidenceExpected: DB design/as-built drawing stating the specified earth-leakage trip current and time. Latest trip test record confirming the unit trips within that rating.
target: Amperage as per design
walkabout: At the DB, check the installed ELU/RCD's rated current against the design drawing; check for evidence of an actual measured trip test (not just a test-button press), and check the unit hasn't been bypassed for nuisance tripping without reinstatement.

acsaDocs.title: Maintenance of Certificate of Compliance Issuance Procedure
Management of Safe Work Procedures (Working Instruction)

acsaRequirement: Earth leakage testing is required as part of the SANS 10142-1 inspection and testing that must precede issue of any Certificate of Compliance, and the Registered Person shall refuse to issue the certificate until any fault or defect is rectified. S010 003WI separately requires a written, approved Safe Work Procedure for 'testing of earth leakage and polarity', approved by both the GMR 2(1) and the GMR 2(7) appointee.
acsaThreshold: COC inspection cycle "Yearly (Y)" (D060 004M cl. 4.9.1) and immediate re-issue on alteration (cl. 4.9.2). No standalone earth-leakage test interval, no trip-current (mA) and no trip-time (ms) value is stated in any ACSA document.
acsaEvidence: Certificate of Compliance plus SANS 10142-1 test report (which carries the earth leakage test result)
Calibration Certificate — Testing Tools
Written Safe Work Procedure for testing of earth leakage and polarity, approved by the GMR 2(1) and GMR 2(7) appointees
Register of all Safe Work Procedures (OHS Quality Manager)
acsaConflict: ACSA prescribes no periodic earth-leakage push-button test interval for distribution boards, even though SANS 10142-1 expects regular functional testing — the only trigger is COC issue/re-issue. Test whether a GMR 2(7) appointee actually exists at KSIA: without that second signature every Safe Work Procedure at the airport, including the earth-leakage SWP, is technically unapproved (S010 003WI cl. 4).

requirement: Refrigerant leak test records
basis: SANS10147 Incorporated under PER
evidenceExpected: Quarterly refrigerant leak-check records (visual or electronic detection) for each refrigerant circuit. Referenced to the system's refrigerant charge. Any detected leak logged and the repair verified.
target: quarterly
question: What is this system's documented refrigerant charge size/category, which determines the correct SANS 10147 check interval?
walkabout: At the refrigeration/AC plant, check the leak-check method actually used (visual vs electronic detection) is stated in the record; check refrigerant top-up logs for a pattern of repeated top-ups without an investigated cause, which would mask an ongoing leak.

acsaDocs.title: Maintenance of HVAC Systems Procedure
Maintenance of HVAC Systems Procedure

acsaRequirement: Chillers must be checked tri-monthly for oil and refrigerant charge and any refrigerant leaks, together with proper functioning of controls, gauges and the electric panel. Console units (ACU) and split units (ASU) must have gas charge checked and operating pressure RECORDED tri-monthly, and be checked yearly for leaks and abnormal vibration.
acsaThreshold: Chiller refrigerant charge and leak check "Tri-Monthly (3M)" — D080 025M cl. 4.4.1. Console/split unit gas charge check and recorded operating pressure "Tri-Monthly (3M)"; leak check "Yearly (Y)" — cl. 4.4.2/4.4.6. No leak rate (g/yr or % charge), no pressure value and no charge weight is stated.
acsaEvidence: Chiller Unit Heat Pump checklist CMMS 008
Split and Console Units checklist CMMS 018
Recorded operating pressures for console and split units (tri-monthly)
Weekly chiller records of measured temperature, pressures and amps (cl. 4.4.1)
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit ME 031
acsaConflict: ACSA requires a leak CHECK but never a leak TEST to a stated method or acceptance limit, and cl. 4.8 declares no calibration certificates required — so the leak detector used is uncalibrated by ACSA rule. No refrigerant logbook or charge/recovery reconciliation is required despite SANS 60335-2-104:2003 (refrigerant recovery/recycling) being cited.

requirement: Indoor air quality measurements (Airport Environmental dept)
basis: OHS Act
evidenceExpected: Airport Environmental department's most recent indoor air quality measurement report, dated within the two-year cycle. States the reference standard/guideline values it was assessed against.
target: Two - Yearly
question: Which zones/areas does the report actually cover compared to what exists on site today, and was any flagged exceedance actioned?

acsaDocs.title: Occupational Medical Health Procedure
Hearing Conservation (Working Instruction)

acsaRequirement: ACSA has no indoor air quality procedure. The only recurring measurement obligation that could capture it is the Occupational Hygiene Survey, which shall be conducted every two years by an external, accredited Approved Inspection Authority in line with the OHS Act 85 of 1993, facilitated by the OHS department, with all survey reports made available to the clinic for further analysis and used to inform Occupational Risk Exposure Profiles.
acsaThreshold: Occupational Hygiene Survey "every two (2) years" by an external accredited AIA — S010 012M cl. 4.4.1 (and S010 001WI cl. 4.1). Hygiene survey reports retained "FORTY (40) YEARS" — S010 012M cl. 11. No CO2, CO, VOC, particulate, temperature or relative humidity limit is stated anywhere.
acsaEvidence: Occupational Hygiene Survey report by an accredited AIA (2-yearly, retained 40 years)
Health Risk Assessment (reviewed annually, recorded in the ACSA Risk Register)
Occupational Risk Exposure Profile (OREP) per Homogenous Exposure Group
acsaConflict: No ACSA document specifies indoor air quality parameters or limits, and the checklist attributes IAQ to the Airport Environmental department while ACSA's only hygiene-survey obligation sits with OHS/the Occupational Health Clinic — an ownership gap. S010 012M is Version 2 with a Next Revision Date of March 2026 and is therefore OVERDUE at the audit date.

requirement: Energy Optimisation functional audit
basis: Environmental Legislation, Airport cost reduction, company sustainability
evidenceExpected: ACSA's most recent annual energy optimisation / functional audit report for the HVAC plant. Findings and any actioned recommendations.
target: Yearly
walkabout: Where the report cites a specific finding (e.g. a specific AHU or chiller flagged), spot-check that unit's current condition against the finding to confirm it was actually actioned.

acsaDocs.title: Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency
Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency
Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency

acsaRequirement: D100MAN sets commissioning acceptance criteria requiring pre- and post-energy-efficiency verification and an energy savings report for lighting, motion sensors and HVAC (including functional test of CAV and VAV, verification of pumps, chillers, VAV air-handling units and terminals, refrigerant charge and fan airflow). Tenant consumption must comply with SANS 204 table 2, and the BMS must raise an alert when energy consumption falls outside that range, processed as an ENERGY AUDIT JOB CARD via the CMMS.
acsaThreshold: "Availability — 99.5%; System Design life — 20 years" (cl. 4.6.2); "Energy Savings (Retrofits) > 40%" and "Power Factor 0,95" (cl. 8.5); GBCSA "4 STAR Rating as a minimum" (cl. 4); motors "not less than 50% load but not more than 100%" with VSD control (cl. 7.4.2/8.4); energy use models to give consumption "per asset/system/process/area PER HOUR" (cl. 4.6.1); "All additional electrical demand from 1MVA shall incorporate renewable or alternative energy supplying a minimum of 40% of the additional demand" (cl. 7.6 a).
acsaEvidence: Pre- and post-Energy Efficiency reports for retrofitting projects; Energy Savings report (cl. 9.2/9.5)
Energy audit job card raised via the CMMS on BMS out-of-range alert (cl. 7.6)
Design reports with design calculations against the floor plan
Constant Air Volume and Variable Air Volume Usage — ME 085
Illumination Guideline ME 082; Lighting Heat Gains ME 084; Voltage Dips Categorization ME 087
36-month maintenance schedule and as-built pack at handover (cl. 9.2)
acsaConflict: D100MAN governs design, commissioning and handover of NEW and refurbished installations — it does not impose a recurring in-service energy optimisation audit on existing KSIA plant. There is no stated periodicity for an operational energy audit, so the only recurring trigger is a BMS out-of-range alert. The records table lists the master document as 'D060MAN' while the document itself is D100MAN.

requirement: Noise monitoring requirement by an AIA according to SABS 083
basis: Noise Induced Hearing Loss Regulations
evidenceExpected: Current AIA occupational noise assessment report (SANS 10083 methodology), dated within the regulatory cycle. Identifies noise zones and any areas at/above the 85 dB(A) action level.
target: Yearly
walkabout: Walk the plant rooms/noise areas named in the AIA report and check the noise-zone demarcation/signage on site matches what the report identifies; confirm the report covers the full facility, not only some plant rooms.

acsaDocs.title: Hearing Conservation (Working Instruction)
Hearing Conservation (Working Instruction)
Hearing Conservation (Working Instruction)
Occupational Medical Health Procedure

acsaRequirement: An Approved Inspection Authority registered with the Department of Employment and Labour shall conduct an Occupational Hygiene Survey every two years; the hygienist shall conduct a Noise Survey during this process and identify noise zones across the airport. Noise surveys shall be conducted in terms of SANS 10083:2013 to determine the 8-hour rating level, and where noise exceeds 85 dBA a hearing conservation programme shall be carried out and noise shall be reduced at source before hearing protection is relied on.
acsaThreshold: Noise action level "at or above 82 dBA" (8-hour rating, continuous) and "at or above 135 dBC" (peak, impulse); noise-rating limit "at or above 85 dBA" and "at or above 137 dBC" — S010 001WI cl. 3.1. AIA survey "every two (2) years" — cl. 4.1. Customised hearing protection and six-monthly audiograms above "one hundred and five (105) dBA" — cl. 4.4.3/4.5. All noise records retained "FORTY (40) YEARS" — cl. 4.6.
acsaEvidence: Occupational Hygiene Survey / Noise Survey report by an Approved Inspection Authority (2-yearly, per SANS 10083:2013, retained 40 years)
Noise exposure risk assessment and noise exposure monitoring programme records
Noise zone symbolic signage records and hearing protector attenuation data
Baseline audiograms within 30 days of employment; annual (or 6-monthly above 105 dBA) audiograms
Training Attendance Register OHS 017; Task Analysis Worksheet OHS 016
acsaConflict: The checklist row cites 'SABS 083'; ACSA's current designation is SANS 10083:2013 (S010 001WI cl. 4.8) — cite the ACSA/SANS reference, not the withdrawn SABS number. S010 001WI is written to the Noise Exposure Regulations 2024 while S010 012M still cites the older NIHL Regulation — a cross-document currency inconsistency. ACSA names 'air conditioning plant rooms' as an example noise zone (cl. 4.3.2), which puts HVAC plant squarely in scope.

requirement: Chiller/AHU plant logs: set-points, ΔT, alarms cleared; controls in AUTO; refrigerant leak log; PER certificates for pressure equipment.
basis: OHS Act - Pressure Equipment Regulations; SANS 10147; OEM
evidenceExpected: Plant logs; PER certificates
target: Compliant
walkabout:
1. At the plant room/BMS screen, check the controller mode is AUTO, look for any active or unacknowledged alarms, and note the current supply/return temperatures against the delta-T logged.
2. At the chiller, look for visible signs of refrigerant leakage such as oil staining at pipe joints or ice build-up on refrigerant lines, and check gauge pressures look normal.
3. Locate the pressure vessel nameplate on site and check its ID matches the PER certificate, and confirm the certificate's next-due date has not passed.

acsaDocs.title: Maintenance of HVAC Systems Procedure
Maintenance of HVAC Systems Procedure
Maintenance of Specialised Equipment Procedure

acsaRequirement: Chillers must be checked daily for normal operation and abnormalities; temperature, pressures and amps must be MEASURED AND RECORDED weekly; tri-monthly checks cover controls, gauges and electric panel, oil and refrigerant charge, refrigerant leaks and structural looseness; yearly work includes removal of an oil sample for analysis and report, checking the condition of all safety devices AND CALIBRATING IF REQUIRED, an annual winter service and a condenser tube fouling check. AHUs require monthly recording of operating parameters and filter cleaning, with filters changed yearly. Pressure equipment is on a three-yearly statutory inspection and test.
acsaThreshold: Chiller "MEASURE AND RECORD TEMPERATURE, PRESSURES AND AMPS" Weekly (W); tri-monthly controls/charge/leak checks; yearly oil sample analysis, safety device check and calibration, condenser tube fouling — D080 025M cl. 4.4.1. AHU "RECORD OPERATING PARAMETERS; CLEAN FILTERS" Monthly (M), "CHANGE FILTERS" Yearly (Y) — cl. 4.4.5. Pressure Equipment inspection and testing "Three Yearly (3Y)" per the Pressure Equipment Regulations — D080 017M cl. 4.2.3.
acsaEvidence: Chiller Unit Heat Pump checklist CMMS 008
Air Handling Units checklist CMMS 001
Fan Coil Units checklist CMMS 011
Weekly chiller records of measured temperature, pressures and amps
Chiller oil sample analysis and report (annual)
Recorded AHU operating parameters (monthly)
Pressure Equipment Regulations register (3-yearly) — D080 017M
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit ME 031
acsaConflict: ACSA requires values to be RECORDED but states no set-point, no delta-T, no approach temperature and no alarm limit anywhere in D080 025M — the numbers sit in D063MAN, which must be requested. Two drafting defects to raise: the weekly chiller activity in cl. 4.4.1 is missing from the cl. 4.3 frequency table, and the Hot Water System monthly row wrongly reads 'perform yearly maintenance'. Also cl. 4.8 says HVAC calibration certificates are 'None required', which conflicts with the yearly 'calibrate if required' safety-device task in cl. 4.4.1 and with D080 017M cl. 4.2.3.

requirement: Cooling towers/evaporative condensers: water treatment programme, cleaning & disinfection records, Legionella testing.
basis: SANS 893-1/-2; OHS Act
evidenceExpected: Treatment & test records
target: Per SANS 893 schedule
walkabout:
1. At the cooling tower, check dosing pumps and chemical tanks are present, connected and appear to be operating — not empty or disconnected.
2. Physically inspect the cooling tower basin and fill for visible biological growth (slime, algae), scale build-up or debris.

acsaDocs.title: Maintenance of HVAC Systems Procedure

acsaRequirement: Cooling towers (ACT) must be inspected monthly for leaks and valve condition, with eliminators checked clean and secure, fan motor, bearing and drive inspected and the spray system and nozzles inspected; tri-monthly the V-belt is inspected and tensioned or replaced, the sump and its associates are cleaned and dampers are inspected.
acsaThreshold: Cooling tower leak/eliminator/fan/spray inspection "Monthly (M)"; V-belt, sump cleaning and damper inspection "Tri-Monthly (3M)" — D080 025M cl. 4.3/4.4.3.
acsaEvidence: Cooling Towers checklist CMMS 009
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit ME 031
Asset Information Update Request ME 038
Asset Request ME 039
Asset Preventative Maintenance Request ME 040
Asset Activity Update Request ME 041
acsaConflict: D080 025M mandates cleaning but NO water treatment programme, no biocide/dosing regime, no disinfection procedure, no bleed/conductivity control and no Legionella or microbiological testing — the words Legionella and water treatment do not appear in any of the 99 ACSA documents. NFPA 214 (water-cooling towers) is cited in the standards list but nothing implements it. Cooling towers are applicable at FALE, so this is a live exposure.

requirement: Annexure A certificates for Lifts/Elevators
basis: Lifts, escalators and passenger conveyors Regulations, SANS 1545-1
evidenceExpected: Annexure A certificate of test and examination after erection for each lift. Issued at commissioning or after any substantial modification. References SANS 1545-1 (electric) or 1545-2 (hydraulic).
target: A Certificate of test and examination after erection/installation must be issued before a newly installed or substantially modified lift is put into service, confirming it was tested and examined per the relevant SANS 1545 part and complies with the Regulations.
walkabout: At each lift, check the asset/serial number plate against the certificate on file; check for evidence of a substantial modification (e.g. a new controller) since the certificate date that would require a fresh Annexure A.

acsaDocs.title: Maintenance of People Movers Procedure

acsaRequirement: The two-yearly machinery space inspection requires a documentation check confirming that the Annex 1 or original Government certificate of registration and a copy of the Annex A document are present per lift, together with a compliant, signed and up-to-date record book, rope/belt inspection records and certificates, and recorded annual safety gear, governor and buffer tests. Documents are checked in accordance with SANS 50081.
acsaThreshold: Documentation verification "Two Yearly (2Y)"; "Previous records retained for the previous 10 years" — D080 020M cl. 4.6.1 (Machinery Space items 10-16). Elevator monthly maintenance must "CHECK IF RECORDS REQUIRED AS PER SANS 50081 AND THE LIFT, ESCALATOR AND PASSENGER CONVEYOR REGULATIONS ARE IN PLACE" — cl. 4.6.1.
acsaEvidence: Annex 1 or original Government certificate of registration (per lift)
Copy of Annex A document
Current Annex B document
Comprehensive Report (Annexure B) — machine compartment, retained TEN (10) YEARS
Record book / logbook, compliant, signed and up to date
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit M&E 031
pfq: People movers rated Unacceptable (escalators / travelators / lifts).

requirement: Validity of Annexure B certificates for Lifts/Elevators
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Lift, Escalator and Passenger Conveyor Regulations 2010 (GNR 829) reg 6 — comprehensive report required on first use, after modification, after a reportable incident, on change of lift service provider, and thereafter at intervals not exceeding 24 months 2. acsaThreshold: "Statutory Requirements — a) Calibration Certificates: NONE REQUIRED" — D080 029M cl. 4.11. Competency in cl. 4.7.7 is expressed only as personnel being "adequately trained on the use of the operating equipment, tools or any other elements associated with the task".
acsaEvidence: (none required by D080 029M)
Counter-benchmark evidence to demand: competent person appointment under the Construction Regulations and six-monthly/yearly structural inspection reports — D080 028M cl. 4.2.5
acsaConflict: PRIMARY FINDING. D080 029M contains NO structural assessment, NO load test, NO non-destructive testing, NO corrosion grading or acceptance criteria, NO section-loss or coating-condition threshold, NO defined trigger for escalating visible corrosion or cracking to an engineering assessment, and NO requirement for a Professional Engineer, ECSA-registered person or Construction Regulations competent person anywhere in the document — competency is only 'adequately trained' (cl. 4.7.7), and cl. 4.11 says calibration certificates are 'None required'. This is why the March 2025 KSIA finding (PLB corrosion with no Professional Engineer structural assessment) cannot be closed from ACSA's own documentation. The internal counter-benchmarks are D080 028M cl. 4.2.5 (buildings: 3-monthly visual escalating to 6-monthly and yearly structural inspection by a competent person under the Construction Regulations) and D080 017M cl. 4.2.1/4.2.7 (statutory load tests and registers on lifting machines and gondolas at FALE). Note the counter-benchmark itself is weak evidence: D080 028M is Version 2 dated 01 Sep 2022 with a Next Revision Date of September 2025 and is roughly a year overdue.
pfq: Signs of corrosion; no structural assessment reports by Professional Engineers to rule out structural failure.

requirement: A 3 yearly valid On-site Emergency Plan
basis: Major Hazard Installation Regulations
evidenceExpected:
1. Current on-site emergency plan, reviewed/updated in consultation with the local authority within the last 3 years (MHIR reg 6(1)(c)).
2. Records of the annual practical drill of the plan (MHIR reg 6(1)(g)).
target:
1. On-site emergency plan reviewed and, where necessary, updated in consultation with the relevant local authority at least once every three years — matches the checklist's "3 yearly" target exactly.
2. The plan must be tested in practice at least once a year, with records kept — a related but distinct requirement from the 3-yearly review.
question: 2. Do they show the drill was actually run (not just scheduled)?
walkabout:
1. Compare the emergency plan's site layout/emergency contact list against the current physical site — flag any mismatch (renamed buildings, changed access routes, outdated contacts).
2. Ask to see the drill records/photos/attendance sheets from the most recent annual drill and confirm they correspond to an actual exercise, not merely a paper sign-off.

requirement: A 3 yearly and AIA witnessed Piping Pressure test records
basis: PERs
evidenceExpected: AIA-witnessed piping pressure test certificate for the fuel piping, dated within the last 3 years. Test pressure applied, pass result, and the AIA's name/registration.
target: Periodic in-service pressure testing/inspection by or witnessed by an Approved Inspection Authority; a 3-yearly cycle is a common PER in-service inspection interval for piping in this risk category, though the specific PER regulation number and interval basis (which depends on the piping's PER category per SANS 347) were not independently re-verified this session.
question: What is the piping's documented PER category/classification?
walkabout: Check the certificate's AIA signature/stamp is present (not just a contractor's own sign-off), and confirm the tested sections cover the full piping network (tank farm and hydrant lines), not just part of it.

basis: NERSA Licence requirements, API/JIG/EI requirements, PERs

2. Evidence of the fuel system's NERSA licensing status, if applicable.

question: 2. Is this fuel system, or the pipeline supplying it, required to hold a NERSA petroleum pipeline licence — and if so, can you produce evidence of that licensing status?

requirement: ESB Test records
basis: NERSA Licence requirements, OHS Act section 8
evidenceExpected: Functional test record of the ESB (Emergency Shut-off/Shutdown Button, or equivalent emergency isolation system), showing it was activated and confirmed to isolate fuel flow/power. ACSA's own definition of "ESB" referenced on the form.
target: Emergency shut-down/shut-off systems for fuel installations must be periodically function-tested to confirm they isolate fuel flow/power on demand — standard practice under EI/JIG aviation fuel facility standards and the OHS Act general duty.

walkabout: Physically locate the ESB device/button referenced and confirm site staff can identify what system it isolates; where a test can be observed, confirm the record shows the actual valve/pump isolation occurred, not just that the button was pressed.

requirement: Cathodic Protection records
basis: Pipeline Integrity Management, API/EI Requirements by NERSA
evidenceExpected: Pipe-to-soil potential survey records / rectifier check logs for buried fuel piping and tanks. Readings against the -850 mV CSE protection criterion. Interval per the site's cathodic protection maintenance plan.
target: Pipe-to-soil potential readings monitored at intervals set by API RP 651/1632 (commonly annual survey with more frequent rectifier checks, e.g. bimonthly/quarterly) to confirm protection criteria (typically -850 mV CSE) are met — industry best-practice, not SA statute.
walkabout: At the rectifier station(s), check the current reading/log against the required interval; confirm records identify which specific pipe section or tank each reading relates to, and check whether any out-of-range reading has a linked corrective action.

requirement: Buried piping external coating spot inspection records
basis: 1. SANS 10089-1:2008 cl. 5.2.4 — all below-ground pipelines to be protected against corrosion with suitable corrosion-resistant materials, with any cathodic protection system complying with SANS 10121 2. SANS 10089-1:2008 cl. 5.2.6 — recommendation that all buried pipelines be pressure-tested annually throughout their service life 3. SANS 10089-3:2010 cl. 7.5 — buried steel piping to be protected by an anti-corrosion petrolatum wrapping system with a PVC outer wrap and at least 50 % overlaps (cl. 4.3 for cathodic protection) 4. National Environmental Management Act 107 of 1998 s 28 and National Water Act 36 of 1998 s 19 — duty of care to prevent pollution, which is what a failed buried-line coating causes
evidenceExpected: Coating-integrity/holiday-test inspection records for buried piping, taken during excavation works or via close-interval survey.
target: Spot inspections of buried piping external coating (holiday/coating-integrity checks) during excavation or via close-interval survey — an API-standard pipeline-integrity practice, with no specific SA legislated frequency identified.
question: What method was used?
walkabout: Ask whether any excavation has occurred recently that would have allowed visual access to buried piping coating; if none, note that no inspection was possible by this method and check whether a close-interval survey has been done instead.

Given that ACSA maintains cathodic protection at FALE (implying buried steel), the absence of any coating condition requirement is a coherent finding: CP is maintained but the coating it protects is never inspected.
basisNote: Holiday testing and close-interval survey are Energy Institute/JIG and API pipeline-integrity practice — recommended practice, not statutory; no South African instrument sets a coating spot-inspection frequency, so the finding is against the corrosion-protection duty rather than a missed interval.

basis: API/EI Requirements by NERSA, NEMA, NEMRs

requirement: Hydrant pit valve integrity test records
basis: Pipeline Integrity Management, API/EI Requirements by NERSA
evidenceExpected: Hydrant pit valve leak-tightness/integrity test records for each pit valve. Referenced to the site's fuel facility maintenance manual.
target: Hydrant pit valve leak-tightness testing per the site's fuel-facility maintenance manual.
question: Does the record state which test method was used (pressure decay vs visual)?
walkabout: Cross-check the apron's hydrant pit valve array against the test records to confirm every pit valve has been tested, not just some; check whether the maintenance manual referenced actually exists on site and states a required frequency.

acsaEvidence: Statutory pressure test records for the hydrant line (yearly at FALE)
Tightness Control System monthly maintenance records with noted leak rate
Calibration certificate for the Tightness Control System (cl. 4.9.1)
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit ME 031 (5 years)
Annual Fuel Depot audit report (procedures, record keeping, staff training) — cl. 4.8.2
Managing Participant maintenance documents kept at the Fuel Depot
acsaConflict: ACSA requires the leak rate to be NOTED but sets no allowable leak rate, so the record cannot be scored pass/fail from ACSA's documentation. There is also no individual pit-valve integrity test task — the yearly statutory test is on the hydrant LINE, not per pit valve.

basis: OHS Act section 8, Risk Management, Insurance requirements, API/EI/JIG Requirements by NERSA

requirement: Hazardous area classification map for bulk storage sites
basis: SANS10108
evidenceExpected: Current hazardous-area (zone) classification map/drawing for the bulk fuel storage site, per SANS 10108, dated to reflect the current plant configuration.

requirement: DB earth leakage, Wiring diagrams, COC
basis: EIRs
evidenceExpected:
1. Earth-leakage trip test record for the fuel system's DB.
2. As-built wiring diagram for the fuel system's DB.
3. Current CoC for the fuel system's DB.
target:
1. DB earth-leakage protection must trip within its rated current/time; for this fuel-system installation, this is read together with the hazardous-area (Ex) requirements of SANS 10108/10086 given the flammable-atmosphere context.
2. The wiring diagram must be as-built current, reflecting any additions made for hazardous-area equipment.
3. A valid CoC must be held for the fuel system's DB.
question: 1. Does the installed equipment meet the correct Ex-rating for its hazardous-area zone?
walkabout:
1. At the DB, check whether nearby electrical equipment is correctly Ex-rated for the zone it's in, and check the earth-leakage test record shows a measured trip current/time, not just a test-button check.
2. Compare the wiring diagram against the DB's actual internal layout, checking specifically for hazardous-area-related additions not shown on the diagram.
3. Check the CoC's asset reference against the DB in the field.

requirement: Conveyor interlocks, siren and trip test records
basis: OHS Act section 8 and Driven Machinery Regulations
evidenceExpected:
1. Functional test records for conveyor guarding interlocks, showing the conveyor stopped when an interlock tripped.
2. Functional test records for warning sirens, showing the siren sounded before start-up.
target:
1. Conveyor guarding interlocks must stop the conveyor when tripped, per the guarding/safe-operation duties of the Driven Machinery Regulations.
2. Audible warning sirens must sound before conveyor start-up to warn personnel, consistent with the Regulations' guarding/safe-operation duties.
walkabout:
1. At a conveyor, trip (or observe a test of) a guarding interlock and confirm the conveyor physically stops; check for any interlock that appears bypassed or defeated for operational convenience.
2. Observe or review a siren test and confirm the siren is audible over ambient terminal noise before the conveyor begins moving.

acsaRequirement: For the tilt-tray sorter, monthly maintenance requires checking the startup siren and emergency stop operation, wiping and inspecting all sensors and reflectors, and confirming error-free alarm logs, with daily pre-operation, post-start and post-shutdown walk-arounds against the sorter alarm log. Baggage elevators/hoists are checked monthly for operation of all safeties and interlocks, receive a six-monthly safety inspection by an independent and qualified hoist/elevator inspector and an annual load test with certificate issued by an independent and qualified person. Faults not rectified within 5 minutes must be escalated, and preventative maintenance must be scheduled at least 30 days in advance.
acsaThreshold: Startup siren and emergency stop test "Monthly (M)"; sorter alarm-log walk-arounds "Daily (D)" — D060 002M cl. 4.8.7. Baggage elevator safeties and interlocks "Monthly (M)"; independent safety inspection "Six Monthly (6M)"; load test and certificate "Yearly (Y)" — cl. 4.8.9. Fault escalation "if the responding person cannot rectify the fault within 5 minutes" — cl. 4.2. PM "scheduled at least thirty (30) days in advance" — cl. 4.1. Scale spot check with a "certified 20 kg weight" Daily; SANAS verification Yearly — cl. 4.8.12.
acsaEvidence: Inspection Sheet — Baggage Conveyor CMMS 005
Inspection Sheet — Carousel CMMS 006
Audit Sheet — Check in Conveyor CMMS 007
Six-monthly independent hoist/elevator safety inspection report
Annual load test record and certificate by an independent and qualified person

Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit ME 031
Job cards / check sheets and the monthly report of all preventative maintenance work
acsaConflict: D060 002M still cites the Trade Metrology Act of 1973, which was repealed and superseded in South Africa by the Legal Metrology Act No. 9 of 2014 — the procedure's statutory basis for scale verification is out of date. Separately, ACSA sets no pull-cord/lanyard emergency-stop test interval for belt conveyors (only the sorter siren and e-stop are on a monthly cycle) and no interlock test acceptance criterion. Work-order timeliness for any resulting defect is governed by D060 016M cl. 4.2.1 (execution within 14 days or 7 days of issuance), whose own next revision date of 31 August 2026 falls two weeks before this audit.

requirement: Conveyor Nip points Inspections
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, General Machinery Regulations reg 3 — every exposed and dangerous part of machinery within the normal reach of a person to be effectively safeguarded by insulation, fencing, screening or guarding, and machinery to be installed, operated and maintained so as to prevent exposure to hazardous conditions 2. OHS Act, Driven Machinery Regulations 2015 reg 3 — every pulley, wheel, drum, sprocket, coupling and every driving belt, rope or chain to be securely fenced or guarded 3. OHS Act 85 of 1993 s 8 — general duty to provide and maintain plant and systems of work that are safe and without risks to health 4. ISO 14120 (guards) and ISO 13857 (safety distances) — international good practice for guard design and reach distances; not statutory in South Africa
evidenceExpected: Nip-point guard inspection records confirming all identified nip points remain guarded/interlocked and undamaged.
target: Nip points on conveyors (belt-to-roller/pulley) must be guarded (fixed or interlocked); guards inspected periodically to confirm they remain fitted, undamaged, and interlocks intact — no separate numeric SANS clause identified beyond this general guarding duty.
walkabout: Walk the conveyor lines and visually check nip points for guards fitted and intact; check for any guard propped open or missing after maintenance access, and check whether an interlock switch on a guard appears defeated/bridged out.

acsaRequirement: D060 002M requires belt conveyors (CVB) to be checked MONTHLY with drive safety covers confirmed in position, and TRI-MONTHLY the under-guarding is removed, cleaned and reinstalled (cl. 4.8.3); the tilt-tray sorter (CVS) has a DAILY pre-operations walk-around confirming all bottom covers are in position and nets functional (cl. 4.8.7). S010 003WI cl. 4(a) requires ACSA to hold a written Safe Work Procedure for 'machine guarding', approved by both the GMR 2(1) and GMR 2(7) appointees.
acsaThreshold: Conveyor drive safety covers checked in position monthly; under-guarding removed, cleaned and reinstalled tri-monthly (D060 002M cl. 4.8.3); sorter bottom covers and nets confirmed daily before operations (D060 002M cl. 4.8.7)
acsaEvidence: Inspection Sheet - Baggage Conveyor - CMMS 005
Inspection Sheet - Carousel - CMMS 006
Audit Sheet - Check in Conveyor - CMMS 007
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit - ME 031
Machine guarding Safe Work Procedure (S010 003WI cl. 4(a)), approved by GMR 2(1) and GMR 2(7) appointees
acsaConflict: D060 002M nowhere uses the term 'nip point' and sets no guard-gap, reach-distance or guard-integrity criterion despite citing the General Machinery Regulations GN R1521 and Driven Machinery Regulations GN R1010. Guarding is evidenced only as a tick on CMMS 005/006/007; the substantive nip-point standard sits outside ACSA's procedure.
basisNote: Neither GMR 3 nor DMR 3 sets an inspection frequency — the duty is continuous, so a guard found missing, propped open or with a defeated interlock is itself the contravention regardless of when it was last inspected.

requirement: Carousel siren test records
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, General Machinery Regulations reg 6(3)(b) — machinery operated by more than one person to be provided with an audible warning device to be sounded before the machinery is set in motion 2. OHS Act, General Machinery Regulations reg 3 — safeguarding of machinery; machinery to be operated and maintained so as to prevent exposure of persons to hazardous conditions 3. EN 619 — continuous handling equipment and systems: safety requirements for equipment for the mechanical handling of unit loads, including start-up warning and safeguarding of baggage conveyors and carousels 4. ISO 12100 — safety of machinery: general principles for design and risk assessment (recommended practice, not statutory)
evidenceExpected: Carousel start-up warning siren functional test record confirming the siren sounds for the required period before the carousel begins moving.
target: Carousel start-up warning siren sounds for a required period before automatic machine motion begins; test frequency is operational/maintenance, not a fixed statutory interval.
walkabout: Observe (or review evidence of) a carousel start and confirm the siren is audible over terminal noise and sounds with an adequate margin before the carousel actually moves, not merely that it sounds at some point.

acsaDocs.title: Maintenance of Baggage Handling Systems Procedure
Maintenance of Baggage Handling Systems Procedure

acsaRequirement: D060 002M cl. 4.8.4 sets only MONTHLY carousel (CVC) tasks - noise/oil-leak check, slats and cladding damage and safety, cleaning - with OEM-specific work 'as required by OEM'. A start-up siren test is required MONTHLY, but only for the tilt-tray sorter (CVS) at cl. 4.8.7, not for carousels.
acsaEvidence: Inspection Sheet - Carousel - CMMS 006
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit - ME 031
acsaConflict: ACSA's own procedure has an asymmetry: a monthly start-up siren test is mandated for the sorter (cl. 4.8.7) but no siren test at all is listed for carousels (cl. 4.8.4), even though carousels present the same start-up crush risk. Carousel siren testing at KSIA is therefore governed only by the undefined 'as required by OEM' catch-all - raise with ACSA.
basisNote: GMR 6(3)(b) makes the warning device itself compulsory, but no instrument sets a test interval — the frequency and the required lead time before motion remain ACSA's own operational choice.

requirement: Localised Conveyor and carousel E-stop test records
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, General Machinery Regulations reg 6(3)(a) — machinery operated by more than one person to be provided at every operation point with a stopping device which locks out when used and requires manual resetting 2. OHS Act, General Machinery Regulations reg 6(1) — starting and stopping devices to be positioned where they can readily and conveniently be reached and so constructed and arranged as to prevent accidental starting 3. ISO 13850 — safety of machinery, emergency stop function: principles for design, including that resetting the device must not by itself restart the machinery 4. EN 619 — continuous handling equipment and systems: safety requirements for equipment for the mechanical handling of unit loads
evidenceExpected: E-stop functional test records for each conveyor/carousel, confirming immediate halt and deliberate manual reset.
target: Localised E-stop pull-cords/buttons must immediately halt the machine and require deliberate manual reset.
walkabout: Walk the conveyor/carousel line, physically test (or observe a test of) a sample of E-stop buttons/pull-cords, confirm immediate halt with no auto-restart, and check for any E-stop that is physically damaged or obstructed.

acsaRequirement: D060 002M cl. 4.8.7 requires MONTHLY testing of emergency stop operation on the tilt-tray sorter (CVS), and cl. 4.8.9 requires MONTHLY checking of the operation of all safeties and interlocks on baggage elevators/hoists (ELB). No E-stop test is listed for belt conveyors (cl. 4.8.3), roller conveyors (cl. 4.8.6), deflectors (cl. 4.8.5) or carousels (cl. 4.8.4).
acsaThreshold: Emergency stop operation tested monthly on the tilt-tray sorter (D060 002M cl. 4.8.7); all safeties and interlocks checked monthly on baggage elevators/hoists (D060 002M cl. 4.8.9)
acsaEvidence: Inspection Sheet - Baggage Conveyor - CMMS 005
Inspection Sheet - Carousel - CMMS 006
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit - ME 031
acsaConflict: ACSA mandates monthly E-stop testing only on the sorter and the baggage hoist. Localised conveyor and carousel E-stops - the great majority of E-stops in a BHS - have no test interval anywhere in D060 002M, so a complete localised E-stop test record set cannot be demanded under ACSA's own procedure.
basisNote: GMR 6(3)(a) is the statutory basis for both the immediate halt and the manual-reset requirement; the monthly test interval, and its extension to belt conveyors and carousels, is ACSA's own.

requirement: Carousel roller shutter doors , fire detection and carousel interlock test records
basis: 1. SANS 10400-T:2020 cl. 4.10.4 — every fire door and fire shutter to be fitted with a self-closing or automatic closing device in accordance with SANS 1253 2. SANS 10400-T:2020 cl. 4.31 — fire detection and alarm systems to be designed, installed and serviced in accordance with SANS 10139, which governs the cause-and-effect logic and ancillary outputs that drive the shutter 3. SANS 1253 — fire-doors and fire-shutters, including hold-open devices released on actuation of the detection system 4. OHS Act 85 of 1993, General Machinery Regulations reg 3 — machinery to be installed, operated and maintained so as to prevent exposure of persons to hazardous conditions (shutter closing onto a moving carousel)
evidenceExpected:
1. Test record showing the carousel roller shutter door closes automatically on fire alarm activation, cross-referenced to the fire engineer's cause-and-effect matrix.
2. Test record showing the roller shutter door correctly interlocks with the carousel drive.
target:
1. A roller shutter door forming part of a fire compartment must close automatically on fire-detection activation.
2. The roller shutter must interlock correctly with the carousel/conveyor drive to prevent entrapment or fire spread — i.e. it must not close onto a moving belt.
walkabout:
1. Where a test can be observed, confirm the shutter is actually triggered via the fire alarm system, not manually operated and recorded as if alarm-triggered; check a cause-and-effect matrix exists on site to confirm the correct response is defined.
2. Observe or review evidence of the shutter-to-drive interlock test, checking specifically that the closing sequence is verified against a moving carousel, not just a stationary one.

Maintenance of Sliding and Roller Shutter Doors Procedure

acsaRequirement: D060 002M cl. 4.8.8 requires MONTHLY maintenance of BHS roller shutter doors (DRS): noise/oil-leak check, damage check, cleaning, draft curtains in good condition, operator controls and correct opening/closing limits. D080 007M cl. 4.4.4 separately requires MONTHLY maintenance of motorised roller shutter doors (guides, barrels, gearbox and motor, seats) recorded on Roller Shutter Door checklist CMMS 017. Fire detection is inspected WEEKLY and the global and local panels functionality-tested MONTHLY under D080 002M cl. 4.7.5, with auxiliary system activation tests by double-knock/fire simulation every 3 MONTHS.
acsaThreshold: Roller shutter door maintenance monthly incl. correct opening/closing limits (D060 002M cl. 4.8.8; D080 007M cl. 4.4.4); fire detection inspection weekly, panel functionality test monthly, auxiliary system activation (double knock) test 3-monthly (D080 002M cl. 4.7.5)
acsaEvidence: Inspection of Roller Shutter Door - CMMS 017
Inspection Sheet - Carousel - CMMS 006
Fire panel logbook (one per panel) with logging analysis
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit - ME 031
acsaConflict: No ACSA document requires an integrated test of the roller-shutter / fire-detection / carousel interlock as one interlocked chain. The 3-monthly 'auxiliary system activation test' in D080 002M cl. 4.7.5 is the only clause that comes close, and it applies only 'where the fire rational design supports activation of auxiliary systems' - so the KSIA rational design must be obtained to know whether the test is owed at all.
basisNote: SANS 10400-T is the deemed-to-satisfy route for National Building Regulation T1; the shutter-to-drive interlock itself is not separately standardised in SANS, so GMR 3 is the statutory hook.

requirement: Sorter/Conveyor Interlock test records
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, General Machinery Regulations reg 3 — safeguarding of machinery: machinery to be suitable, installed, operated and maintained so as to prevent exposure of persons to hazardous conditions 2. General Machinery Regulations reg 6(3)(a) — machinery operated by more than one person to have stopping devices at each operating point that lock on operation and require manual resetting before restart 3. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Driven Machinery Regulations 2015 reg 3 — revolving machinery: shafts, pulleys, sprockets, couplings, driving belts and chains to be securely fenced or guarded 4. EN 619 (continuous handling equipment and systems — safety requirements for mechanical handling of unit loads) and ISO 14119 (interlocking devices associated with guards) — international design standards for the sortation plant; no test interval prescribed
evidenceExpected: Interlock test records across the sortation system's conveyors, showing each interlock zone tested for guarding/safety-interlock integrity.
target: Sorter/conveyor interlocks must be periodically tested to confirm guarding/safety-interlock integrity across the sortation system; specific interval not fixed in statute.
walkabout: Walk the sortation system and check whether interlock zones are being bypassed to maintain throughput during peak periods; confirm test records cover all interlock zones across the system, not a partial sample.

acsaRequirement: D060 002M cl. 4.8.9 requires MONTHLY checking of the operation of all safeties and interlocks on baggage elevators/hoists. For the sorter, cl. 4.8.7 requires a DAILY alarm-log review (before operations, immediately after start and after shutdown, scrolling the day's alarm history) and MONTHLY confirmation that sorter servers and high-level control hardware are operational with error-free alarm logs.
acsaThreshold: All safeties and interlocks checked monthly on baggage elevators/hoists (D060 002M cl. 4.8.9); sorter alarm log reviewed daily and high-level control confirmed error-free monthly (D060 002M cl. 4.8.7)
acsaEvidence: Inspection Sheet - Baggage Conveyor - CMMS 005
Audit Sheet - Check in Conveyor - CMMS 007
Sorter daily alarm history / alarm log records
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit - ME 031
acsaConflict: ACSA names interlock testing only for baggage elevators/hoists. Sorter-to-conveyor interlocks are covered indirectly through daily alarm-log review, not by a positive functional interlock test, so no discrete sorter/conveyor interlock test record is required by D060 002M.
basisNote: No statute fixes a test interval, so a finding on interval is procedural against ACSA's own D060 002M, while a bypassed or defeated interlock is a direct GMR 3 and GMR 6 contravention.

requirement: Sorter siren test records
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, General Machinery Regulations reg 6(3)(b) — where machinery is operated by more than one person, an audible warning device to be sounded before the machinery is set in motion 2. General Machinery Regulations reg 6(3)(a) — stopping devices at each operating point that lock on operation and require manual resetting 3. General Machinery Regulations reg 3 — safeguarding of machinery: safe installation, operation and maintenance 4. EN 619 — continuous handling equipment and systems, safety requirements for equipment for mechanical handling of unit loads (international design standard for the sortation plant, cited at document level)
evidenceExpected: Sorter warning siren functional test record confirming the siren sounds for the required period before the sorter begins moving.
target: Sorter warning siren sounds for a required period before the sorter begins moving.
walkabout: Observe (or review evidence of) a sorter start and confirm the siren is audible over ambient noise and precedes motion by an adequate margin.

acsaRequirement: D060 002M cl. 4.8.7 requires, as part of MONTHLY sorter (CVS) maintenance, a check of the start-up siren together with emergency stop operation, sensor/reflector cleaning and inspection, and confirmation of error-free alarm logs.
acsaThreshold: Sorter start-up siren checked monthly (D060 002M cl. 4.8.7)
acsaEvidence: Inspection Sheet - Baggage Conveyor - CMMS 005

requirement: DB Earth leakage test records, Inspection records of Electrical/Control wiring diagrams
basis: EIRs, Risk Management Framework
evidenceExpected:
1. Earth-leakage trip test record for the BHS control system's DB(s).
2. Current CoC and as-built wiring diagrams for the BHS control system's DB(s).
target:
1. The BHS control system DB's earth-leakage protection must be tested and confirmed to trip correctly.
2. Current CoC and as-built wiring diagrams held for the BHS control system, reflecting the current panel configuration — significant given these panels are frequently reconfigured as the system changes.
walkabout:
1. At the BHS control DB, check for evidence of a measured trip test and confirm the panel hasn't been reconfigured since the last test without a re-test.
2. At the BHS control panels, spot-check the wiring against the diagram given these panels are frequently reconfigured; check the CoC date against any recent control panel upgrade.

acsaRequirement: D060 002M cl. 4.8.10 requires MONTHLY electrical panel (PNL) maintenance including checking earth bonding, connector fastening, wire discolouring, panel wiring neatness and that the required documentation is in the panel (outage required). Cl. 4.10 makes a Certificate of Compliance for electrical installations a statutory requirement. D060 004M cl. 4.9.1 requires a YEARLY inspection confirming all COCs are accounted for in all asset-group circuits, with new COCs raised for any unaccounted circuit, and cl. 4.10.10 requires the testing tools' calibration certificate at every COC issue or re-issue. S010 003WI cl. 4(b) requires a written Safe Work Procedure for 'testing of earth leakage and polarity'.
acsaThreshold: Electrical panel earth bonding and in-panel documentation checked monthly (D060 002M cl. 4.8.10); COC reconciliation across all asset-group circuits yearly (D060 004M cl. 4.9.1); testing-tool calibration certificate produced at every COC issue/re-issue (D060 004M cl. 4.10.10)
acsaEvidence: Certificate of Compliance in the latest SANS 10142-1 format plus accompanying test report
Calibration Certificate - Testing Tools
Inspection Sheet - Baggage Conveyor - CMMS 005
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit - ME 031
Earth leakage and polarity testing Safe Work Procedure (S010 003WI cl. 4(b))
acsaConflict: No ACSA document sets an earth-leakage test interval or a trip-current/trip-time acceptance value anywhere. D060 002M requires only an 'earth bonding' check monthly; earth leakage testing appears solely as a SANS 10142-1 activity within COC issue (event-driven) and as a required Safe Work Procedure topic. The register row's 'no specific numeric threshold' therefore remains genuinely open and should be raised as an ACSA gap.

requirement: Guarding, emergency stops, lock-out procedure, conveyor PM completion rate, spares for critical drives.
basis: OHS Act - GMR & Driven Machinery Regs; OEM
evidenceExpected: CMMS PM reports
walkabout:
1. Walk the BHS and visually check guards are fitted over all moving parts, drive units and pinch points, and that none are missing, propped open or bypassed.
2. Locate E-stop buttons/cords along the conveyor route and check they're accessible, undamaged and clearly marked; ask for a safe demonstration/test if operationally possible.
3. Ask a technician to describe or demonstrate the lock-out steps they'd follow before clearing a jam or working on a conveyor.
5. Ask to see the spares store/shelf for critical drive spares and check stock is physically present, not just listed on paper.

acsaRequirement: D060 002M requires guarding checks monthly and tri-monthly (cl. 4.8.3), monthly E-stop testing on the sorter (cl. 4.8.7), all routine preventative maintenance scheduled AT LEAST 30 DAYS in advance and communicated to Baggage Operations (cl. 4.1), and administrative catch-up on any deviation within AT MOST ONE WORKDAY (cl. 4). S010 003WI requires approved Safe Work Procedures for machine guarding and for electrical isolation notice - lock out. D090 001M cl. 4.4.6 b) fixes the critical-spares minimum: minimum quantity = annual usage divided by twelve (12) months to give monthly average usage, then one month's average usage over the LEAD TIME PERIOD.
acsaThreshold: PM scheduled at least thirty (30) days in advance (D060 002M cl. 4.1); deviation admin completed at most one (1) workday after the work (D060 002M cl. 4); minimum spares quantity = annual usage / 12 months applied over the lead time period (D090 001M cl. 4.4.6 b); monthly review of quantity-on-hand against minimum via Inventory Count Sheet INV 009 (D090 001M cl. 4.4.6 c)
acsaEvidence: Inspection Sheet - Baggage Conveyor - CMMS 005
Inspection Sheet - Carousel - CMMS 006
Audit Sheet - Check in Conveyor - CMMS 007
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit - ME 031
KARDEX Card - INV 001 (with lead time and minimum quantity fields)
Inventory Count Sheet - INV 009 (monthly)
Inventory Purchase Request Form - INV 002
Machine guarding and lock-out Safe Work Procedures (S010 003WI)
acsaConflict: ACSA sets no PM completion-rate target anywhere - D060 002M fixes only scheduling lead time (30 days) and administrative catch-up (1 workday), not a percentage completion KPI. Any PM completion-rate threshold used in the audit must come from the NEC service contract, not from ACSA's procedure.

requirement: Extinguisher pressure test records
basis: Building regulations, SANS1475, OHS Act section 8, Insurance Inspections
evidenceExpected: Extinguisher's hydrostatic pressure-test date stamp/tag (SANS 1475-1 interval for the extinguisher type).
target: Periodic hydrostatic pressure testing of the cylinder at the interval fixed by SANS 1475-1 for the extinguisher type (water/foam/dry powder ~5-yearly; CO2 cylinders on a different, typically longer, interval per SANS/SABS pressure-vessel rules), in addition to the annual service.
walkabout: Physically check the pressure-test date stamp on each extinguisher's tag/cylinder, confirming it's legible and current; specifically check CO2 cylinders are checked against their own (not the water/foam) interval table.

Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit - ME 031

The hydrostatic interval for portables must be confirmed against SANS 1475 with ACSA.

requirement: Extinguisher Inspection records
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Environmental Regulations for Workplaces 1987 reg 9 — fire precautions and means of egress: fire-fighting equipment to be provided, maintained in good working order and readily accessible 2. SANS 10400-T:2020 cl. 4.37 — portable fire extinguishers to be provided, installed and maintained in accordance with SANS 10105-1 3. SANS 10105-1:2021 — the use and control of fire-fighting equipment: routine inspection and annual servicing of portable and mobile fire extinguishers 4. SANS 1475-1:2010 — production of reconditioned fire-fighting equipment, portable and wheeled rechargeable extinguishers (the longer-interval pressure test referred to in the adjacent check)
evidenceExpected: Monthly visual inspection log (accessibility, gauge in green zone, seal/pin intact, no damage). Annual service certificate from a SANS 10105-1 registered service agent.
target: Monthly visual inspection (accessibility, pressure gauge in green zone, seal/pin intact, no physical damage) and a full annual service by a certified/SABS-approved service agent, distinct from the longer-interval SANS 1475-1 pressure test in row 64.
walkabout: Physically inspect the extinguisher: confirm it's in its logged location, accessible, pressure gauge needle in the green zone, seal/pin intact, and no visible damage; check the monthly log for gaps.

A monthly-tag non-conformance at KSIA cannot be raised against ACSA's own procedure - only against SANS 1475 / municipal by-law. Raise the ACSA-vs-industry divergence explicitly.
basisNote: The monthly visual inspection and annual service by an accredited agent derive from SANS 10105-1 and municipal fire by-laws rather than directly from the OHS Act; ACSA's quarterly inspection interval is longer than the SANS routine-inspection expectation.

requirement: Annual service by SANS 1475-accredited provider; hydrostatic test dates; monthly inspection tags; correct type/location.
basis: SANS 1475; SANS 10105; SANS 10400-T
evidenceExpected: Service tags; register
target: 100% current

2. Locate the level sensors/float switches in the wet well and check they're correctly positioned, clean and undamaged; check the telemetry panel shows a live, working connection.
3. Look around the pump station and surrounding ground for evidence of past overflow (staining, odour, distressed vegetation) that isn't accounted for in the spill register.
4. Locate the standby generator/power source for the station and check it's present, fuelled (if diesel) and shows evidence of recent testing.

Regulations for Hazardous Biological Agents, 2022 reg 15 — written decontamination procedures, infectious waste handling procedures and disinfection of fixtures and machinery that come into contact with HBA waste 3. National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 s 26 — prohibition of unauthorised disposal; s 16 — general duty of a holder of waste; s 20 — waste management licence for listed activities 4. Waste Classification and Management Regulations, 2013 (GN R634) reg 11 — waste manifest system for hazardous waste; reg 10 — records of waste generation and management kept for five years

question: Is that site confirmed as officially designated?
walkabout: At the treatment plant, check for evidence that decontamination/disinfection is actually being carried out on equipment in contact with HBA waste (not just documented as a procedure), and check manifests exist for every disposal run.

Regulations for Hazardous Biological Agents, 2022 reg 11 — personal protective equipment and facilities: PPE where exposure cannot otherwise be controlled, kept in hygienic and efficient condition, plus washing facilities and separate clean and contaminated change rooms 3. Regulations for Hazardous Biological Agents, 2022 reg 6 — risk assessment for HBAs, and reg 4 — information, instruction and training 4. OHS Act 85 of 1993 s 8(2)(b) and (d) — safe plant and systems of work and the elimination or mitigation of hazards before reliance on PPE; General Safety Regulations reg 2 — personal safety equipment and facilities

The only PRIOR-TO-USE obligation in ACSA's set is S010 003WI, which requires the relevant Maintenance & Engineering Manager to ensure the operator fully understands the written Safe Work Procedure PRIOR TO USE, recorded on Training Attendance Register OHS 017, with the SWP conspicuously displayed at stationary machinery and filed in the supervisor's office for mobile machinery.
acsaThreshold: Ladders inspected monthly and Ladder Register ME 065 updated; fall arrest systems inspected monthly; portable electric equipment inspected monthly on CMMS 019; gondola minor maintenance and inspections tri-monthly (D080 017M cl. 4.2.4, 4.2.5, 4.2.6, 4.2.7)

acsaConflict: ACSA HAS NO PRE-USE USER CHECKLIST for facade access equipment. D080 017M's shortest interval for gondolas is tri-monthly; the monthly ladder and fall-arrest inspections are the nearest analogues. The only 'prior to use' duty (S010 003WI) is that the operator understands the Safe Work Procedure, not that a checklist is completed before each use. This check cannot be evidenced from ACSA's documents.

This is a pointed inconsistency in ACSA's own governance: D118MAN cl. 4.2 and D119MAN cl. 3.2 expressly require an ECSA-registered professional electrical engineer or technologist to sign off UPS and power transformer design, testing and commissioning, but no equivalent professional-registration requirement exists anywhere for lifting machinery inspection - the highest-consequence statutory inspection at the facade of a terminal building. requirement: The surface is maintained in such a condition such as to prevent formation of harmful irregularities
evidenceExpected:
- Latest pavement condition survey report (Pavement Condition Index (PCI)/visual condition survey) for the runway
- Weekly/annual inspection records (TGM §8.5–§8.7) noting any surface irregularity findings and remedial work orders raised
target: (CATS 139.02.22(2)(P); TGM §6.2.1) The runway surface must be kept free of ruts, depressions, humps or other variations that could hazard aircraft, degrade friction/drainage, or cause handling/structural problems. 'Harmful irregularity' is a functional (hazard-based) test, not a fixed numeric limit — severity is graded via engineering assessment (see KSIA-CIV-016).
walkabout: Walk/drive the runway (especially the touchdown zone and high-turn areas) looking, and where available using a straightedge, for ruts/depressions/humps; cross-check against the latest pavement condition survey and inspection records for any noted-but-unremediated irregularities. Pass = no hazardous irregularity found, or all findings have linked work orders showing remediation; fail = visually hazardous irregularity present with no corrective action on file.

requirement: Pavement Bearing Strength
basis: 1. ICAO Annex 14 Vol I §2.6 — strength of pavements: bearing strength of a pavement intended for aircraft above 5 700 kg to be made available using the ACR-PCR method 2. ICAO Doc 9157 Aerodrome Design Manual Part 3 (Pavements) — determination and reporting of PCR, and of aircraft ACR 3. SACAA Civil Aviation Regulations 2011, Part 139 reg 139.02.21 — notification of aerodrome data and information (publication of the rating) 4. SACAA Technical Guidance Material: Calculation of Pavement Bearing Strength — the calculation authority D060 014M itself defers to
evidenceExpected:
- Most recent published PCR report/certificate for the runway (in the 5-part coded format)
- Traffic mix data (aircraft types and annual movements) used to confirm no aircraft's ACR exceeds the published PCR
target: A Pavement Classification Rating (PCR) must be reported for each runway at least annually, in the 5-part coded format (PCR value / pavement type R or F / subgrade category A–D / allowable tyre pressure category W/X/Y/Z / determination method U or T), e.g. 'PCR 680/F/C/X/U'. Every aircraft type regularly using the pavement (≥250 annual departures for the 'Using Aircraft' method) must have an Aircraft Classification Rating (ACR) not exceeding the published PCR; if ACR > PCR, an operating restriction/pavement concession is required.
walkabout: Observe the aircraft types/mix actually operating on the runway and cross-check against the ACR figures in the PCR report to confirm no aircraft type exceeds the published rating.

Asset Information Update Request Form — ME 038

No ACSA document publishes or governs a PCN.
basisNote: ACR-PCR replaced the ACN-PCN method with effect from 28 November 2024, so a register or AIP entry still expressed as a PCN is out of date.

requirement: Provision of RESA at runway ends
basis: 1. ICAO Annex 14 Vol I §3.5 — runway end safety areas: when a RESA must be provided, minimum and recommended length, width, surface characteristics and ability to support rescue and firefighting vehicles 2. ICAO Doc 9157 Aerodrome Design Manual Part 1 (Runways) — RESA design and grading guidance 3. SACAA Civil Aviation Regulations 2011, Part 139 reg 139.02.10A — aerodrome physical characteristics as prescribed in Document SA-CATS 139
evidenceExpected:
- Runway's declared distances/RESA calculation report (per the SACAA TGM methodology)
- Aerodrome layout drawing showing actual RESA length and width provided at each runway end
- Recent survey or inspection confirming no encroachment
target: A Runway End Safety Area (RESA) must be provided at each end of a runway strip where the code number is 3 or 4, and at each end of an instrument runway strip where the code number is 1 or 2. Minimum (Standard) length = 90 m beyond the runway strip end. Recommended length = 240 m for code 3/4 runways and 120 m for code 1/2 instrument runways, wherever practicable. Width must, wherever practicable, be at least twice the runway width and equal to the width of the graded portion of the runway strip. The RESA surface need not be graded to strip standard but must enhance aircraft deceleration in an overrun/undershoot and support rescue and firefighting vehicles.
walkabout: Walk or drive out each RESA and, where a survey/design drawing is available, compare its actual length/width against the required figures; check visually for encroaching objects, vegetation, standing water or uneven ground that would impair deceleration. Pass = RESA meets minimum dimensions and is clear/functional; fail = falls short of minimum with no documented deviation/exemption, or is encroached/poorly maintained.
