acsaRequirement: D080 014M requires monthly inspection of the water reticulation system including main line and internal valves for wear and damage and water meters for proper operation, and daily inspection of aircraft watering points. D080 019M requires a weekly Building and Facilities Maintenance audit of ablution facilities inspecting for wear, damage and structural defects to doors, ceiling, walls, floors, TOILETS, glazing, signage and lighting, plus the Plumbing Audit against CMMS 004. T050 005M cl. 4.1 requires water consumption to be monitored and recorded so all water consumed can be accounted for and water leaks detected, and cl. 4.5 requires walkabout inspections for leaking tanks and pipelines.

Ablution B&FM audit Weekly (W) (D080 019M cl. 4.8.1). Ablution inspection by the contractor's supervisor every two hours, countersigned by ACSA at least once a day (D060 003M cl. 4.5.12). SANS 10254:2004 (fixed electric storage water heating systems) is cited in D080 014M's standards list.

Weekly ablution B&FM audit records

acsaConflict: ACSA sets NO hot-water storage or delivery temperature (no legionella control temperature and no scald limit), NO backflow prevention or non-return valve requirement and no backflow device test interval, and no odour-control requirement. Leak detection is inferred from consumption monitoring rather than being a specified programme.

requirement: Any building shall be provided with storage area for refuse containers
basis: Building Regulation Part U
evidenceExpected: Approved building plans showing the designated refuse storage area.
target: SANS 10400-U Regulation U1: every building must have a suitable storage area for refuse containers, sized and located appropriate to the building's use and refuse-generation rate, constructed of impervious, easily-cleaned surfaces and (deemed-to-satisfy) protected from weather and vermin.
walkabout: Locate the refuse storage area on site and check its surfaces are impervious and easily cleaned, weather/vermin protection (covers, screening) is present and intact, and its size matches current refuse generation.

acsaRequirement: T050 002M cl. 4.5 requires a designated area for sorting and storing general, hazardous and recyclable waste that conforms to the requirements of the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008, requires that the area shall NOT attract bird and wildlife to the site because this poses a safety risk to aircraft operations, requires all waste storage areas to be recorded in the Register of On Site Waste Stores EMS 111 with access control implemented through general site security, and prohibits dumping in non-designated areas at all times. Cl. 4.3 requires waste bins to be provided, correctly labelled and coloured, and each waste storage area to carry a sign describing the waste type which may be disposed of there.
acsaThreshold: No dimensional or capacity standard is stated for the refuse storage area. The stated obligations are qualitative: conformance to NEMWA 59 of 2008, recorded in EMS 111, access-controlled, signed per waste type, and not attracting bird and wildlife (T050 002M cl. 4.5 and 4.3).
acsaEvidence: Register of On-Site Waste Stores - EMS 111 (retained 5 years)
Waste Register - EMS 112 (retained 5 years)
Signage at each waste storage area describing the permitted waste type
Correctly labelled and colour-coded waste bins
AEMR approval of any additional/temporary waste storage area
acsaConflict: T050 002M imposes no size, containment, roofing, drainage or hardstanding requirement for the refuse storage area, and no requirement that it be bunded or drained to sewer despite hazardous waste being stored there - so a KSIA waste yard could satisfy the ACSA procedure while failing basic containment. The bird and wildlife rule is nevertheless a strong, directly testable aerodrome safety cross-check at KSIA.
pfq: Refuse disposal improved; good housekeeping maintained. Verify sustained.

requirement: Check Availability of storage area
basis: 1. National Building Regulations reg U1 (provision of areas) — any building, other than a dwelling house, in which refuse is or will be generated must be provided with an adequate storage area for refuse containers 2. eThekwini Municipality Waste Removal By-law, 2016 s6 (waste bins and bulk waste containers) and s8 (waste storage areas) — storage area appropriate to the number and size of containers and not a nuisance 3. National Norms and Standards for the Storage of Waste, 2013 (GN R.926, GG 37088) s6 (location) and s7 (construction and design) — applicable to a storage facility exceeding 100 m³ general or 80 m³ hazardous waste capacity 4. NEM: Waste Act 59 of 2008 s16 — general duty of care in respect of waste holding and storage
target: Direct field-verification counterpart of the refuse storage area requirement above (SANS 10400-U Regulation U1): confirms the physical area exists, is sized/located correctly, and matches the approved building drawings.
walkabout: Sight the refuse storage area directly against the approved drawings during the site walk-down, and check for any informal/unofficial additional refuse collection points that have grown up around the building.

acsaDocs.title: Waste Management
Waste Management

acsaRequirement: T050 002M requires all waste storage areas to be recorded in the Register of On Site Waste Stores EMS 111, requires waste to be separated into the defined streams at the designated area, and permits additional areas (for example stakeholder-controlled areas) to be used for temporary waste storage ONLY if approved by the AEMR or designated department and conforming to the procedure. All work areas must be kept clear of uncontrolled waste at all times.
acsaThreshold: No area, volume or number of storage areas is prescribed. The register EMS 111 is retained five (5) years. Named waste streams to be separated: general domestic; office and administration paper; galley waste from international flights; fluorescent tubes; oil; medical waste; hazardous maintenance waste; building rubble; asbestos waste; glass, plastic, wood, scrap metal; rubber (tyres); batteries (T050 002M cl. 4.3).
acsaEvidence: Register of On-Site Waste Stores - EMS 111
AEMR written approval for any temporary or stakeholder-controlled waste storage area
Waste Register - EMS 112 recording each stream
Special training records for authorised waste persons (retained 5 years)
acsaConflict: The register is the only evidence ACSA requires that a storage area exists and is adequate; there is no adequacy test, no capacity calculation against waste generation rates, and no inspection frequency for the storage areas themselves in T050 002M (D060 003M cl. 4.6.3 supplies daily satellite bin station and weekly sorting facility inspections instead).
basisNote: The 2013 Norms and Standards bite only above the 100 m³ general / 80 m³ hazardous capacity thresholds, so confirm KSIA's yard capacity before citing them as binding rather than as good practice.
pfq: Refuse disposal improved; good housekeeping maintained. Verify sustained.

requirement: Check Odour control at the storage area
basis: 1. National Norms and Standards for the Storage of Waste, 2013 (GN R.926) s9 (operation) — a waste storage facility must be free from odour or emissions at levels likely to cause annoyance 2. eThekwini Municipality Waste Removal By-law, 2016 s8(3) — the waste storage area and containers must not cause a nuisance and containers must be properly covered by a lid or other covering; s6(4) — containers kept clean, hygienic and in good condition 3. NEM: Waste Act 59 of 2008 s16 — general duty of care: reasonable measures to prevent waste causing pollution or a nuisance 4. Fertilizers, Farm Feeds, Agricultural Remedies and Stock Remedies Act 36 of 1947 s10 and the Regulations relating to the Registration of Pest Control Operators (GN R.98 of 2011), with SANS 10204 for the application of fumigants — the pest-control contractor's operator registration and application standards
evidenceExpected: Records of pest-control measures at the refuse storage area; records of bin-sealing/servicing; any log of odour-related complaints and their resolution.
target: No distinct SANS 10400-U sub-regulation addresses odour at refuse areas (U1–U3 do not cover it); governed instead by the general duty of care in NEM: Waste Act 59 of 2008 s16 and the applicable municipal Health/Waste By-law's nuisance provisions, evidenced through practical measures — sealed bins, pest control, removal frequency.
walkabout: Check bins/containers at the storage area are sealed/covered, note any odour on approach, and look for evidence of an active pest-control programme (bait stations, service stickers).

acsaDocs.title: Waste Management
Waste Management
Maintenance of Soft Services Procedure

acsaRequirement: The nearest ACSA requirements are hygiene and attractant controls rather than odour controls: T050 002M cl. 4.5 requires the storage area not to attract bird and wildlife and all work areas to be kept clear of uncontrolled waste at all times; cl. 4.4 requires waste to be transferred from source to skip or drum so as not to generate environmental impacts through spills or leaks and requires contaminated soil to be removed IMMEDIATELY where the spill involved hazardous waste. D060 003M cl. 4.6.2 requires bait stations and traps to be inspected daily and infestation control to be performed monthly by the pest control contractor.
acsaThreshold: 'any contaminated soil shall be removed immediately' following a hazardous waste spill (T050 002M cl. 4.4). Pest control bait station inspection Daily (D); infestation control and reporting Monthly (M) (D060 003M cl. 4.6.2). Quarterly fumigation register to be inspected at the three-monthly building inspection (D080 028M cl. 4.2.5).
acsaEvidence: Daily bait station and trap inspection records
Monthly pest control contractor infestation reports
Quarterly fumigation register
Register of On-Site Waste Stores - EMS 111
Contaminated soil removal and rehabilitation records
acsaConflict: ACSA has NO odour-control requirement for waste storage areas - no ventilation, wash-down, lidded-container, collection-interval or odour-complaint record obligation appears in T050 002M, D060 003M or D080 028M. Odour is addressed only indirectly through pest control and the bird/wildlife attractant rule. This is an ACSA documentation gap, not a KSIA record gap.
basisNote: The register states no SANS 10400-U sub-regulation covers odour, which is correct — but the 2013 Norms and Standards do state an express odour requirement, so the check is better anchored there than on the by-law's general nuisance wording alone.
pfq: Refuse disposal improved; good housekeeping maintained. Verify sustained.

requirement: Check frequency of waste removal
basis: 1. eThekwini Municipality Waste Removal By-law, 2016 s5 (domestic and business waste removal service) — the municipality need not collect business waste where the generator has contracted an authorised waste removal contractor and the waste is being effectively and timeously removed; s9 (waste collection day) 2. NEM: Waste Act 59 of 2008 s16 — general duty of care: waste must be stored and removed so as to prevent pollution and nuisance, whatever the interval used 3. Waste Classification and Management Regulations, 2013 (GN R.634) reg 11 — waste manifest system for hazardous waste consignments; reg 10 — records of waste generation and management, kept at least five years 4. National Norms and Standards for the Storage of Waste, 2013 (GN R.926) s15 (monitoring and inspection) and s19 (records) — inspection and record-keeping regime for the storage facility
evidenceExpected: Refuse-removal contract or municipal collection schedule stating the contracted/required frequency; collection log/waybills for the last 3 months.
target: No single national statutory refuse-removal frequency exists; municipal by-laws prescribe collection frequency for commercial/industrial premises (commonly at least weekly for general waste, more frequently for putrescible waste). NEM: Waste Act s16's general duty of care requires waste to be stored/managed to prevent nuisance/pollution regardless of the specific frequency used.
walkabout: Check the current fill-level of refuse storage containers against the stated collection schedule (overflowing bins indicate missed/delayed collections), and look for ad-hoc overflow storage suggesting a capacity/frequency mismatch.

acsaDocs.title: Waste Management
Waste Management
Maintenance of Soft Services Procedure

acsaRequirement: T050 002M cl. 4.10 requires identified authorised persons to inspect waste skips before removal and at other times for correct waste separation and to maintain waste records for waste storage areas, and requires those persons to receive special training in waste identification and separation. Cl. 4.6 requires the Designated Person to supervise collection of waste from site and the AEMR to approve the waste collection contractor to ensure waste is transported legally and responsibly. D060 003M cl. 4.6.3 requires daily inspections of satellite bin stations and weekly inspections of sorting facilities.
acsaThreshold: No waste removal frequency is stated. T050 002M cl. 4.10 says only 'before removal and at other times'. The only interval-bearing requirements are D060 003M cl. 4.6.3: satellite bin station inspections Daily (D); sorting facility inspections Weekly (W).
acsaEvidence: Skip inspection records completed before each removal
Waste Manifest Documents and Safe Disposal Certificates (retained 5 years)
Waste Register - EMS 112 reconciling quantities generated, disposed and recycled
Contract with the waste collection contractor and AEMR approval
Daily satellite bin station and weekly sorting facility inspection records
acsaConflict: This is a material ACSA gap: no ACSA document sets a waste removal or skip collection frequency for any airport. Removal frequency can therefore only be tested against the KSIA waste contract SLA, not against an ACSA procedure. B130 001M is equally silent on FOD bin emptying intervals. Recommend the finding be raised against ACSA's procedure set rather than only against the site.
basisNote: No national instrument fixes a removal frequency: the external test is the by-law duty to have waste effectively and timeously removed by an authorised contractor, so the audit finding turns on capacity against actual fill rate rather than on a stated interval.
pfq: Refuse disposal improved; good housekeeping maintained. Verify sustained.

requirement: Check access to the strorage area
basis: 1. National Building Regulations reg U2 (access to areas) — the location of the refuse storage area must be such that access to it from any street, for the purpose of removing the refuse, is to the satisfaction of the local authority 2. National Norms and Standards for the Storage of Waste, 2013 (GN R.926) s8 (access control and notices) — effective access control to prevent unauthorised entry, with signage naming the risks, hours of operation and the responsible person 3. eThekwini Municipality Waste Removal By-law, 2016 s9(2) — containers to be placed for collection where the collection service can reach them 4. NEM: Waste Act 59 of 2008 s16 — general duty of care over the storage area and its use
evidenceExpected: Site access drawings showing the designated collection-vehicle route to the refuse storage area.
target: SANS 10400-U Regulation U2: the refuse storage area must be readily accessible both to occupants/waste generators and to collection vehicles/personnel, without requiring passage through areas that would create a health, safety or hygiene risk (kitchens, public circulation routes, passenger areas).
walkabout: Walk the collection-vehicle access route from the public road to the refuse storage area, checking it is unobstructed and does not pass through passenger or food-service areas; check the access gate/door can be opened by collection personnel on schedule.

acsaDocs.title: Waste Management

acsaRequirement: T050 002M cl. 4.5 requires all waste storage areas to be recorded in the Register of On Site Waste Stores EMS 111 'with access control implemented through general site security', prohibits dumping in non-designated areas at all times, and permits additional temporary storage areas only with AEMR or designated-department approval.
acsaThreshold: No specific access control standard, no gate, fence, lock or permit specification, and no access log requirement. The only stated control is 'access control implemented through general site security' (T050 002M cl. 4.5).
acsaEvidence: Register of On-Site Waste Stores - EMS 111 recording access control arrangements
Site security access control arrangements covering the waste yard
AEMR approval records for additional storage areas
acsaConflict: ACSA states an access control obligation but no standard against which it can be scored - no fencing specification, no restricted-access signage requirement, and no access register. An unfenced, unlocked KSIA waste yard could not be scored non-compliant against ACSA's own wording without importing an external standard.
basisNote: Two different senses of 'access' apply: reg U2 is collection-vehicle access to the satisfaction of the local authority, while GN R.926 s8 is security access control — T050 002M cl. 4.5 addresses only the second, so the collection-access requirement is uncovered.
pfq: Refuse disposal improved; good housekeeping maintained. Verify sustained.

Hazardous waste classified per SANS 10228 and NEMWA 59 of 2008 (cl. 4.2). pfq: Refuse disposal improved; good housekeeping maintained. Verify sustained.

requirement: Structural steel, canopies, cladding and PLB gantries, corrosion protection intact; repainting programme.
basis: SANS 10160; SANS 10162; SANS 1200 H
evidenceExpected: Inspection; programme
target: Maintained [PRIOR Mar 2025 - improved to Acceptable, verify sustained]

acsaRequirement: D080 028M requires the three-monthly visual structural inspection to check all roofs for rust and all gutters and drop box systems to be secure and clear of rust, and the monthly inspection to check all walkways and canopies and all shade ports and covers for signs of failure and buildings for obvious signs of failure including paint. D119MAN cl. 7.6 requires corrosion protection to be designed and implemented to SANS 780 appropriate to site environmental conditions 'including humidity, pollution levels and coastal or aggressive atmospheric exposure' - directly relevant given KSIA's coastal location. D060 009M cl. 4.11 requires visual inspections of buildings on the aerodrome which require repainting.
acsaThreshold: Roof, gutter and drop box rust check: Three Monthly (3M); canopy, walkway, shade port and paint check: Monthly (M) (D080 028M cl. 4.2.5). Repainting frequency: 'THE FREQUENCY SHALL BE DETERMINED ACCORDING TO THE NEED TO REPAINT' - no fixed interval is set (D060 009M cl. 4.11). Corrosion protection per SANS 780 for coastal exposure (D119MAN cl. 7.6), a design requirement only.
acsaEvidence: Monthly building inspection records covering canopies, walkways and paint condition
Three-monthly visual structural inspection records covering roof and gutter rust
Repainting programme and visual inspection reports determining the need to repaint
Six-monthly / yearly competent-person structural inspection reports where corrosion is structural
acsaConflict: ACSA has NO repainting programme interval, NO coating system or dry film thickness specification and NO corrosion-grading scale for structural steel, cladding or PLB gantries in service; D119MAN's SANS 780 corrosion requirement applies only to NEW transformer installations at design stage, and D060 009M expressly leaves repainting frequency to 'need'. Given KSIA's coastal, high-humidity environment this absence should be raised as a network-level ACSA finding, using D080 028M's own escalation logic (visible structural deterioration triggers a competent-person assessment) as the benchmark.
pfq: Building corrosion (steel structure) previously Tolerable, addressed, now Acceptable. Verify sustained.

requirement: Movement/expansion joint sealants and covers intact in terminal, walkways and parkades.
basis: SANS 10400-B; manufacturer specs
evidenceExpected: Inspection
target: No failed joints
walkabout: Walk terminal floors, walkways and parkade decks/ramps and inspect movement joints for torn, perished or missing sealant, damaged or missing cover plates, and any signs of water ingress or trip hazard.

Maintenance of Buildings Procedure

acsaRequirement: The only expansion-joint requirement in the whole ACSA set is D080 029M cl. 4.6.1, which requires the yearly Passenger Boarding Bridge inspection to 'check fixed tunnel expansion joints and handrail visually for damage' - and it is written into the FACT (Cape Town) task list, not the FALE task list. For terminal buildings, walkways and parkades the only relevant ACSA requirement is the D080 028M three-monthly visual structural inspection of walls for cracks, water damage and EXPANSION.
acsaThreshold: PLB fixed tunnel expansion joint visual check: Yearly (Y) (D080 029M cl. 4.6.1, FACT task list). Wall crack/water damage/expansion check: Three Monthly (3M) (D080 028M cl. 4.2.2 / 4.2.5). No sealant type, joint gap tolerance, movement range or replacement cycle is stated anywhere.
acsaEvidence: Yearly PLB inspection records covering fixed tunnel expansion joints
Three-monthly visual structural inspection records recording wall expansion observations
acsaConflict: ACSA has no movement-joint requirement for terminal buildings, walkways or parkades at all - no joint register, no sealant replacement cycle, no cover-plate inspection. The single expansion-joint clause that exists sits in the PBB procedure under a FACT-specific task list, so it cannot be applied at FALE without ACSA confirming it applies. Raise as an ACSA documentation gap.

requirement: Curtain wall/glazing safety glass, seals, fixings; façade inspection programme.
basis: SANS 10400-N; SANS 10137

target: Compliant

acsaRequirement: D080 028M requires, both monthly and at the three-monthly visual structural inspection, that 'all windows and glass panes are secure with no visible damage', and its scope expressly includes glazing, window tinting, architectural louvres and finishes. D060 003M cl. 4.5.14 requires all ceilings and surfaces above 1.7 metres, and windows and facades from 1.8 metres and higher, to be cleaned only by a specialised contractor certified for rope access and high-level work whose Safety File must be approved by the OHS Department, with FALE additionally requiring proof of training of all staff working at height. D080 020M requires lift glass door panels and car sides to be certified and marked at the two-yearly inspection.
acsaThreshold: Glazing security and damage check: Monthly (M) and Three Monthly (3M) (D080 028M cl. 4.2.5). Height threshold for certified high-level cleaning contractors: surfaces above 1.7 metres; windows and facades from 1.8 metres and higher (D060 003M cl. 4.5.14). Lift glass panels 'certified and marked': Two Yearly (2Y) (D080 020M cl. 4.6.1).
acsaEvidence: Monthly and three-monthly building inspection records covering windows and glass panes
Height-cleaning contractor Safety File approved by the OHS Department, with FALE proof of training at height
Weekly height/rope-access cleaning schedule, monitored and signed off
Lift glass panel certification and markings
acsaConflict: There is no facade inspection programme, no safety-glass (SANS 10400 Part N) compliance requirement for terminal glazing, no glazing fixing or structural sealant inspection interval and no requirement to hold glazing certificates for the curtain wall. The only glass certification requirement in the whole set applies to lift car panels. D060 003M's two height thresholds (1.7m for surfaces, 1.8m for windows/facades) are also inconsistent within the same procedure.

requirement: Floors, ceilings, doors, finishes and furniture in safe condition; slip resistance; housekeeping.
basis: SANS 10400; OHS Act - Facilities Regs
evidenceExpected: Site inspection
target: No hazards
walkabout: Walk terminal public and back-of-house areas checking floors for damage, wear or slipperiness (especially near entrances and wet areas), ceilings for damaged/missing tiles or water staining, doors for correct function, and general finishes/furniture for condition and housekeeping standard.

acsaRequirement: D060 003M sets ACSA's terminal-condition and housekeeping regime and names FALE explicitly: contractor performance is monitored against a benchmark of 85% overall cleanliness monthly using the QMS, with FALE additionally required to achieve an ASQ rating of 4.2; the contractor must run hourly internal inspections, ACSA must join a six-weekly joint inspection, and the FALE Service Level Agreement requires response within five (5) minutes and correction of minor to medium deviations within fifteen (15) minutes of the call being logged. D080 028M requires the monthly inspection to check buildings for obvious signs of failure in ceilings, doors, locks and paint, and to check all passageways and handrails into and out of the building for defects.
acsaThreshold: 'a benchmark of eighty-five (85) percent of overall cleanliness, to be achieved on a monthly basis using the QMS. FALE (King Shaka) specific: an ASQ rating of 4.2 is required' (D060 003M cl. 4.5.11). FALE SLA: 'respond within five (5) minutes and to correct any minor to medium deviations within fifteen (15) minutes' (cl. 4.5.12). SLA response times (cl. 4.5.10): spillages/breakages 5 minutes; litter 5 minutes; hygiene cleaning of toilets 3 hours; high pressure cleaning of pavements 2 hours; cleaning of walls 8 hours; windows up to 1.7m 4 hours; industrial floor machines 7 hours (24h00-05h00); stripping and sealing of floors 3 days per area. Deep cleaning: high traffic ablutions Weekly, all other ablutions Two-Weekly (cl. 4.5.13). Contractor internal inspections Hourly; joint B&FM inspection every six weeks (cl. 4.5.11).
acsaEvidence: Monthly QMS cleanliness score against the 85% benchmark
FALE ASQ rating records (4.2 required)
Hourly contractor internal inspection records and six-weekly joint inspection records
Helpdesk logs evidencing 5-minute response and 15-minute correction at FALE
Monthly cleaning action plan submitted to the FALE B&FM supervisor
Deep cleaning schedule and records for high-traffic and other ablutions
Monthly building inspection records covering floors, ceilings, doors, finishes and handrails
acsaConflict: ACSA sets no slip-resistance value for terminal floors (no pendulum test value, no SANS 10400 Part D reference) despite requiring stripping, sealing and polishing of floors, and no furniture condition standard. D060 003M is also the oldest soft-services issue in use (Version 5 effective 02 August 2024 with a revision history entry compiled 28 July 2022) with a Next Revision Date of 02 August 2027.

acsaRequirement: D080 028M requires the three-monthly visual structural inspection to 'check general signage and emergency exit indication' and to inspect the quality of lighting around the building, and the monthly inspection to check all passageways and handrails into and out of the building for defects. D060 024M cl. 4.7.11 requires a daily visual inspection of emergency lights that verifies lights are on, checks the supporting structure and expressly requires 'CHECK EMERGENCY ESCAPE ROUTES CLEARANCE'. S010 003M cl. 4.9 requires all signage to comply with the Wayfinding Disclaimer Signage Design and Technical Specification Manual. D080 020M sets the only universal-access dimensions in the set, for disabled-accessible lifts.
acsaThreshold: Signage and emergency exit indication check: Three Monthly (3M) (D080 028M cl. 4.2.5). Emergency light inspection including escape route clearance: Daily (D) (D060 024M cl. 4.7.11). Disabled lift alarm button height 900 mm - 1200 mm; mirror required where car width is less than 1 500 mm; handrail fitted and secure on two sides for disabled persons (D080 020M cl. 4.6.1, Two Yearly).
acsaEvidence: Daily emergency lighting inspection records including escape route clearance
Three-monthly building inspection records covering general signage and emergency exit indication
Wayfinding Disclaimer Signage Design and Technical Specification Manual and evidence of KSIA signage compliance
Two-yearly lift inspection records covering disabled-access provisions
acsaConflict: ACSA has no universal-access (SANS 10400 Part S) inspection or compliance requirement for ramps, ablutions or circulation routes, and no statutory safety-signage schedule (SANS 1186) or illumination level for signage. The only measurable accessibility dimensions in the whole 99-document set are the lift alarm button height and car-width mirror rule in D080 020M. The Wayfinding manual named in S010 003M is not part of the document set and must be requested.

requirement: Daily Maintenance Inspection Records
basis: 1. National Building Regulations reg A15(1)(a) and (b) — the owner must keep mechanical equipment, facilities and service installations in a safe and functional condition and, where designed to operate during occupancy, operating to the prescribed standard of performance 2. SACAA Civil Aviation Regulations 2011, Part 139 reg 139.02.23 — the aerodrome licence holder must maintain the aerodrome in a serviceable condition through an established maintenance programme, including preventive maintenance 3. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Construction Regulations 2014 reg 11(2)(c) and (d) — structure kept safe for continued use, with inspection and maintenance records kept and produced on request 4. OHS Act 85 of 1993 s8(1) and s9(1) — safe working environment and the duty toward passengers and other non-employees affected by the condition of the building
evidenceExpected: Daily building-condition/inspection checklist log for the asset for a representative recent period (e.g. the last month), showing it is being completed daily without gaps.
target: No external SA statutory standard mandates daily maintenance inspection records specifically; expected to be ACSA's own internal facilities-management control (e.g. a daily building-condition checklist), underpinned by the general OHS Act s8/Facilities Regulations 2004 duty of care rather than an externally mandated document.
walkabout: Ask to see the current daily checklist log on site (not only in a central system) and spot-check a few recent entries against actual conditions observed, to confirm they reflect real checks rather than generic sign-offs.

acsaRequirement: D080 028M requires a DAILY Building and Facilities Maintenance inspection of all scheduled areas inside and outside of a building covering all B&FM maintainable assets, plus a WEEKLY inspection of all scheduled areas, and separately requires B&FM/Maintenance Engineering personnel to carry out a daily corrective-maintenance inspection of areas where B&FM assets are maintained, with any defects found reported to the IMC and D060 016M followed.
acsaThreshold: Building inspection: Daily (D) and Weekly (W) (D080 028M cl. 4.2.2 / 4.2.4 / 4.2.5). Corrective-maintenance inspection: Daily (D080 028M cl. 4.2.6). Contractor audit using M&E 031: Monthly (D080 028M cl. 4.7.1). All listed records retained five (5) years.
acsaEvidence: Daily building inspection sheets for all scheduled areas inside and outside
Weekly building inspection sheets
Daily corrective-maintenance inspection records and defect reports to the IMC
Oracle eAM work requests raised from daily inspections
Contractor Compliance and Quality Assurance Audit - M&E 031 (monthly)
acsaConflict: D080 028M does not prescribe a daily inspection FORM or checklist for buildings (unlike D080 019M which names CMMS 004, or D080 025M which names CMMS 001/008/009/011/018), so KSIA can present any format. The note at cl. 4.2.2 that 'frequencies of inspections may vary at airports as they are dependent on Maintenance Engineering personnel' expressly permits the daily/weekly regime to be varied, which makes even this clear interval unenforceable as written. The procedure is past its own September 2025 revision date.
basisNote: No external instrument prescribes a daily interval or a checklist format; the target's citation of 'Facilities Regulations 2004 reg 2(1)' for the duty of care is misattributed — the maintenance duty is reg 9, 'Condition of rooms and facilities'.

requirement: List of Closed and Outstanding Job cards
basis: 1. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Construction Regulations 2014 reg 11(2)(c) and (d) — the structure must be maintained so that it remains safe for continued use, and records of inspections and maintenance kept and made available on request; an unclosed defect is the auditable exposure 2. National Building Regulations reg A15(1)(a) — the owner's continuing duty to maintain equipment, facilities and service installations in a safe and functional condition, which an ageing open backlog directly contradicts 3. OHS Act 85 of 1993 s8(1) and s8(2)(a) — provision and maintenance of a safe working environment and of plant and systems of work that are safe and without risks to health 4. ISO 55001, Asset management — Management systems, and ISO 55000 — backlog control, corrective-action tracking and evidence of the management system; recommended practice, not statutory
evidenceExpected: CMMS-generated report listing all closed and outstanding job cards for the asset over the last 12 months, including how long outstanding cards have been open.
target: No external SA statutory standard governs this; an operational maintenance-management record (typically a CMMS report) serving as evidence of the OHS Act/Facilities Regulations maintenance duty, with format and retention set by ACSA's own internal procedure.
walkabout: For a sample of "closed" job cards, check whether the completed work is physically evident on site; for any long-open outstanding job card, check whether the underlying defect is still visibly present.

acsaRequirement: D060 016M requires scheduled PM work orders to be distributed for checking and issue and executed within a stated period of issuance, requires two-stage prioritisation (asset criticality then work priority code 1-5), and requires the Maintenance Coordinator to record hours worked and feedback on the work order in Oracle eAM, generate follow-up work orders where findings are noted, and ensure the signed work order is scanned into Oracle eAM with a hard copy filed at the IMC. Z001 001M sets ACSA's resolution clocks and defines when an item becomes overdue.
acsaThreshold: PM/CM work order 'shall be executed within fourteen (14) days or seven (7) days of issuance' (D060 016M cl. 4.2.1). Non-conformance resolution: Catastrophic within 7 days, Critical 14 days, Serious 14 days, Significant 30 days, Minor discretionary; logging within 1-5 days; verification within 48 hours; OVERDUE = due date exceeded by 7 or more days (Z001 001M). Work orders retained five (5) years (D060 016M cl. 11).
acsaEvidence: Oracle eAM open and closed work order backlog report for KSIA
Signed hard-copy work orders scanned into eAM and filed at the IMC
Non-Conformance form PMD 005 signed by Logger, Investigator, Quality Assurer and Closer
Non-Conformance Register PMD 031 (retained 5 years)
Follow-up work orders generated from work order findings
acsaConflict: The '14 days or 7 days' formulation in D060 016M cl. 4.2.1 does not say which window applies to which class of work order, so an outstanding job card cannot be scored against a single unambiguous ACSA interval until ACSA clarifies. D060 016M's Next Revision Date of 31 August 2026 falls immediately before the audit.
basisNote: No external instrument prescribes the format of a job-card backlog report or a maximum age for an open job card, so the finding must be framed against the statutory duty the open item breaches, not against the report itself.

requirement: Building maintenance plan & PM completion (CMMS); backlog managed; condition grading of buildings.
basis: ACSA maintenance SOPs; GRAP 17
evidenceExpected: CMMS reports
question: Is the maintenance backlog trending up or down over the last few reporting periods, and what is driving any growth?
walkabout: Cross-check PM completion claims against physical condition — spot-check a sample of assets shown as recently "PM completed" in the CMMS to confirm the work is evident, and look for visible signs of deferred maintenance inconsistent with a high reported completion rate.

acsaRequirement: D080 028M supplies the building maintenance plan as an escalating inspection ladder (daily and weekly B&FM inspection, monthly failure inspection, three-monthly visual structural inspection, six-monthly structural inspection and yearly structural integrity inspection by a competent person). D060 016M requires PM work orders to originate from equipment maintenance strategies pre-loaded into Oracle eAM and to be executed within a stated window with quality check and sign-off. D060 026M requires asset condition assessment against six hazards - asset criticality, physical state, safety, regulatory and compliance standards, lifecycle phase and performance/KPIs - and makes hazards three and four (safety, and regulatory/compliance) trigger AUTOMATIC consideration of asset replacement or at minimum a risk assessment and mitigation strategy.
acsaThreshold: Inspection ladder 3M / 6M / Y (D080 028M cl. 4.2.2 / 4.2.5). PM work order executed 'within fourteen (14) days or seven (7) days of issuance' (D060 016M cl. 4.2.1). Physical state test: 'can the asset continue operations for a period of a year or longer?'; Key Assets defined as those that can be non-operational for a period of 8 to 48 hours without immediate impact (D060 026M cl. 4.2.2, 4.1.2). Findings and recommendations presented to MANCO Annually (D060 026M cl. 4.2.6).
acsaEvidence: Oracle eAM preventative maintenance programme and PM completion report for buildings at KSIA
eAM backlog report scored against the 14/7 day execution window
Asset condition assessment records against the six D060 026M hazards
Annual MANCO approval of asset renewal findings and recommendations
Fixed Asset Register - FIN 007
Three-monthly, six-monthly and yearly structural inspection records
acsaConflict: ACSA has NO condition-grading scale for buildings - D060 026M offers only a binary 'can the asset continue operations for a period of a year or longer?' test and a 5-category criticality split, with no 1-5 condition index, no backlog KPI and no target PM completion percentage. So 'condition grading of buildings' cannot be evidenced against any ACSA rating scheme. D060 026M also requires end-of-life assets to be identified 'Regularly' with no stated interval.

requirement: • Authority to distribute
basis: • Electricity Regulation Act (Act 4 of 2006) • Distribution Grid Code (all parts) • SANS 62053-21, Electricity metering Static meters for active energy • SANS 62053-23, Electricity metering, Static meters for reactive energy
evidenceExpected: Signed distribution/supply agreement with the municipality; NERSA distribution licence, registration, or exemption confirmation.
target: signed agreement
acsaConflict: No ACSA document requires the airport to hold, renew or evidence an electricity distribution licence or exemption. D100MAN lists the Electricity Regulation Act 4 of 2006 and the NERSA Grid Codes / South African Distribution Code in its referenced standards but converts neither into an operative requirement, and no clause of D060 004M, D060 023M or D060 019M mentions a distribution authority. By contrast D060 021M cl. 4.14.2 DOES require the Senior Manager: Site Maintenance Engineering to obtain a licence under the Petroleum Pipeline Act for fuel - so ACSA has demonstrated it can mandate a statutory operating licence and has simply not done so for electricity distribution. Raise as an ACSA documentation gap.
pfq: E&DM was not audited at KSIA in Mar 2025, no compliance dashboard exists. This round is the E&DM baseline.

acsaRequirement: D100MAN cl. 7.6 requires electrical ready boards to be available for each kiosk tenant connection, metered and connected to the metering system; tenants on a distribution board to be metered and connected to the electronic metering system; all tenants to abide by the energy efficiency requirements with this included in the tenant lease agreement; and ACSA commercial businesses to submit, present and demonstrate an energy strategy and plan as part of lease agreements. acsaThreshold: Tenant energy consumption shall comply with SANS 204 table 2; BMS provision shall enable alerts when energy consumption is out of the SANS 204 table 2 range, processed as an energy audit job card via the CMMS (D100MAN cl. 7.6 b) to f)). Essential supply charged at 'applicable municipal rates plus a standard levy (essential installation/connection fee, maintenance costs, fuel costs) through a lease agreement' (D118MAN cl. 4.3.3 footnote 2).
acsaEvidence: Tenant lease agreements containing the energy efficiency requirements and the tenant energy strategy and plan
Tenant metering schedule showing each kiosk ready board and distribution board connected to the electronic metering system
BMS out-of-range energy alerts converted to energy audit job cards on the CMMS
acsaConflict: ACSA requires tenants to be metered and billed but nowhere requires the airport to hold a licence or exemption to resell electricity, nor a distribution or bulk supply agreement with the municipality. The reselling authority element of this check cannot be evidenced from any ACSA document.

requirement: 5 Yearly Calibration (>10 MVA)
basis: NRS 057 - South African National Standard Code of practice for electricity metering (4.7.4 page 22) NRS 071 - Automated meter reading for large power users. SANS 62051 - Electricity metering
evidenceExpected: Meter register showing capacity class and last/next calibration date for each >10 MVA metering point; calibration certificates dated within the last 5 years.
target: Bulk supply meters serving connections above 10 MVA must be calibrated/verified by an accredited body at least every 5 years, per NRS 057 clause 4.7.4 (page 22); NRS 071 covers the related automated meter reading requirements for these large power users.
walkabout: Locate the >10 MVA bulk meter(s) on site, check the calibration/test tag date against the register, and check meter seals are intact.

acsaDocs.title: Maintenance of Aerodrome Electrical Systems Procedure

acsaRequirement: The only ACSA requirement touching metering accuracy is D060 023M cl. 4.8, which states that calibration certificates for Metering Equipment and Protection Equipment shall be kept with the Electrical Maintenance Department. No interval, no accuracy class and no MVA banding is stated.
acsaEvidence: Calibration certificates for metering equipment held by the Electrical Maintenance Department
MV Switchgear Calibration Certificate (D060 023M cl. 4.8)
acsaConflict: No ACSA document in the 99-document set sets any metering calibration or re-verification interval, and NRS 057 is not cited anywhere. The only metering-related obligations ACSA writes down are D060 023M cl. 4.8 (calibration certificates for metering and protection equipment to be kept with the Electrical Maintenance Department, no interval), D060 004M cl. 4.10.10 (the calibration certificate of the TESTING TOOLS must be presented for each COC issue or re-issue) and D119MAN cl. 8.1.2 routine test 8 (check of ratio and polarity of built-in current transformers, at the factory only). ACSA therefore has no rule against which a missed 5-, 10- or 20-yearly meter calibration at KSIA can be scored. Raise as an ACSA documentation gap. Specifically for supplies above 10 MVA there is no ACSA 5-yearly calibration rule at all.

requirement: 10 Yearly Calibration (1 MVA - 10 MVA)
basis: 1. SANS 474:2022 (NRS 057) — code of practice for electricity metering: categories of metering installation by supply size, accuracy classes and verification requirements 2. Legal Metrology Act 9 of 2014 (administered by the NRCS) — a measuring instrument used for trade must be of an approved type and must be verified; electricity meters used to bill or account for supply fall within this 3. Electricity Regulation Act 4 of 2006 read with the NERSA Distribution Metering Code (Version 6.1, August 2019) — metering accuracy, sealing and periodic verification obligations on the metering party 4. NERSA Grid Code — The Metering Code (Version 10.0, August 2019) — metering installation requirements where the connection is at key-customer or transmission level
evidenceExpected: Meter register showing capacity class and last/next calibration date for 1–10 MVA metering points; calibration certificates dated within the last 10 years.
target: Meters serving connections between 1 MVA and 10 MVA must be calibrated/verified at least every 10 years. No legal basis is cited on this specific row in the source; NRS 057 — the standard cited for the adjacent >10 MVA tier (EDM-003) — most likely governs this tier too, but confirm the exact clause with ACSA.
walkabout: Locate a sample of meters in the 1–10 MVA range, check the calibration/test tag date against the register, and check seals are intact.

acsaRequirement: As for all metering bands, the only ACSA requirement is D060 023M cl. 4.8 - calibration certificates for Metering Equipment and Protection Equipment shall be kept with the Electrical Maintenance Department. ACSA states no 10-yearly interval for 1 MVA to 10 MVA supplies.
acsaEvidence: Calibration certificates for metering equipment held by the Electrical Maintenance Department
acsaConflict: No ACSA document in the 99-document set sets any metering calibration or re-verification interval, and NRS 057 is not cited anywhere. The only metering-related obligations ACSA writes down are D060 023M cl. 4.8 (calibration certificates for metering and protection equipment to be kept with the Electrical Maintenance Department, no interval), D060 004M cl. 4.10.10 (the calibration certificate of the TESTING TOOLS must be presented for each COC issue or re-issue) and D119MAN cl. 8.1.2 routine test 8 (check of ratio and polarity of built-in current transformers, at the factory only). ACSA therefore has no rule against which a missed 5-, 10- or 20-yearly meter calibration at KSIA can be scored. Raise as an ACSA documentation gap. Specifically for the 1 MVA to 10 MVA band there is no ACSA 10-yearly calibration rule at all.
basisNote: NRS 057 was issued as SANS 474 and is now in its second edition (SANS 474:2022); the 10-year tier for 1 MVA to 10 MVA sits in that code's verification table, but the clause could not be confirmed from an authoritative copy, so it is cited at document level.

requirement: 20 Yearly Calibration (<100 kVA)
basis: 1. SANS 474:2022 (NRS 057) — code of practice for electricity metering: whole-current (direct-connected) metering for supplies below 100 kVA, accuracy class and verification interval 2. Legal Metrology Act 9 of 2014 — where ACSA on-sells electricity to tenants the meter is a measuring instrument used for trade and must be of an approved type and verified; this, not ACSA procedure, is the binding duty on tenant sub-metering 3. Electricity Regulation Act 4 of 2006 read with the NERSA Distribution Metering Code (Version 6.1, August 2019) — accuracy, sealing and verification of the metering installation 4. SANS 62052-11 and the SANS 62053 series — type and accuracy requirements for a.c. electricity metering equipment against which a meter is verified
evidenceExpected: Meter register showing capacity class and last/next calibration date for <100 kVA metering points; calibration certificates or installation records dated within the last 20 years.
target: Meters serving connections under 100 kVA (typically tenant/back-of-house supplies) must be calibrated/verified at least every 20 years — the longest of the three interval tiers, reflecting lower financial exposure. No legal basis is cited on this row; likely the same NRS 057 standard cited for EDM-003 — confirm with ACSA.
walkabout: Spot-check a sample of small tenant/back-of-house meters for a calibration/installation date tag against the register.

The only metering-related obligations ACSA writes down are D060 023M cl. 4.8 (calibration certificates for metering and protection equipment to be kept with the Electrical Maintenance Department, no interval), D060 004M cl. 4.10.10 (the calibration certificate of the TESTING TOOLS must be presented for each COC issue or re-issue) and D119MAN cl. 8.1.2 routine test 8 (check of ratio and polarity of built-in current transformers, at the factory only). ACSA therefore has no rule against which a missed 5-, 10- or 20-yearly meter calibration at KSIA can be scored. Raise as an ACSA documentation gap. There is also no meter register requirement anywhere in ACSA's document set and no in-service CT/VT ratio verification requirement - D119MAN's check is a factory routine test only.

requirement: Municipal tariff category verified as correct; supplies reconciled against bills; no unbilled premium supplies (kick-off risk item 6.5.1).
basis: Municipal tariff by-laws; NERSA
evidenceExpected: Bills vs meter data reconciliation
target: Reconciled
question: Has ACSA specifically checked for any supply point that exists on site but is not billed at all (the 'unbilled premium supply' risk), and if one was found, what back-billing/corrective action was taken?
walkabout: Confirm every metering point/intake substation on site is accounted for in the reconciliation list — look for a supply (e.g. newer building, generator, tenant connection) without a corresponding municipal account.
acsaConflict: No ACSA document addresses municipal tariff category verification, reconciliation of supplies against bills, or identification of unbilled premium supplies. D118MAN cl. 4.3.3 footnote 2 is the only tariff reference in the set and it concerns charging tenants for essential (post-switchover) supply at municipal rates plus a levy - it imposes no verification duty on ACSA for its own incoming tariff. J060 002M's compliance regime would cover this only if the applicable tariff legislation were entered on the Regulatory Compliance Universe GOV 005, which should be requested and tested. Raise the kick-off risk item 6.5.1 against ACSA's procedure set as well as against KSIA.

requirement: • Energy Optimisation
basis: D060MAN ACSA standards and Guidelines for energy efficiency
evidenceExpected: Prior FY actual kWh; current FY actual (or annualised) kWh; the % change calculation; register of optimisation initiatives implemented and their estimated savings.
target: 2.5% of past FY actual kWh
walkabout: Confirm cited optimisation initiatives (e.g. LED retrofits, VSDs, control upgrades) are physically installed and operating as claimed.

acsaDocs.title: Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency

acsaDocs.clause: 4.6.2 Availability of the Resource and/or System
acsaDocs.title: Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency
Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency
Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency
Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency

acsaRequirement: D100MAN is ACSA's energy optimisation standard and it sets hard numeric targets for any energy system, retrofit or new load: retrofits must deliver an energy saving above a stated percentage, additional demand from a stated threshold must be part-supplied from renewable or alternative energy, the power factor must be maintained at a stated minimum, and any energy system must demonstrably achieve a stated availability and design life. Energy use models must resolve generation and consumption per asset, system, process or area per hour.
acsaThreshold: 'Energy Savings (Retrofits) > 40%'; 'Power Factor 0,95'; 'Standard Frequency 50 Hz +/- 2,5% (NRS 048)'; 'MV volt drop > 500V: deviation +/- 5% (NRS 034)'; 'LV volt drop < 500V: deviation +/- 10%' (D100MAN cl. 8.5). 'All additional electrical demand from 1MVA shall incorporate renewable or alternative energy supplying a minimum of 40% of the additional demand' (cl. 7.6 a)). 'Availability - 99.5%; System Design life - 20 years' (cl. 4.6.2). Energy use models: 'energy generation and energy consumed per asset/system/process/area PER HOUR' (cl. 4.6.1). GBCSA '4 STAR Rating as a minimum' (cl. 4).
acsaEvidence: Pre and post Energy Efficiency reports for every retrofitting project
Energy Savings report per D100MAN section 9.5 / 9.2
Hourly energy use model output per asset, system, process or area
Site Energy Engineer and Electrical Maintenance Manager approval of any new load at or above 1MVA
Power factor recording at the Utility's point of delivery (main electrical power intake station)
Commissioning acceptance criteria checklists for lighting, motion sensors and HVAC
acsaConflict: D100MAN is a DESIGN and selection standard for new buildings, refurbishments, upgrades and replacement cycles - it imposes no operational energy optimisation duty on a running airport, sets no measurement interval for verifying that 99.5% availability or power factor 0.95 is actually being achieved in service, and its master record is filed under 'D060MAN' in its own records table, a document-control error to raise.

requirement: • Cost Savings
basis: 1. Public Finance Management Act 1 of 1999 s.51(1)(a)(i) and s.51(1)(b)(ii) — the accounting authority of a Schedule 2 major public entity must maintain effective, efficient and transparent systems of financial management and must prevent fruitless and wasteful expenditure, which makes a tracked energy cost-saving target a governance duty rather than a discretionary metric 2. SANS 50010 — measurement and verification of energy savings: the South African method for establishing a baseline and quantifying a claimed saving, and the yardstick for whether a stated Rand or percentage saving is defensible 3. ISO 50001:2018 cl. 6.2 (energy objectives and energy targets, which must be measurable) and cl. 6.4 (energy performance indicators) — voluntary unless ACSA has adopted or certified to the standard, not statutory 4. Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 s.12L with the Regulations on the Allowance for Energy Efficiency Savings — an incentive ACSA may claim against verified savings; it is an opportunity, not a duty, and not taking it is not a finding
evidenceExpected: Any documented cost-saving target and actual Rand savings achieved, with the calculation basis (e.g. avoided cost vs. baseline tariff x baseline consumption).
target: No specific numeric cost-saving target is stated in the source for this item — confirm with ACSA whether a Rand or percentage cost-saving figure is set for the period, and whether it is tracked as a distinct metric from the 2.5% kWh optimisation target (EDM-008).
question: Does ACSA track a specific cost-saving target for energy at KSIA, what is it for this period, and has it been achieved?

acsaDocs.title: Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency
Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency

acsaRequirement: D100MAN cl. 4.4 fixes the business case viability criteria every ACSA energy efficiency investment must satisfy: the internal rate of return must exceed the weighted average cost of capital, net present value must return positive cashflow, the profitability index must exceed 1, and the payback period must be less than a set fraction of the estimated useful life of the asset. Cl. 8.5 fixes the minimum energy saving a retrofit must deliver.
acsaThreshold: 'IRR > WACC; NPV positive cashflow; Profitability Index > 1; Payback Period less than 75% of the estimated useful life of the asset' (D100MAN cl. 4.4). 'Energy Savings (Retrofits) > 40%' (D100MAN cl. 8.5).
acsaEvidence: Business case with IRR, NPV, profitability index and payback calculations for each energy project
Pre and post Energy Efficiency reports and the Energy Savings report
Disposal certificate of all lights where retrofitting (D100MAN records table)
Electronic datasheets of equipment purchased and letters of warranty
acsaConflict: The 75%-of-useful-life payback test and the >40% retrofit saving are design-approval gates only; D100MAN requires no post-implementation verification that the claimed savings were realised beyond the 'pre and post Energy Efficiency reports', and sets no interval for reporting cost savings in operation.
basisNote: No South African instrument fixes a numeric energy cost-saving target for an airport operator, so a finding here should be framed as the absence of a measurable, verified target rather than as breach of a threshold.

requirement: • Emmision Reduction
basis: 1. National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004, National Greenhouse Gas Emission Reporting Regulations GN 275 of 3 April 2017 (as amended by GN 994 of 2020) — mandatory registration and annual reporting by data providers conducting a listed activity above the capacity threshold 2. Climate Change Act 22 of 2024 — the national framework of sectoral emission targets and carbon budgets against which an entity-level reduction target is now judged 3. Carbon Tax Act 15 of 2019 — liability and reporting for Schedule 2 activities above threshold; purchased grid electricity is taxed at the generator, not at ACSA 4. ISO 14064-1 — quantification and reporting of a greenhouse gas inventory, including baseline year and reporting boundary; the ACI Airport Carbon Accreditation programme cited in T010 001P is an industry scheme, not law
evidenceExpected: Prior and current FY kWh (and/or calculated tCO2e) figures with the % change calculation; emissions calculation methodology used.
target: 2% of past FY kWh

acsaDocs.title: Integrated Environmental Management Policy
Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency
Integrated Environmental Management Policy

acsaRequirement: T010 001P cl. 4.1.2.2 commits ACSA to quantify its carbon footprint and to add airports to the ACI Airport Carbon Accreditation Programme, and cl. 4.3 lists carbon footprint size and air emissions among the network-wide environmental monitoring parameters. D100MAN cl. 7.6 a) delivers the only quantified emission-reduction mechanism in the set by requiring renewable or alternative energy on additional demand.
acsaThreshold: 'All additional electrical demand from 1MVA shall incorporate renewable or alternative energy supplying a minimum of 40% of the additional demand' (D100MAN cl. 7.6 a)). T010 001P states no emission reduction target, no baseline year and no percentage: monitoring is 'in accordance with need' and its extent and frequency 'determined by risk assessment of need plus regulatory requirements' (cl. 4.1.2.5, 4.3).
acsaEvidence: Carbon footprint calculations and ACI Airport Carbon Accreditation records for KSIA
Integrated Annual Report environmental indicators
Site Energy Engineer approval of new loads at or above 1MVA showing the 40% renewable component
acsaConflict: ACSA sets no emission reduction target, no reduction percentage, no baseline and no reporting frequency anywhere in the set - only a commitment to quantify. The single numeric emission-reduction lever (1MVA / 40% renewable) sits in a design standard and applies only to NEW additional demand, so existing KSIA load carries no reduction obligation under any ACSA document.
basisNote: Whether KSIA is a data provider under the reporting regulations turns on its own combustion capacity rather than on its electricity purchases, so confirm registration status before treating the 2% target as a regulatory obligation; no South African instrument fixes a percentage reduction for an airport's purchased electricity.

requirement: Monthly consumption records; KPIs (kWh/pax, kWh/m²) tracked against targets; energy saving initiatives tracked.
basis: ACSA D060MAN standards & guidelines; ISO 50001 principles
evidenceExpected: Energy reports
target: Targets met
walkabout: Spot-check that BMS/metering dashboards referenced in the reports are live and showing current data.

acsaDocs.title: Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency
Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency
Integrated Environmental Management Policy
Waste Water Management

acsaRequirement: D100MAN cl. 4.6.1 requires energy use models to provide, as a minimum, energy generation and energy consumed per asset, system, process or area PER HOUR, and cl. 7.6 requires the BMS to enable alerts when energy consumption falls outside the SANS 204 table 2 range, with each alert processed as an energy audit job card via the CMMS. T010 001P cl. 4.3 lists electricity consumption as a network-wide monitoring parameter. T050 005M cl. 4.1 gives the only stated consumption-recording interval in the set, for water.
acsaThreshold: Energy use model granularity: 'per asset/system/process/area PER HOUR' (D100MAN cl. 4.6.1). Tenant consumption benchmark: SANS 204 table 2, with BMS alerts outside that range raised as an energy audit job card via the CMMS (D100MAN cl. 7.6 f)). Water consumption: 'on a monthly (where possible) or quarterly basis' (T050 005M cl. 4.1). Electricity consumption monitoring under T010 001P cl. 4.3: 'in accordance with need' - no interval stated.
acsaEvidence: Hourly energy use model data per asset, system, process or area
BMS out-of-range consumption alerts and the resulting CMMS energy audit job cards
Monthly electricity consumption records for KSIA
Integrated Annual Report electricity consumption indicator
acsaConflict: ACSA nowhere defines kWh/pax or kWh/m2 as an energy KPI, sets no energy targets against which performance can be scored, and prescribes no monthly consumption reporting interval for electricity - only water carries the monthly/quarterly rule. The only consumption benchmark in the whole set is SANS 204 table 2 and it applies to TENANTS, not to ACSA's own operation.

requirement: Ensure that max demand never exceed NMD. When an airport exceed their NMD more than once in a given month, a penalty is levied over the next 12 months
basis: • Electricity Regulation Act (Act 4 of 2006) • NERSA NMD Rules
evidenceExpected: Demand profile/interval data (e.g. 30-minute kVA readings) from the bulk supply meter for the review period; the registered NMD value; any penalty notices/invoices.
target: Actual maximum electrical demand must never exceed the airport's Notified Maximum Demand (NMD) registered with the municipality/NERSA. Under the NERSA NMD Rules, exceeding NMD more than once within a calendar month triggers a demand penalty applied over the following 12 months.
acsaConflict: No ACSA document mentions Notified Maximum Demand, maximum demand exceedance, or the resulting municipal penalty regime. D100MAN's quality-of-supply table (cl. 8.5) covers volt drop, frequency and power factor but not demand, and D060 019M covers only PLANNED outage lead times, not demand management or load curtailment. There is therefore no ACSA requirement, threshold or record against which NMD exceedance at KSIA can be tested. Raise as an ACSA documentation gap with a direct financial exposure: a single exceedance repeated in a month triggers a penalty levied over the following 12 months.

requirement: Maximum demand never exceeds Notified Maximum Demand; NMD penalties tracked; load-shedding/peak strategy.
basis: Electricity Regulation Act; municipal tariff conditions
evidenceExpected: Demand profile data
target: 0 exceedances
walkabout: Confirm demand-management equipment (e.g. BMS demand-limiting function, generator/load-shed triggers) is physically installed and configured; ask control-room/BMS staff how an approaching demand peak is identified and managed.

acsaDocs.title: Power Outage Management Procedure
Management of Electricity Backup Systems Procedure

acsaRequirement: ACSA has no maximum demand or load-shedding requirement. The nearest related provisions are D060 019M cl. 4.2.4, which states that no lead times apply to faults, unplanned outages or emergency switching and that emergency switching may only be conducted if people and equipment are exposed to danger, and D060 006M cl. 4.5.7, which requires each diesel generator to be tested on load monthly with the change-over time from simulated mains failure to generator supply restoration recorded.
acsaThreshold: 'TEST EACH DIESEL GENERATOR ON LOAD FOR A MINIMUM OF 15 MINUTES' with recorded change-over time, and off-load 'FOR A MINIMUM OF FIVE (5) MINUTES' weekly (D060 006M cl. 4.5.7). No NMD figure, no demand limit and no penalty threshold exists in any ACSA document.
acsaEvidence: Monthly generator on-load test records including recorded change-over time
Weekly generator off-load test records
Municipal accounts showing notified maximum demand and any exceedance penalty
acsaConflict: ACSA has no NMD, maximum demand, load-shedding or peak-strategy procedure anywhere in the 99-document set. D060 019M governs planned outages only (customer notification 14 working days, scope of work 10 working days, Operating Screeds and Single Line Diagrams 7 working days, load studies 5 days) and is silent on demand management. The check cannot be evidenced against ACSA's own documents; only the municipal account and any KSIA-local practice can be tested.

requirement: Annual maintenance, ensuring optimal performance and preservation of warranties and guarantees
basis: •ICAO Annexure 14, •OHS Act 85 of 1993, Electrical Machinery Regulations •ORHVS Regulations (on elec Retic components) •SANS 10142 part 1 & 2 - Code of Practice for the LV Installations •NRS 048 - Electricity supply •SANS 10142-1 The wiring of premises •D060 004 - Maintenance of Certificate of Compliance Issuance
evidenceExpected: Annual PV maintenance service report/certificate dated within the last 12 months; O&M manual/warranty terms specifying the required maintenance; CoC reissued or confirmed after maintenance per D060 004, where applicable.
target: date (once a year)
walkabout: Inspect the PV array and inverter enclosure for a current service tag/sticker, visible cleanliness, and no obvious loose cabling, damaged panels, or unresolved fault indicators.
acsaConflict: ACSA has NO solar PV maintenance procedure anywhere in the 99-document set. The only mention of solar plant as an operating asset is D118MAN cl. 4.3.3, which lists 'solar system' among the critical loads requiring no-break power through an online UPS and a backup generator - a load classification, not a maintenance requirement. No annual maintenance activity, task list, frequency, warranty-preservation obligation or OEM maintenance requirement exists for PV plant, and D100MAN (ACSA's energy design standard) contains no PV clause at all. Every other asset class at KSIA has a D060 or D080 procedure with named asset groups, task lists and frequencies; PV plant has none, so there is no ACSA-authored basis on which to score PV maintenance, warranty preservation or guarantee compliance. Raise a finding against ACSA's asset procedure set as well as against the site, and request the PV plant OEM maintenance and warranty documentation directly from KSIA.

requirement:
Min Irradiance Threshold (MIT)
(all ACSA plants are designed at 50-70 W/m2)
basis: 1. IEC 61724-1:2021 — photovoltaic system performance monitoring: irradiance sensor selection, accuracy, plane-of-array placement, calibration and cleaning, and the monitoring system classes (A, B, C) that fix how good the measurement must be 2. IEC 62446-1:2016+A1:2018 — grid-connected PV documentation, commissioning tests and inspection: the commissioning record that establishes the expected start-up and generation behaviour the plant is now measured against 3. NRS 097-2-1:2024 (and NRS 097-2-3 for larger embedded generators) — grid interconnection requirements for embedded generation, applied through the distributor's connection agreement 4. OHS Act 85 of 1993, Electrical Installation Regulations 2009 reg 2(1) — the user's duty for the safety and maintenance of the installation, which carries the sensor and monitoring hardware
evidenceExpected: PV monitoring/SCADA data showing irradiance vs. generation output, with any low-irradiance startup failures flagged.
walkabout: Check the on-site irradiance sensor/pyranometer is clean, undamaged and correctly positioned (a dirty/obstructed sensor gives false readings), and confirm the monitoring dashboard is live with current data.
acsaConflict: No ACSA document states a Minimum Irradiance Threshold, an irradiance design basis, or the 50-70 W/m2 figure quoted in the checklist row. D100MAN, which is ACSA's energy design standard, addresses lighting, HVAC, pumps, motors, building envelope and supply quality but contains no solar PV design or performance clause at all. The 50-70 W/m2 figure cannot be attributed to any ACSA document and must not be cited as an ACSA requirement.
basisNote: The 50-70 W/m2 minimum irradiance threshold is an inverter start-up and design parameter set by the OEM and the plant designer, not a figure fixed by any standard; what is externally governed is the quality, calibration and upkeep of the irradiance measurement used to judge it, and IEC 61724-1 is cited at document level because its clause numbering could not be confirmed.

requirement: Performance Ratio and Plant efficiency
basis: 1. IEC 61724-1:2021 — defines performance ratio and the measured quantities and monitoring accuracy required to compute it, including the temperature-corrected variant; the source of the PR metric itself 2. IEC TS 62446-2:2020 — maintenance of grid-connected PV systems: periodic performance checks and the response to measured underperformance 3. IEC 62446-1:2016+A1:2018 — commissioning tests and documentation establishing the expected performance baseline 4. NRS 097-2-1:2024 / NRS 097-2-3 — embedded generation connection and operating requirements, including metering of generated energy at the point of connection
evidenceExpected: PV monitoring system PR reports (monthly and rolling annual).
question: If PR is below 0.9, what has been identified as the cause, and what corrective action has been taken?
walkabout: Inspect the array for visible soiling, shading obstructions, or damaged/discoloured panels, and check inverters for fault codes or reduced-output warnings.

acsaDocs.clause: 4.6.2 Availability of the Resource and/or System
acsaDocs.title: Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency
Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency

acsaRequirement: There is no PV-specific performance ratio requirement, but D100MAN cl. 4.6.2 applies to ANY energy system and requires it to demonstrably achieve a stated availability and design life, and cl. 4.6.1 requires energy use models to report energy GENERATION as well as consumption per asset, system, process or area per hour - which brings a PV plant within scope of an hourly generation reporting duty.
acsaThreshold: 'Availability - 99.5%; System Design life - 20 years with allowable component replacement as per OEM or matched to the design life of the larger investment' (D100MAN cl. 4.6.2). 'energy generation and energy consumed per asset/system/process/area PER HOUR' (D100MAN cl. 4.6.1).
acsaEvidence: Hourly PV generation data from the energy use model / monitoring platform
Availability record for the PV plant tested against 99.5%
PV plant design life and component replacement schedule
acsaConflict: D100MAN sets availability and design life for energy systems generally but states NO performance ratio, NO plant efficiency target, NO specific yield and no PV degradation limit. Applying the 99.5% availability and 20-year design life to the KSIA PV plant is defensible on the face of cl. 4.6.2 but should be put to ACSA for confirmation, since D100MAN is a design standard for new works rather than an operating standard.
basisNote: No external standard sets a minimum performance ratio; 0.9 sits above the 0.75 to 0.85 range typical of a well-performing fixed-tilt plant, so it is an ACSA design target and a shortfall against it is a performance observation rather than a breach of a standard.

requirement: Array is not shaded
basis: 1. IEC 62446-1:2016+A1:2018 — grid-connected PV documentation, commissioning and inspection: the shading assessment and site layout recorded at commissioning, against which any later change is judged 2. IEC TS 62446-2:2020 — maintenance of grid-connected PV systems: periodic visual inspection of the array and its surroundings and investigation of localised underperformance 3. IEC 61724-1:2021 — string-level and array-level monitoring, the means by which persistent shading on particular rows is detected rather than assumed 4. IEC 61215 series — module design qualification including the hot-spot endurance test; a design standard explaining the damage mechanism, not an operational duty on ACSA
target: should not be shaded, as shade will affect generation capacity
question: Has anything changed around the array since commissioning (tree growth, new structures, temporary equipment) that could now cast shadow on the panels during operating hours?
walkabout: Visually check for shadow falling on panels from trees, structures, or equipment at the time of the site visit — especially early morning/late afternoon when shadows are longest; check string-level monitoring, if available, for consistent underperformance on particular rows.
acsaConflict: No ACSA document contains any shading, vegetation-clearance or obstruction requirement for solar arrays. D060 005M (Vegetation and Habitat Management) sets grass-cutting priorities and heights for navigational aids, runway strips and perimeter fences but does not list PV arrays as a protected asset, and D060 015M (Obstacle Limitations) protects navigational aids, not generation plant. There is therefore no ACSA basis on which to require or score shading management at the KSIA PV plant.
basisNote: No statute or SANS standard imposes a shade-free duty on an operating array; the external authority is the inspection and monitoring regime in the IEC 62446 series, and freedom from shading is usually also a condition of the module and yield warranties, which is contract and recommended practice rather than law.

requirement: PV performance ratio monitored; inverter and panel maintenance/cleaning records; PV installation CoC; earthing/lightning protection.
basis: SANS 10142-1-2; OEM; SANS 62305
evidenceExpected: Monitoring data; CoC
target: PR ≥ design
walkabout: 1. Confirm the PV monitoring system is live on site. 2. Check panels for soiling and inverters for cleanliness, ventilation clearance, and absence of fault indicators. 3. Spot-check DC/AC combiner box and cable labelling for consistency with the CoC. 4. Visually inspect earthing conductors, bonding, and surge protection devices at the array/inverter for physical integrity (no corrosion, disconnection, or damage).
