Maintenance of Certificate of Compliance Issuance Procedure
Maintenance of Certificate of Compliance Issuance Procedure

acsaDocs.clause: 4.6.2 Availability of the Resource and/or System
acsaDocs.title: Standards and Guidelines for Energy Efficiency

acsaRequirement: D060 004M brings the PV installation within the electrical Certificate of Compliance regime: a COC is required for new LV installations, alterations and extensions; only a Registered Person may issue one, after inspection and testing to SANS 10142-1; the COC must be accompanied by a test report in the format approved by the Chief Inspector; and the calibration certificate of the testing tools must be presented at each issue or re-issue. D100MAN cl. 4.6.2 sets 99.5% availability and a 20-year design life for any energy system.
acsaThreshold: COC issued only after inspection and testing per SANS 10142-1; 'the user or lessor may not allow a change of ownership if the Certificate of Compliance is OLDER THAN TWO YEARS' (D060 004M cl. 4.4 (h)); calibration certificate of testing tools required at every COC issue or re-issue (cl. 4.10.10). Yearly COC reconciliation inspection for the substation, LV switchboard, transformer and lighting asset groups (cl. 4.7.1 / 4.9.1). Availability 99.5%; design life 20 years (D100MAN cl. 4.6.2).
acsaEvidence: Certificate of Compliance for the PV installation in the latest SANS 10142-1 format, with test report
Calibration Certificate - Testing Tools
Yearly COC reconciliation record for the KSIA electrical asset groups
Earthing and lightning protection test results (must be requested - not required by any ACSA procedure)
acsaConflict: ACSA has NO PV performance ratio monitoring requirement, NO inverter or panel maintenance or cleaning task list or frequency, and NO earthing or lightning protection inspection requirement for PV. Only the generic LV COC obligation and the generic energy-system availability figure can be applied. The absence of a PV maintenance regime is an ACSA documentation gap.

requirement:
• Grid Connection - agreement with utility to export
• Land rights - submission to the council
• Environmental - depending on technology. Hydro one must comply with regulations under water section and battery storage must comply with 
• Wheeling agreements
basis: • Battery Storage Grid Code on DS network connection - NERSA • Renewable Energy Grid Code - NERSA • Electricity Regulation Act (Act 4 of 2006)
evidenceExpected: 1. Signed grid connection/export agreement; grid code compliance confirmation. 2. Land rights submission and council approval. 3. Environmental authorisation matching the storage technology (e.g. water use licence). 4. Signed wheeling agreement.
target: This row bundles four approvals for energy storage, each applicable only if relevant to the installed technology. 1. Grid connection: any storage system exporting to/interacting with the grid needs a signed agreement with the utility, complying with the applicable NERSA grid code (Battery Storage Grid Code or Renewable Energy Grid Code). 2. Land rights: where land use is required, rights/authorisation must be formally submitted to and approved by the relevant council. 3. Environmental: approvals matching the storage technology — e.g. water-use authorisation under the National Water Act for hydro storage, or applicable environmental/safety approvals for battery storage. 4. Wheeling: where energy is wheeled through the municipal/utility network, a signed wheeling agreement with the network operator is required.
question: Of these four approval types, which actually apply to KSIA's current energy storage installation(s), given the specific technology and configuration in use?
acsaConflict: ACSA has no energy storage standard or procedure at all. Nothing in the 99-document set addresses grid connection or export agreements with the utility, land rights or council submissions, or the technology-specific environmental regimes named in this check (water-use authorisation for hydro, battery-specific requirements). The nearest transferable clause is T050 003M cl. 4.3.1, which requires AEMR involvement in planning and design, identification of significant environmental impacts per T010 001M, determination of whether an EIA is required per N010 006M, and an Environmental Authorisation under NEMA 107 of 1998 before construction - but that clause is written for above and underground storage TANKS, not for battery or hydro storage, and cannot be applied to an energy storage project without ACSA confirming it. Raise as an ACSA documentation gap; request any grid connection/export agreement directly from KSIA.

requirement: Battery storage: ventilation, fire detection/suppression, isolation, manufacturer maintenance.
evidenceExpected: Inspection
target: Compliant
walkabout: 1. Check ventilation louvres/fans are unobstructed and, where mechanical, running. 2. Check detector heads are present and undamaged, with current service tags. 3. Locate isolation switches and confirm labelling and accessibility. 4. Check current service tags and any visible damage, corrosion, or thermal distress on battery cabinets.

acsaDocs.title: Standards and Guidelines Manual for Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)
Standards and Guidelines Manual for Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)
Standards and Guidelines Manual for Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)
Maintenance of Fire Fighting Systems Procedure
Maintenance of Fire Fighting Systems Procedure

acsaRequirement: The closest ACSA standard is D118MAN, which mandates the battery technology, requires installation to comply with SANS 10142-1 and the Electrical Machinery Regulations 'ensuring proper ventilation and thermal management, safe and accessible layout, correct earthing and bonding, appropriately rated cable sizing and protection, clear labelling and isolation provisions, and an adequate enclosure/cabinet IP rating', and requires back feed protection to prevent hazardous voltage appearing at the input terminals in stored energy mode. Fire detection and suppression covering battery rooms falls under D080 002M.
acsaThreshold: 'The battery technology for UPS systems shall be lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery technology' (D118MAN cl. 8.6). Environmental limits for normal operation: 'Temperature: 0 degC to +40 degC; Relative Humidity: 20% to 80%; Altitude: up to 1000 m above sea level without derating' (D118MAN cl. 8.2). Modular design considered for UPS sizes from at least 20kVA, with a maintenance bypass for critical installations (cl. 4.3.8). Fire Detection inspection Weekly (W), maintenance Monthly (M); Gas Suppression maintenance Yearly (Y); hydrostatic pressure test on all gas suppression cylinders 10 Yearly (D080 002M cl. 4.7.2, 4.7.4).
acsaEvidence: D118MAN Stage 3 design report and type test certificates to SANS/IEC 62040-3
Certificate of Compliance and the twelve D118MAN handover deliverables
Weekly fire detection inspection and monthly panel functionality test records
Annual gas suppression maintenance records and 10-yearly cylinder hydrostatic test records
Manufacturer maintenance schedule and CMMS asset loading proof
acsaConflict: D118MAN governs UPS, not grid-scale or standalone battery energy storage, and it specifies NO minimum battery autonomy or backup duration and NO battery end-of-life or replacement criteria despite mandating Li-ion - both are gaps ACSA should close. There is no isolation, ventilation rate or thermal runaway requirement specific to battery energy storage anywhere in the set.

requirement: BMS set-points and schedules optimised; alarms managed; plant not in manual override.
basis: ACSA D060MAN; ISO 50001 principles
evidenceExpected: BMS screenshots/logs
target: Auto control
walkabout: In the BMS control room, check for any plant left in 'manual/hand override' and check the active alarm list for unresolved/aged alarms; cross-check a sample of plant on site is running per its scheduled state.

requirement:
•measurement of hydrocarbons (HC), carbon monoxide (CO), carbon dioxide (Co2) and oxides of nitrogen (NOx) to determine mass emissions through calculations during aircraft landing and take-off cycle (LTO). to comply with ICAO 9889 & Annex 16
• The LTO cycle is based on times in mode data during high activity periods at major airports for four modes of engine operation: taxi/idle, take-off, climb-out and approach.
• The mass emissions for these modes are combined to yield the reported emissions certification levels.

basis: • ICAO Doc 9889 (Airport Air Quality Manual) • NEMA • National Framework for Air Quality Management in RSA (section 5.2.1.3) • SANS 1929 - Limits for common pollutants • ICAO Annex 16 Vol II - Aircraft Engine Emissions

acsaRequirement: B170 001M requires HIRA exercises to be made on a continuous basis in all areas of operations, and a formal documented HIRA to be conducted and completed PRIOR TO each of five named triggers: adoption of a new safety procedure or process; a change to an existing safety procedure or process; the start of any airside works in progress; the start of any new project impacting airside operations; and as and when new hazards are identified in existing WIP, procedures or projects. The register is the ICAO SMM Hazard Identification and Safety Risk Management Log with eight columns in a fixed order, scoring an initial Safety Risk Index despite existing defences (column 6) and a residual index after further action (column 8), scored only on ACSA's approved matrix.
acsaThreshold: 5 x 5 = 25-cell matrix, Severity A-E x Likelihood 1-5, cells written likelihood-number-first. UNACCEPTABLE (Red): 5A, 5B, 5C, 4A, 4B, 3A - 'Unacceptable under the existing circumstances. Risk mitigation critical'. MITIGATION REQUIRED / MANAGEMENT DECISION (Amber): 5D, 5E, 4C, 4D, 4E, 3B, 3C, 3D, 2A, 2B, 2C, 1A. ACCEPTABLE (Green): 3E, 2D, 2E, 1B, 1C, 1D, 1E (B170 001M cl. 4.3.3 / 4.3.4). Eight-column log in the stated order (cl. 4.4). 'only the matrices outlined in this procedure shall be utilised' and the SACAA Director of Civil Aviation 'shall only accept safety information using the said format' (cl. 4.6). THERE IS NO PERIODIC HIRA RE-ASSESSMENT INTERVAL: the only cycle stated anywhere in B170 001M is the three-year review of the procedure itself.
acsaEvidence: Hazard Identification and Safety Risk Management Log - the eight-column ICAO SMM log with initial (column 6) and residual (column 8) Safety Risk Index
Documented formal HIRAs evidencing each of the five B170 cl. 4.1 triggers
HIRA reports submitted to the SACAA Director of Civil Aviation in the prescribed matrix format
Non-conformance registrations raised under Z001 001M for any deviation from B170 001M
Internal Review (Level 1) and Internal Audit (Level 3) records
acsaConflict: THE CHECK CANNOT BE EVIDENCED AS WRITTEN. B170 001M sets NO annual or periodic HIRA review interval - only the five formal-HIRA triggers and 'continuous' workplace HIRA - so a checklist row asserting that the site HIRA is 'reviewed annually' has no basis in ACSA's own procedure and must be reworded to test the five triggers instead. Two further defects to raise: the bands are NOT numbered Priority I/II/III anywhere in B170 001M (they are named and colour-coded Red/Amber/Green only), so any KSIA register using I/II/III is not on ACSA's approved format; and the worked example at cl. 4.4.1 contradicts itself - the narrative states a residual index of '2D ... Acceptable ... Green' while Figure 8 of the same example shows '2A', which falls in the Amber band. The log also has no control-owner column, so 'controls and owners' must be evidenced from J060 002M's Compliance Risk Management Plan instead.

acsaRequirement: B170 001M cl. 4.4.1 requires existing defences - policies, procedures, training, legislation and regulatory requirements - to be listed in column 5 of the log and the initial Safety Risk Index to be scored despite those defences, with further actions entered in column 7 and the residual index re-scored in column 8. Cl. 4.5 ties the residual band to a mandatory strategy: Unacceptable (Red) requires AVOIDANCE, Amber requires REDUCTION, and Acceptable (Green) requires SEGREGATION OF EXPOSURE. J060 002M cl. 4.2.3 fixes the mandatory content of the Compliance Risk Management Plan GOV 006, which is where control owners and dates live. J010 001P cl. 4.3.1.2 places SAFETY risks inside Operational Risks under Executive Committee accountability, so KSIA safety and asset risks must appear in the enterprise risk registers at Divisional and Airport level.
acsaThreshold: Mandatory CRMP content (J060 002M cl. 4.2.3): '(a) Regulations, sections and subsections; (b) Provisions; (c) Risk description; (d) Controls (People, Process or Systems and the nature of controls, i.e. Directive, Preventative, Detective, Contingent and Automated/Manual, Frequency); (e) Control environment assessment (Design effectiveness assessment and Operating effectiveness testing); (f) Residual risk rating; (g) Required additional controls; (h) Responsibility; and (i) Target date'. Risk-reduction strategies (B170 001M cl. 4.5): 'Avoidance: The operation or activity is cancelled because the risks exceed the benefits'; 'Reduction: The frequency of the operation is reduced, or action is taken to reduce the magnitude of the consequences'; 'Segregation of Exposure: Action is taken to isolate the effects of risks or build in redundancy'. Corporate matrix threshold: 'Risks rated as I and II as a minimum shall be included in the Integrated Assurance Coverage Plan' (J060 002M cl. 4.2.4).
acsaEvidence: Compliance Risk Management Plan - GOV 006 with all nine mandatory fields including residual risk rating, Responsibility and Target date
Hazard Identification and Safety Risk Management Log columns 5, 6, 7 and 8
Evidence that the residual band was matched to the mandated strategy (Avoidance / Reduction / Segregation of Exposure)
Regulatory Compliance Universe - GOV 005
Action-tracking record for compliance audit findings, management initiated actions and non-compliances
Enterprise and Airport-level risk registers under J010 001P
acsaConflict: Two scale conflicts must be resolved before scoring: B170 001M uses Severity A-E x Likelihood 1-5 with three named bands, while the CORPORATE matrix reproduced identically in J060 002M cl. 4.2.4 and the Combined Assurance Framework uses Consequences 1-5 (Minor to Catastrophic) x Likelihood 1-5 (Not Likely to Expected) producing Priority I/II/III - structurally identical but with a numeric severity axis, and neither corporate document uses the words Unacceptable/Tolerable/Acceptable. J010 001P itself contains NO rating scale, matrix, consequence criteria or quantified appetite at all, delegating them to J010 001FW, J010 003FW, RM 002 and RM 003, none of which are in the document set. J060 002M cl. 4.5 assigns action-tracking responsibility but states no tracking frequency, escalation rule for overdue actions, or evidence standard for closure.

Emergency plan submitted to DOE (NERSA) annually (cl. 4.11 c)). HYDRANT LINE STATUTORY PRESSURE TEST: 'At FACT, FABL and FALE (King Shaka) the hydrant line pressure test is YEARLY; at FAOR, FAPE, FAUP and FAEL it is THREE-YEARLY' (cl. 4.17.5). 'Bunding shall allow for at least 110% of the total volume of the biggest container within the bunded area' (T050 003M cl. 4.3.1). 'The oil store bunding shall be built to accommodate at least 110% of the total volumes... and shall comply with National Building Regulations SANS 10400 specifications' (T050 004M cl. 4.4).

acsaConflict: Three gaps in ACSA's own MHI coverage. First, D060 021M requires an MHI risk assessment but nowhere requires MHI NOTIFICATION to the Department of Employment and Labour or the local authority under the MHI Regulations, nor an MHI classification/quantification record - so the notification limb of this check has no ACSA basis. Second, no ACSA document mentions hydrant pit lids, pit drainage or water ingress into hydrant pits - the only related requirement is the FALE-specific weekly task at cl. 4.17.1/4.17.5 to 'test for existence of fuel on top of water table', which is groundwater monitoring, not pit integrity. Third, the Tightness Control System requires the leak rate to be noted (cl. 4.17.11) but NO numeric leak-rate limit is stated, so a recorded leak rate cannot be scored pass or fail.

acsaRequirement: T050 004M requires that in the event of a spill necessary measures be taken to ensure fuel does not enter stormwater drains or contact unlined or open surface, that fuel be contained using an appropriate absorbent (peat-based products, spill sorbs), that remaining hydrocarbons in the lined surface be cleaned using scrubbers or environmentally friendly methods immediately after the initial clean-up, that all spillages be reported to the Helpdesk/Information Centre/IMCC and any aerodrome spillage recorded per D070 003M, and that an oil separator be used and regularly inspected and maintained. T050 003M cl. 4.6 requires appropriate clean-up materials to be available on site and stored within a reasonable distance of the HCS in use. D060 012M cl. 4.5 supplies the only numeric separator and spill criteria in the whole set, and D060 021M cl. 4.17.10 sets the FALE separator pit regime.
acsaThreshold: 'OIL SEPARATORS SHALL BE TESTED ANNUALLY FOR EFFICIENCY'; 'SLUDGE DEPTH SHALL NOT EXCEED 25% OF CHAMBER DEPTH'; 'DISPOSAL RECORDS SHALL BE RETAINED FOR 5 YEARS'; 'SPILL RESPONSE TIME SHALL NOT EXCEED 2 HOURS FOR CONTAINMENT' (D060 012M cl. 4.5 (a)-(d)). Separator Pit (STR) at FALE: weekly clean out of liquids and sludge, plus maintenance Monthly, Tri-Monthly and Six-Monthly (D060 021M cl. 4.17.10). Spill severity boundary: 'a Minor Spill is any hydrocarbon or sewerage spill that can be contained on the apron; an Emergency/major environmental spill is any spillage that is reportable to the DEA and DWS' (T050 004M cl. 3.1). Clean-up materials 'within a reasonable distance of the HCS in use' - no numeric distance (T050 003M cl. 4.6).
acsaEvidence: Weekly separator pit clean-out records for FALE
Annual oil separator efficiency test results
Sludge depth measurements tested against the 25% of chamber depth limit
Certificates of safe disposal for all hydrocarbon waste, oils and greases
Spillage reports logged with the Helpdesk / Information Centre / IMCC and aerodrome occurrence records per D070 003M
Spill kit and absorbent inventories at fuelling positions and the fuel farm
Hazardous waste manifests for separator sludge (retained 5 years)
acsaConflict: ACSA requires NO spill drill or spill exercise anywhere - the only tested emergency provision in the set is the 12-monthly Fuel Depot emergency plan test in D060 021M cl. 4.11 b), which is not a spill drill. Spill kit placement is governed only by 'a reasonable distance' (T050 003M cl. 4.6) and 'in or near areas where hydrocarbons are handled' (T050 006M cl. 4.2), with no numeric distance or minimum contents list, and T050 004M sets no numeric response time ('as soon as practical'). The 2-hour containment limit must therefore be imported from D060 012M, a stormwater procedure. T050 004M and T050 006M also omit NEMA and the National Water Act from their legislation lists despite governing water pollution.

acsaRequirement: S010 013M fixes the notification and investigation clocks for every incident category and requires a preliminary investigation within a stated period and a full investigation within a stated period, with lessons learned shared through the ACSA Incident/Accident Recall Form and incident statistics and trends presented to the SHE Committee. B170 001M cl. 4.2 requires hazards to be identified through both proactive and reactive means expressly including 'incident and accident investigations' and 'analysis of operational data and trends', so investigation outputs must feed the HIRA. D060 016M cl. 4.3 requires Root Cause Analysis by the Supervisory and Quality Management function and requires work order comments to be reviewed for maintenance task list upgrades or changes using the ME 038-041 asset strategy forms via engineering change management - the formal route by which a failure mode changes a maintenance regime. D060 012M cl. 5 requires an annual trend analysis that identifies repeat blockage zones and sediment sources and adjusts maintenance frequency accordingly.
acsaThreshold: Notification: work and non-work-related fatality 'IMMEDIATELY OR WITHIN 12 HOURS OF OCCURRENCE'; Section 24 injury and Lost Time Injury within 24 hours; Section 24(c) equipment failure within 36 HOURS with the Annexure 1 form to the Department of Employment and Labour WITHIN 7 DAYS; medical treatment, first aid and property damage within 24 hours; near misses within 72 hours (S010 013M cl. 4 (iv), 4.1 Table 1.1). Preliminary investigation 'WITHIN SEVEN DAYS after the incident happened' (cl. 4.2 (iii)); 'A FULL INVESTIGATION MUST BE COMPLETED WITHIN ONE (1) MONTH of the incident occurrence' (cl. 4.3.1). Investigation team 'THREE (3) OR MORE people' with 'at least one (1) member... competent to lead' (cl. 4.5.2). Section 24 injury threshold: booked off work 14 days and above; LTI: less than 14 days (cl. 3.1). Trend analysis Annually (D060 012M cl. 5).
acsaEvidence: OHS Incident Report and Investigation Form / OHS Incidents Smartsheet
Annexure 1 forms submitted to the Department of Employment and Labour within 7 days
Preliminary investigation reports (within 7 days) and full investigation reports (within one month)
ACSA Incident/Accident Recall Form and Incident Recall Template - OHS 000
SHE Committee minutes recording incident statistics and trends

acsaConflict: No ACSA document requires investigation findings to be formally fed back INTO the HIRA log - B170 001M cl. 4.2 names incident investigation as a hazard identification method but sets no obligation, form or timescale for updating the log after an incident, so the feedback loop asserted in this check is a practice expectation rather than an ACSA requirement. S010 013M also states LTIFR and PFR formulae ('Number of LTIs x 100 / 200 000') that are arithmetically inconsistent with their own per-200 000-hours and per-million-passengers definitions, and still cites the withdrawn OHSAS 18001:2007 in its legislation list.

acsaRequirement: ACSA operates three interlocking permit systems. S010 002WI restricts hot work permit issue to designated Maintenance & Engineering and ARFFS persons, requires the Permit Issuer and Permit Receiver to inspect the work site together before issue, requires a signed and dated task risk assessment verified before issue, requires gas testing results to be recorded on the permit form, requires the permit to be displayed at the work site and cancelled with both parties signing, and prohibits any change to an issued permit. D060 011M requires a Permit to Work M&E 070 for all work on electrical apparatus or in live chambers, made out in duplicate, issued only by an authorised person to a competent responsible person, with the isolation and earthing status physically shown and proved dead, and a Risk Assessment ME 069 and Workers Register ME 068 used before any work. S010 011M sets the ACSA Permit to Work validity and the high-risk activity definitions that drive audit frequency.
acsaThreshold: Fire watch: 'REMAIN IN PLACE AT LEAST THIRTY (30) MINUTES AFTER COMPLETION OF HOT WORK OPERATIONS'; work area inspected ONE HOUR AFTER COMPLETION with the site 'PERIODICALLY MONITORED FOR AN ADDITIONAL THREE HOURS'; fire watch remains in effect for SIXTY (60) MINUTES after any work stoppage (S010 002WI cl. 4.3.3, 6.2.7). Combustible clearance: 'THIRTY-FIVE (35) FEET' (cl. 4.2, 4.5) versus 'at least 10m' (cl. 4.3.3). 'NO WORKER MAY WORK UNDER MORE THAN ONE WORK PERMIT AT A TIME' (D060 011M cl. 4.7). MV defined as 1 kV < Un <= 44 kV (D060 011M cl. 3.1). ACSA Permit to Work 'valid for ONE (1) YEAR from the date of issue' for fixed term contractors (S010 011M cl. 4.8). High-risk activities include 'work at heights above two (2) meters' and 'ELECTRICAL WORK GREATER THAN 50 VOLTS' (S010 011M cl. 4.11(c)). SHE File Review Form OHS 037 'MINIMUM SCORE OF 90%' or 'THE WORK PERMIT SHALL BE REVOKED', with monthly SHE File review audits for high-risk contractors (cl. 4.11). SHE file at least fourteen (14) days before commencement, reviewed within seven (7) working days (cl. 4.5.1, 4.5.2). Construction work permit applied for at least thirty (30) days before commencement (cl. 4.9). Compliance audits: high-risk bi-annually, low-risk annually (cl. 4.10).
acsaEvidence: Hot Work Permit Form - SAF 019, signed by both parties at issue and at cancellation, with gas testing results recorded on the permit face (retained 5 years)
Permit to Work - M&E 070 / OHS 043, original with the responsible person and copy in the work permit book
Risk Assessment - ME 069 and Workers Register - ME 068 for every electrical job
Workers Declaration Form - M&E 081
SHE File Review Form - OHS 037 with score, tested against the 90% minimum
Construction Work Permit from the Department of Employment and Labour, displayed at the main site entrance
Contractor compliance audit reports (7 days notice, report within 14 days, contractor action plan within 7 days)
Documented Lock Out SOP and Approved Contractor Safety Plan
acsaConflict: Four unresolved contradictions to raise. (1) S010 002WI uses thirty-five (35) feet at cl. 4.2 and 4.5 but 10 m at cl. 4.3.3 for the same combustible clearance controls, so KSIA teams could be applying two different separation distances; S010 003M cl. 4.3.4.7 compounds this with 'five (10) meters'. (2) D060 011M cl. 4.6 requires all original work permit forms and completed work permit books to be retained TWELVE (12) MONTHS before being destroyed, directly contradicting its own section 11 records table which sets FIVE (5) YEARS for Permit to Work ME 070 and the work permit books. (3) D060 011M cl. 4.25 sets the contractor audit at 'prescribed or contracted frequency' while its own section 6.2 says monthly. (4) CONFINED SPACE is not covered: S010 007M Confined Spaces Entry is cross-referenced by S010 002WI cl. 4.6, D060 021M cl. 4.6.2 and D060 012M but is NOT in the 99-document set and must be requested. S010 011M also claims alignment to the Construction Regulations 2024 while citing the 2014 Regulations and 'CR 2015 Annexure 3', lists 'Construction Regulation, 2044', and refers to a non-existent 'Section (32) agreement' where OHS Act s37(2) is the correct provision for a mandatary.

All flammable substances must be stored in a flammable store designed per SANS 10400 when not in use. A valid Department of Health licence is required for keeping Group III (electronic) and Group IV (radioactive) substances, with radiation exposure testing conducted and results kept on file. All asbestos on site and its condition must be identified and recorded in the Asbestos Register EMS 103, and transformer condition in the Transformers and Substations Register EMS 104 with only PCB-free oil used and tested or certified. S010 003WI requires written Safe Work Procedures for hazardous chemical substances, transportation and storage of flammable liquids, work with cleaning solvents, compressed gas cylinders and management of work in a confined space, each approved by BOTH the GMR 2(1) and GMR 2(7) appointees.
acsaThreshold: 'a comprehensive SDS... kept accessible and within close proximity to all HCS' - no distance figure given (T050 003M cl. 4.1). 'at least 110% of the total volume of the biggest container within the bunded area' (cl. 4.3.1). 'Only PCB-free oil shall be used; all oil shall be tested and/or certified to be PCB-free' - no ppm limit here; the only numeric PCB limit in the set is D060 023M cl. 4.7.7: reclaimed mineral insulating oils 'not more than 20 mg/kg' per SANS 555 / IEC 61619, tested Yearly. Safe Work Procedures reviewed 'TWO YEARLY, or as and when changes are introduced' and retained forty (40) years (S010 003WI cl. 4, 12).

There is NO LPG installation certification requirement anywhere in the set (no SANS 10087 reference, no gas installation certificate, no LPG installer registration). requirement: People Movers
basis: • LEPC Regulations - Appointment of responsible contractor and maintenance schedules/annexes
evidenceExpected:
1. Written appointment/contract with the lift service provider covering the specific units; monthly maintenance visit records; the 6-monthly rope-examination and 12-monthly safety-gear/governor/buffer test records.

2. The accredited inspection authority's comprehensive report/certificate, valid within the last 24 months (or re-issued after modification, failure, or change of service provider), and confirmation the authority is accredited/registered.
target:
1. OHS Act — Lift, Escalator and Passenger Conveyor Regulations, 2015 (GNR 763), Regulation 7 (maintenance); travelators/"people movers" fall within the definition of "passenger conveyor". Owner/user must appoint, in writing, a competent registered lift service provider to maintain the equipment at minimum monthly (Reg 7(1)) — or shorter per the manufacturer's risk assessment. Suspension ropes must be examined at least six-monthly, and safety gear, overspeed governors and buffers tested at intervals not exceeding 12 months (Reg 7(2)). Maintenance/inspection records must be kept on site.

2. Same Regulations, Regulation 6 (inspection and testing). A full inspection and load/function test by an accredited inspection authority is required before first use, after any modification or failure, on change of service provider, and thereafter at intervals not exceeding 24 months.
walkabout:
1. Locate the unit's on-site maintenance register and confirm monthly visit entries are unbroken and dated, and that 6-monthly rope and 12-monthly safety-gear/governor/buffer entries exist and are current. Visually check the unit runs and doors/gates interlock correctly. Pass: unbroken, dated log matching required frequencies. Fail: gaps, or generic servicing tickets in place of the prescribed checks.

2. Check the current inspection certificate's issue date is within 24 months and confirm the issuing body's accreditation, not just the maintenance contractor's own paperwork. Pass: valid, dated certificate from a confirmed accredited authority. Fail: expired, or not re-issued after a change of provider or a modification/failure event.

requirement: Certificate of Compliance issuance
basis: •D060 004M Maintenance of Certificate of Compliance Issuance
evidenceExpected: Current Certificate of Compliance and its test report for each electrical installation/plant room, confirming date and the issuer's registration status.
target: OHS Act — Electrical Installation Regulations 2009, Regulation 7 (Certificate of Compliance) and Regulation 9 (registration of persons), read with SANS 10142-1. Only a registered person (Electrical Tester for Single Phase / Installation Electrician / Master Installation Electrician) may issue a valid COC. A COC with an accompanying test report is required for every new installation before energising, on any change of ownership (existing COC not older than 2 years, otherwise a new one is required), and after any alteration or addition (new COC covering at least the modified portion).
walkabout: Locate the installation's COC and test report. Check the date against the 2-year rule where issued for a change of ownership, and confirm it covers any visible subsequent additions (e.g. a newer sub-board not matching the original COC scope). Pass: current COC/test report matching the installation as it stands. Fail: COC older than 2 years post-ownership-change, missing test report, or an uncovered addition.

requirement: Trade tested and “wiremans license”
basis: •SAQA and SANS regulations
evidenceExpected:
1. The individual's original National Artisan Certificate / trade test certificate (electrical trade / "red seal") — not a training attendance or learnership-completion letter.

2. The individual's registration certificate/number (Electrical Tester for Single Phase / Installation Electrician / Master Installation Electrician) with the Department of Employment and Labour.
target:
1. National Artisan Trade Test framework (QCTO/merSETA), electrical trade. The individual must hold a genuine National Artisan Certificate / trade test certificate ("red seal") for the electrical trade, issued via a QCTO-accredited trade test centre — not a training or learnership-attendance certificate.

2. OHS Act — Electrical Installation Regulations 2009, Regulation 9 (registration of persons) and Regulation 11. The individual must separately hold registration as a "registered person" with the Department of Employment and Labour — Electrical Tester for Single Phase, Installation Electrician, or Master Installation Electrician — in a category matching the scope of work performed. Registration (not the trade test alone) is what legally entitles the holder to inspect, test, certify and issue Certificates of Compliance (see KSIA-MEM-008).
walkabout:
1. Match the certificate on file to the person actually carrying out electrical work on site. Confirm it is the actual trade test certificate for the electrical trade specifically. Pass: genuine certificate matching the person on site. Fail: only an attendance/learnership letter, or a certificate for a different trade.

2. requirement: Aerodrome lighting and power back up systems maintenance - ICAO
basis: •D060 001M Maintenance of Aerodrome Lighting and AGL Systems Procedure
evidenceExpected:
1. AGL system's unserviceable-light log/register showing repair turnaround times; any NOTAM history triggered by AGL unserviceability.

2. Standby generator/UPS changeover-time test records for lighting circuits, benchmarked against the requirement for the runway's approach category.
target:
1. ICAO Annex 14 Vol I, Chapter 5 (aeronautical ground lighting) and ICAO Doc 9157; implemented via Civil Aviation Regulations Part 139/SA-CATS 139; ACSA's internal procedure D060 001M. A minimum percentage of lights in each AGL system must remain serviceable at all times, with a rule against two adjacent unserviceable lights; photometric standards also apply. The specific numeric percentage-unserviceable threshold was not confirmed against the primary ICAO/SA-CATS text in this research — treat D060 001M as the authoritative local reference and confirm the exact figure with ACSA.

2. Same ICAO Annex 14 Chapter 5 framework — standby/backup power changeover-time requirements, stricter for higher precision-approach categories (Cat I/II/III); ACSA's internal procedure D060 001M. Standby generators/UPS serving critical AGL circuits must switch over within the changeover time required for the runway's approach category, periodically re-tested. Specific numeric changeover-time figures were not confirmed against the primary ICAO/SA-CATS text — confirm the exact figure via D060 001M.
question: 1. What is the target repair turnaround time for an unserviceable AGL light, and is a NOTAM issued when repair exceeds it?
walkabout:
1. Walk (or drive) the runway/taxiway edge and approach lighting, ideally at night, or review the current unserviceable-light log; scan for dark or damaged fixtures, specifically checking whether any two adjacent lights are both unserviceable. Pass: log actively maintained, no two adjacent lights out. Fail: no log kept, or adjacent lights unserviceable.

2. Where feasible, request a live changeover demonstration; check the test date isn't stale — batteries and generators can drift out of spec with age. Pass: recent test on file, measured time within the required limit. Fail: no re-test since installation, or a measured time exceeding the requirement.

requirement: Water usage and storm water drainage
basis: •National Environmental Management Act (NEMA)
evidenceExpected:
1. The Water Use Licence, or a documented basis for a General Authorisation exemption, for stormwater discharge points.

2. The airport's stormwater management plan; maintenance/inspection records for oil-water separators and fuel/de-icing area containment; any discharge quality monitoring results.
target:
1. National Water Act 36 of 1998, Section 21 (water use, incl. 21(c) impeding/diverting flow and 21(i) disposing of waste/water containing waste), read with Section 39 (General Authorisations). Stormwater run-off at an airport (which can carry de-icing fluid, fuel and oil) constitutes a "water use" requiring either an individual Water Use Licence or documented qualification for a lower-risk General Authorisation exemption. Note: "NEMA" alone (as cited in the checklist) is imprecise — the NWA is the primary licensing driver.

2. NEMA 107 of 1998, Section 28 (general duty of care to prevent, minimise and remediate pollution). Requires reasonable measures to prevent stormwater pollution — in practice a stormwater management plan with pollution-prevention controls (oil/water separators, fuel/de-icing containment) and discharge quality monitoring.
walkabout:
1. Physically identify the site's stormwater discharge points and confirm they match what's described/authorised in the licence or exemption assessment. Pass: current WUL, or a documented, reasoned GA exemption assessment matching the actual discharge points. Fail: no licence and no documented exemption assessment — status simply assumed.

2. Inspect oil-water separators and containment bunding at fuel and de-icing areas for visible condition, overflow/leakage signs, and evidence of scheduled desludging; check the plan reflects the current site layout. Pass: separators/containment visibly maintained on a documented schedule, plan matches site reality. Fail: separators shown on drawings only with no inspection schedule, or an outdated plan.

requirement: RWY friction testing and rubber removal
basis: •D060 010 Friction Testing Procedure
evidenceExpected:
1. ACSA's D060 010 Friction Testing Procedure; continuous friction-measuring device test reports/logs per runway, dated and compared against the applicable minimum; the device's own calibration certificate.

2. Rubber-removal work records (method and date), tied to the friction test results that triggered them.
target:
1. ICAO Annex 14 Vol I, Attachment A (runway surface friction) and ICAO Doc 9137 Part 2, Chapter 7; ACSA's internal procedure D060 010 "Friction Testing Procedure". Friction must be measured periodically with a continuous friction-measuring device and compared against ICAO-defined minimum friction levels; below minimum, corrective action must be taken. Commonly cited ICAO-guidance testing-frequency bands by daily jet movements: <15 = annual; 16-30 = six-monthly; 31-90 = quarterly; 91-150 = monthly — these figures come from regional guidance material rather than SA-CATS 139 itself, so cross-check against D060 010 for any airport-specific or SACAA-mandated frequency.

2. ICAO Doc 9137 Part 2, Chapter 8 (rubber deposit removal); ACSA's internal procedure D060 010. Rubber removal should be triggered by degraded friction test results (not run on an unrelated fixed calendar alone), using a method appropriate to the runway surface type, without damaging surface macro-texture.
walkabout:
1. Check test dates against the expected frequency band for that runway's traffic volume, confirm the device's calibration certificate is on file, and check whether any below-minimum results are documented together with corrective action. Pass: testing at the correct frequency, calibrated device, results above minimum or with documented corrective action. Fail: frequency mismatch, missing calibration certificate, or below-minimum results with no follow-up.

2. Visually inspect runway touchdown zones for visible rubber build-up. Compare the most recent removal record's date/location against the friction results that should have triggered it. Pass: removal tied to friction-test triggers, touchdown zones free of excessive build-up. Fail: removal on a fixed calendar with no link to friction results, or degraded friction with no removal scheduled.

acsaRequirement: D060 010 fixes the friction survey frequency for King Shaka expressly: RWY 06/24 is surveyed once every three months, escalated from six-monthly on traffic grounds under the ICAO Table A traffic-band ladder. Testing is self-wetting to at least 1 mm water depth with a smooth tread tyre, with a minimum of six tests at 65 km/h and 95 km/h, scored against the Table B matrix of design objective / maintenance planning level / minimum friction level for six device types. A result at or below the maintenance planning level triggers corrective maintenance and rubber removal; at or below the minimum friction level triggers immediate action plus a NOTAM. The operator of the friction testing device shall be fully trained to operate the device, and friction testing shall be conducted under the supervision of Maintenance Engineering personnel. Signed friction test results must be assessed and signed off by the Manager: Civil Maintenance and/or Senior Manager: Site Maintenance Engineering within two weeks of the test, and rubber removal records - date of removal, method used, treated runway sections and post-treatment friction test results - submitted within two weeks of completion.

Records retained five (5) years.

requirement: Asbestos register
basis: •OHS Act - Manage asbestos and prevent its spread
evidenceExpected: Current asbestos register/inventory (last review date, must be within 24 months); floor plans marking ACM locations; risk categorisation and management strategy per item; evidence of distribution to employees/contractors (and a new owner, on sale).
target: OHS Act — Asbestos Abatement Regulations 2020 (GG 43893), Regulation 4 (inventory), read with Regulation 3 (identification). All asbestos/ACM must be identified and recorded in a written register: date of identification, quantity/area and condition, floor-plan location, warning-label confirmation, risk categorisation, and management strategy (manage-in-place or remove, with timeframe and responsible person). A competent person must review/update the register at least every 24 months, and more often when ACM is newly identified, removed or encapsulated.

Pass: register current (reviewed within 24 months), signage matches register. Fail: overdue review, missing signage, or ACM altered since the last review without an update.

requirement: Sustainability
basis: 1. Companies Act 71 of 2008 s.72(4) read with Companies Regulations 2011 reg 43(1) and reg 43(5)(a)(iii) — every state-owned company must appoint a social and ethics committee, which must monitor the company's activities with regard to "the environment, health and public safety, including the impact of the company's activities and of its products or services"; this is the one hard statutory sustainability duty on ACSA 2. National Environmental Management Act 107 of 1998 s.28(1) — the duty of care: every person who causes, has caused or may cause significant pollution or degradation of the environment must take reasonable measures to prevent, minimise and rectify it 3. ISO 14001:2015 cl. 9.1.2 (evaluation of compliance) and cl. 9.2 (internal audit) — the EMS clauses that T010 001P and T030 002M implement, including the periodic legal compliance audit; binding on ACSA only through its own certification commitment 4. King IV Report on Corporate Governance for South Africa 2016, Principle 3 (responsible corporate citizenship) and Principle 4 (sustainable development as an inseparable element of value creation) — recommended practice applied on an "apply and explain" basis, not statutory
target: No single South African statute mandates a discrete "Sustainability" compliance item in this engineering/maintenance context. Most plausible governing frameworks: ACSA's own corporate Sustainability/ESG policy and reporting, King IV Principle 2 (responsible corporate citizenship), and/or ISO 14001 (Environmental Management Systems) where ACSA holds site certification. No specific numeric threshold was identified — this line most likely reflects internal ESG governance rather than a hard legal requirement. Do not assign it a fabricated legal citation; scope it with ACSA's audit sponsor first.
question: What specifically is this line meant to test — an ISO 14001-certified environmental management system, a specific internal sustainability policy/target, or reporting against ACSA's ESG/Integrated Annual Report framework — and can you produce the relevant certificate, policy, or report extract?
walkabout: If ISO 14001 alignment is claimed, look for a certification plaque/certificate or visible EMS documentation/signage on site.

acsaRequirement: ACSA's sustainability requirements are set in engineering standards, not in an appointment or competency procedure. D100MAN requires the design basis and selection criteria for energy efficiency systems to target Green Building Council South Africa certification of 4 Star Rating as a minimum, with 99.5% energy system availability, a 20-year design life, power factor maintained at 0.95, a 1MVA trigger for 40% renewable integration, greater than 40% energy saving required on retrofits, and business case viability tested on IRR exceeding WACC, positive NPV, Profitability Index exceeding 1 and payback less than a set fraction of the estimated useful life. Handover must include a 36-month proposed maintenance schedule, one electronic and three hard copies of as-built drawings, FMEA and RAM studies, and the competency and skill sets of operations and maintenance personnel including certification. requirement: Risk management
basis: 1. Public Finance Management Act 1 of 1999 s.51(1)(a)(i) — the accounting authority must ensure the public entity "has and maintains ... effective, efficient and transparent systems of financial and risk management and internal control"; this section applies to every public entity, Schedule 2 included, and is the binding enterprise-risk duty on ACSA 2. Treasury Regulation 29.1.1 — the corporate plan of a Schedule 2 public entity must include a risk management plan and a fraud prevention plan 3. Civil Aviation Regulations 2011 Part 140, regs 140.01.1, 140.01.2 and 140.01.3 — the holder of a Category 4 or higher aerodrome licence issued under Part 139 where commercial activities take place must establish a safety management system containing safety risk management, hazard identification and safety risk assessment and mitigation; read with ICAO Annex 19 and Doc 9859 (Safety Management Manual), the source of the B170 001M matrix format the SACAA will accept 4. Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 s.8(2)(d) — the employer must establish, as far as reasonably practicable, what hazards attach to any work, article, substance, plant or machinery used in the business and what precautionary measures are required; this is the plant and engineering level risk assessment the checklist does not distinguish from enterprise risk governance
evidenceExpected: Board-approved risk management policy/strategy and current risk register; Risk Committee or Audit & Risk Committee minutes evidencing regular review.
target: No single confirmed statute governs "risk management" as a discrete maintenance-engineering audit item for ACSA. Most plausibly grounded in the PFMA and its Treasury Regulations (a specific regulation number, e.g. 3.2.1, was checked and found to apply only to Schedule 3A/3C entities, not Schedule 2 entities like ACSA, so no clause number should be cited), King IV Principle 4 (risk governance), and operationally ISO 31000. This is a governance-framework item, not a hard legal pass/fail test — the checklist does not distinguish between enterprise-level risk governance and engineering/plant-specific risk assessment (e.g. OHS Act risk assessments).
question: Is this line testing the Board-approved enterprise risk management policy/register, or plant/engineering-specific (e.g. OHS Act) risk assessments? The checklist doesn't distinguish these — clarify scope with ACSA before rating this item.

acsaConflict: J010 001P, the Enterprise Risk Management Policy itself, contains NO risk rating scale, NO risk matrix, NO consequence or likelihood criteria, NO quantified risk appetite or tolerance thresholds and NO Unacceptable/Tolerable/Acceptable bands - it defines appetite and tolerance in words only and delegates the scale entirely to J010 001FW, J010 003FW, RM 003 and RM 002, none of which is in the ACSA set. The corporate matrix in J050 001FW/J060 002M labels severity numerically 1-5 while B170 001M labels it alphabetically A-E, and neither uses the terms Unacceptable/Tolerable/Acceptable, so that third-tier mapping is unverified against enterprise documentation. B170 001M's own worked example is internally contradictory (narrative says residual '2D ... Acceptable ... Green' while Figure 8 shows '2A', which falls in the Amber band). Per project direction, prefer J050 001FW and B170 001M over CCPS or ISO 45001 as the South African basis. No ACSA document creates a risk management appointment or competency standard.
basisNote: The target is right that Treasury Regulation 3.2.1 is departmental and cannot be cited against ACSA, but it misattributes risk governance to King IV Principle 4 — risk and opportunity governance is Principle 11, Principle 4 being value creation and sustainable development.

requirement: Asset operation and reliability
basis: 1. ICAO Annex 14 Volume I, Chapter 8, Table 8-1 — maximum switch-over times for aerodrome secondary power supply; this, and not an internal availability target, is the source of D118MAN's one-second and fifteen-second limits, applied in South Africa through the Civil Aviation Regulations Part 139 aerodrome licensing and aerodrome manual regime 2. ISO 14224:2016 (3rd ed.) — collection and exchange of reliability and maintenance data for equipment: the recognised taxonomy for failure description, failure cause and failure resolution that D118MAN cl. 9.5 and D119MAN cl. 8.5 require to be captured per maintainable item; recommended practice, not statutory 3. ISO 55001:2024 (2nd ed.) — asset management system requirements: performance evaluation of assets and of the asset management system, including availability and reliability measures (cited at document level, since the 2024 second edition renumbered the clauses of ISO 55001:2014) 4. IEC 60300-3-11:2009 (Ed. 2.0) — Dependability management, Application guide, Reliability centred maintenance — and SAE JA1011 (November 2024 revision), Evaluation Criteria for RCM Processes; professional and industry practice, not statutory
evidenceExpected: If ISO 55001 alignment is claimed: Asset Management Policy, Strategic Asset Management Plan (SAMP), asset register, management review records. If not: planned preventive-maintenance completion-rate reports, breakdown/downtime logs, and reliability KPIs (availability, MTBF) actually tracked for the audited asset.
target: No South African statute specific to "asset operation and reliability" was identified. Most plausible governing framework: ISO 55000/55001 (Asset Management), which requires a documented Asset Management Policy and Strategic Asset Management Plan (SAMP), an asset register, risk-based maintenance/lifecycle planning, and reliability KPIs (availability, MTBF, condition scores) under management review. No legal citation should be asserted — confirm with ACSA whether this line tests formal ISO 55001 alignment/certification or general reliability-centred maintenance practice.
question: Is ACSA claiming formal ISO 55001 alignment/certification for this asset function, or does this line test general reliability-centred maintenance practice? Clarify scope with ACSA before rating this item.
walkabout: Where ISO 55001 alignment is claimed, look for asset tagging/identification on the physical asset consistent with a formal asset register. Otherwise check the asset's physical condition against any available condition score or inspection record, and note visible breakdown/repair history (maintenance stickers, logbooks) as a cross-check against reported KPIs.

basisNote: SAE JA1011 was revised in November 2024 and the commonly quoted 2009 revision is superseded, and ISO 55001:2014 is superseded by ISO 55001:2024, so any ACSA reference to the earlier editions is out of date; the Annex 14 table number is cited from the current edition and should be checked against the edition SACAA has adopted.

requirement: Asset renewal programme
basis: 1. Public Finance Management Act 1 of 1999 s.51(1)(a)(iv) — the accounting authority must ensure the entity has "a system for properly evaluating all major capital projects prior to a final decision on the project"; this is the binding authority for a costed, evaluated renewal programme and for D060 026M's evaluation and approval steps 2. PFMA s.52(b) read with Treasury Regulation 29.1 — the renewal programme and its funding must appear in the Schedule 2 corporate plan covering the following three financial years, submitted at least one month before the start of the financial year 3. IAS 16 paras 51 and 61 — residual value, useful life and depreciation method must be reviewed at least at each financial year-end, which is the accounting counterpart of D060 026M cl. 4.2.5's nine steps ending in Finance updating Fixed Asset Register FIN 007 4. ISO 55001:2024 (2nd ed.) and the International Infrastructure Management Manual (IIMM) — documented renewal and replacement planning derived from condition assessment and criticality; recommended practice, not statutory
evidenceExpected: Current asset renewal/replacement programme or plan, showing which assets/asset classes are due for renewal and over what timeframe, and its linkage to the approved capital budget.
target: No specific statute or numeric threshold was identified for an "asset renewal programme" as a discrete audit item — like the neighbouring sustainability/risk-management/reliability rows, this is a general asset-management governance expectation rather than a hard legal requirement. Most relevant framework: ISO 55001, which expects a documented, costed renewal/replacement programme derived from condition assessments and useful-life reviews, prioritised by risk/criticality (Core/Key/Supporting) and linked to the approved capital budget. Do not assign a fabricated legal citation — clarify with ACSA's audit sponsor exactly what evidence satisfies this line.
walkabout: Where an asset observed on site appears visibly aged, worn or near end-of-life, check whether it appears on the renewal programme with a planned renewal date — a visibly deteriorated asset with no renewal plan on file is a red flag.

acsaRequirement: D060 026M is ACSA's asset renewal programme document. It fixes a seven-step methodology in sequence (identification of end-of-life assets; assessment of asset physical condition; evaluation criteria; decision-making process; approval and implementation; documentation; monitoring and review); requires every asset to carry one of eight strategies (efficiency/reliability, lifecycle replacement, modernisation, new capacity/development, refurbishment, regulation and risk, technology obsolescence, de-bottlenecking); requires condition assessment against six hazards, with safety and regulatory/compliance hazards leading to automatic consideration of replacement or at minimum a risk assessment and mitigation strategy; requires eleven evaluation dimensions to be considered; requires nine mandatory steps before any useful-life adjustment, ending in Finance updating the Fixed Asset Register FIN 007; and requires findings and recommendations to be presented to the relevant MANCO/MANCOs annually. Renewal implementation runs through D060 020M's five sequential asset modification stages with committee approval by class.

acsaRequirement: S010 013M requires non-work and work-related fatalities, lost time injuries, Section 24 injuries and Section 24(c) equipment failures to be reported to ACSA as they occur or within 24 hours of occurrence, with fatality notification immediately or within 12 hours, Section 24 injury and LTI immediately or within 24 hours, Section 24(c) equipment failure within 36 hours, near misses within 72 hours, and the Annexure 1 form to the Department of Employment and Labour within 7 days for work-related fatalities and Section 24(c) equipment failures. A preliminary investigation must be completed and submitted within seven days and a full investigation completed within one (1) month of the incident, on the OHS Incident Report and Investigation form/Smartsheet, by a team of three (3) or more people with at least one competent to lead. Section 24 injury is defined as absence of 14 days and above; LTI as less than 14 days. Machinery failures are routed through the GMR 2(1) appointee, who must report to the inspector 'forthwith' under section 7 of the General Machinery Regulations. Corrective-action closure is governed by Z001 001M: log within a day to five (5) days, verify within 48 hours, and resolve Catastrophic with immediate attention and thereafter within seven (7) days, Critical within fourteen (14) days, Serious within fourteen (14) days, Significant within thirty (30) days, Minor/Observation discretionary; a returned non-conformance is addressed within two (2) days; overdue means the due date is exceeded by seven (7) days or more with no completion date, reported on the System Variance Report; and a monthly Non-Conformance/Compliance report is tabled at Management Committees. B180 001M requires a management review at least once a year across each site taking incident statistics, non-conformance reports and the status of corrective and preventive actions as mandatory inputs.
acsaThreshold: S010 013M cl. 4(iv) and Table 1.1: 12 hours (fatality notification); 24 hours (Section 24 injury, LTI, medical treatment, first aid, property damage); 36 hours (Section 24(c) equipment failure); 72 hours (near misses); Annexure 1 to the DEL within 7 days; preliminary investigation within seven days; full investigation within one (1) month; investigation team of three (3) or more with at least one competent to lead; Section 24 injury = booked off 14 days and above; LTI = less than 14 days; frequency rate factor per 200 000 hours worked. Z001 001M cl. 4.7.1-4.7.3 and 4.11: log within a day to five (5) days; verify within forty-eight (48) hours; Catastrophic immediate attention and thereafter resolve within seven (7) days; Critical fourteen (14) days; Serious fourteen (14) days; Significant thirty (30) days; Minor/Observation discretionary; returned NC within two (2) days; overdue = 'due date is more than seven (7) days or more and the action has no completion date'. B180 001M cl. 4.2: management review 'at least once a year across each site'. Retention: incident records five (5) years; Non-Conformance Register PMD 031, Non-Conformance Manual Report Form PMD 005 and Logging of Non-Conformance Process PMD 036 five (5) years each.

acsaConflict: Two defects to raise. First, S010 013M's stated LTIFR and PFR formulae are arithmetically inconsistent with their own definitions - the document gives 'LTIFR = Number of LTIs x 100 / 200 000' and 'PFR = Number of Non work Fatalities x 100 / 100 0000' where the definitions require multiplication by 200 000 and 1 000 000 respectively - so any KSIA trend figures computed from the procedure as written are wrong. Second, its Related Legislation list still cites OHSAS 18001:2007 clause 4.5.2, a standard withdrawn and superseded by ISO 45001:2018, which every other ACSA OHS procedure cites. Note also that Z001 001M cl. 1.1 expressly excludes corrective maintenance defects and operational incidents/occurrences from its scope, so an OHS incident and its resulting non-conformance run on two separate registers with different clocks.
